summary: Read-only research: Strudel embedding + headless grading + sounds, theory/ear-training pedagogy, and supporting browser tech for the Oak course app

reports.summary:
Build Oak on the granular npm packages, not the convenience bundles. The core is `@strudel/codemirror@1.3.0` (the `StrudelMirror` class) with `@strudel/core@1.2.6`, `@strudel/transpiler@1.2.6`, `@strudel/webaudio@1.3.0` (which pulls in `superdough@1.3.0` and `supradough@1.2.4`), `@strudel/draw@1.2.6`, `@strudel/mini`/`@strudel/tonal@1.2.6` and `@strudel/soundfonts@1.3.0`. All are AGPL-3.0-or-later. The source now lives at codeberg.org/uzu/strudel; the GitHub repo is archived and labelled "MOVED TO CODEBERG". There has been no npm release since 2026-01-18. The `main` branch has moved on with unreleased breaking changes: `repl({defaultOutput})` becomes `onSchedule(hap,time,cps)` and throws if `defaultOutput` is passed (PR #2138), kabelsalat is removed from core, several reverts landed, and `replaceCode`/`insertCode` were added. Code written against the published 1.2.6/1.3.0 API must use `defaultOutput: webaudioOutput`, and Strudel should sit behind our own adapter. `@strudel/repl` (the `<strudel-editor>` element) and `@strudel/web` are self-contained bundles (2.4 MB and 409 KB) that each carry their own copy of core and CodeMirror. You can't share `@codemirror/state` or `Pattern` with them, add CM6 extensions, or mix them with granular imports without loading core twice. `<strudel-editor>` also has an open bug (#2128, fix PR #2178 still open) where several instances on one page freeze the browser.

`StrudelMirror` gives the most control. It wraps `repl()` from core, a `Drawer` (requestAnimationFrame synced to `scheduler.now()`) and a CM6 `EditorView` exposed as `.editor`. Its constructor options are `root`, `id`, `initialCode`, `onDraw`, `drawContext`, `drawTime`, `autodraw`, `prebake` (required), `bgFill` and `solo`, and everything else is passed through to `repl()`: `defaultOutput`, `getTime`, `transpiler`, `onToggle`, `onUpdateState`, `beforeEval`, `afterEval`, `onEvalError`, `beforeStart`, `editPattern`, `sync`, `setInterval`, `clearInterval`, `mondo`. "Solo" (one editor playing at a time) is built in: starting an editor dispatches a document `start-repl` CustomEvent, and every other mirror stops. There is no option for extra CM6 extensions. Use `view.dispatch({effects: StateEffect.appendConfig.of(ext)})`, or build our own `EditorView` from the exported pieces (`highlightExtension`, `updateMiniLocations`, `highlightMiniLocations`, `flashField`, `widgetPlugin`, `sliderPlugin`, `updateWidgets`, `updateSliderWidgets`) driving a core `repl()` and `Drawer`. The official strudel.cc docs component `website/src/docs/MiniRepl.jsx` is the reference for many small editors on one page. It runs `prebake()`, `loadModules()` and `initAudioOnFirstClick()` once at module level and gives each mirror a unique `id`. It drives custom visuals (a keyboard display) through `editPattern: pat => pat.onPaint((ctx,time,haps,drawTime)=>...)`. That pattern also stops `StrudelMirror` from resetting `drawTime` to `[0,0]`, which it does after every eval when no painters are registered. For our own piano roll and staff renderers, use the `onPaint` hook or our own requestAnimationFrame loop that reads `mirror.repl.scheduler.now()` (cycles) and calls `mirror.repl.state.pattern.queryArc(a,b)`. Haps expose `whole.begin`/`whole.end` (Fractions), `value.note`/`n`/`freq`/`s` and `context.locations`.

Bundler compatibility looks good with one gap. Every AudioWorklet (superdough, supradough, kabelsalat) is inlined as a `data:text/javascript` URL. There is no wasm and no `?url` import in the published dists. The only `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` is the NeoCyclist SharedWorker, used only when `sync: true`, so Vite (the stack Strudel itself uses) and Bun.build should both work. The gap: `process.env.NODE_ENV` is left in the core, superdough and webaudio dists (inside `errorLogger`). Bun's docs don't promise to define it for browser builds, so add an explicit define or a `globalThis.process` shim. Otherwise every runtime pattern error becomes "process is not defined". `@kabelsalat/web@0.4.1` (imported by core 1.2.6) has an IIFE `main` and an ESM `module` with no `exports` map. Browser bundlers resolve it fine, but the Node and Bun runtimes (e.g. `bun test`, server-side checking of exercises) will probably fail on `import {SalatRepl}` unless it is aliased to `dist/index.mjs`. There are no TypeScript types and no destroy/dispose method. The global state (scheduler time and cps functions, `evalScope` globals, `Pattern.prototype.p` injection, the superdough AudioContext singleton, localStorage `codemirror-settings`, `:root` theme variables plus the `dark` class on `<html>`, a fullscreen `#test-canvas`) means our wrapper must serialize evaluations and clean up by hand. No React StrictMode issues have been reported upstream; the double-mount hazards described here are inferred from the source.

findings.topic: Release cadence and main-branch divergence (breaking changes are coming)
findings.detail: core release times: 1.0.0 2024-01-22, 1.1.0 2024-05-31, 1.2.0 2025-05-01, 1.2.1/1.2.2 May 2025, 1.2.3 2025-08-18, 1.2.4 2025-09-10, 1.2.5 2025-10-27, 1.2.6 2026-01-17. codemirror/repl/web/webaudio 1.3.0 were published 2026-01-18. Nothing has been released in the roughly 10 months since, while main stays active. main already differs from npm. (1) packages/core/repl.mjs now takes `onSchedule` and throws 'defaultOutput has been removed. use onSchedule(hap, time, cps) instead' (PR #2138, closed 2026-10-12, which also renames doughTrigger to doughOutput and oscTrigger to oscOutput, and adds Pattern.onSchedule). (2) kabelsalat is removed from core (issue #1930). (3) October 2026 reverts: block-based eval #1714, vim shortcuts #1624, autocomplete sound names #1564. As a result, main's codemirror.mjs lacks the 'repl-evaluate'/'repl-stop'/'repl-toggle-comment' document listeners and the rich autocomplete that ARE in the published 1.3.0. (4) main adds StrudelMirror.replaceCode/insertCode. Open PRs: #2178 (fixes the multi-editor widget bug #2128), #2171 (make cpm a global control handled in cyclist). The official examples/codemirror-repl/main.js on main already uses `onSchedule`; copying it against npm 1.2.6 gives silent no-sound, because core 1.2.6 ignores onSchedule and calls an undefined defaultOutput inside a try/catch. strudel.cc is described as stable and warm.strudel.cc tracks main.

findings.detail: `new StrudelMirror({ root, id, initialCode='', onDraw, drawContext, drawTime=[0,0], autodraw, prebake, bgFill=true, solo=true, ...replOptions })`. `prebake` is REQUIRED: the constructor runs `this.prebaked = prebake()` unconditionally and awaits it in beforeEval. replOptions go straight to core `repl()`: defaultOutput (1.2.6 name), getTime, transpiler, onToggle, onUpdateState, beforeEval, afterEval, onEvalError, beforeStart, editPattern, sync, setInterval, clearInterval, mondo. `pattern: silence` is passed by the official code but ignored. StrudelMirror wraps onToggle: on start it calls drawer.start(scheduler) and, if solo, dispatches a document CustomEvent('start-repl',{detail:this.id}); on stop it calls drawer.stop(), updateMiniLocations(editor,[]) and cleanupDraw(true,id). It wraps beforeEval (cleanupDraw, await prebaked, then the user's beforeEval) and afterEval (stores meta.miniLocations and widgets, updates slider/block widgets and highlights, calls the user's afterEval({code,pattern,meta}), then sets drawTime to `pattern.getPainters().length ? this.drawTime : [0,0]` and calls drawer.invalidate). BUG: it computes `this.id = id || s4()` but passes the RAW `id` to repl(), and therefore to the transpiler for widget IDs. Always pass an explicit unique `id`. Minimal working config for 1.2.6/1.3.0: `{ root, id, defaultOutput: webaudioOutput, getTime: () => getAudioContext().currentTime, transpiler, prebake, drawTime, onDraw }`.

Properties: `.editor` (the CM6 EditorView), `.repl` (the core repl object), `.drawer` (a @strudel/draw Drawer), `.code` (current text, updated on every docChanged), `.id`, `.miniLocations`, `.widgets`, `.drawTime`, `.solo`. Methods in published 1.3.0: `evaluate(autostart=true)` (flash, then repl.evaluate(code,autostart); returns nothing), `stop()` (calls repl.scheduler.stop()), `toggle()`, `flash(ms)`, `highlight(haps,time)`, `setCode(code)` (replaces the whole doc through dispatch), `appendCode`, `getCursorLocation()`/`setCursorLocation(n)`, `setFontSize`/`setFontFamily`, `setTheme(name)`, `setLineWrappingEnabled`, `setBracketMatchingEnabled`, `setLineNumbersDisplayed`, `setBracketClosingEnabled`, `setAutocompletionEnabled`, `reconfigureExtension(key,value)`, `updateSettings(settings)` (also persists them to localStorage), `changeSetting(key,value)`, `drawFirstFrame()` (used when autodraw is set: evaluates without starting and paints one frame), and `clear()`. `clear()` ONLY removes the document listeners ('start-repl' plus, in 1.3.0, 'repl-evaluate'/'repl-stop'/'repl-toggle-comment'). There is NO destroy(): it does not destroy the EditorView, stop the Drawer, or stop the scheduler. replaceCode/insertCode exist only on main. Reading code: `mirror.code` or `mirror.editor.state.doc.toString()`. Built-in keymap (Prec.highest): Ctrl-Enter and Alt-Enter evaluate, Ctrl-. and Alt-. stop, Alt-w/Alt-q jump between '$' labels.

findings.topic: StrudelMirror global side effects that conflict with a host app
findings.detail: (1) `codemirrorSettings = persistentAtom('codemirror-settings', defaultSettings)` is stored in localStorage and shared by every mirror (and by strudel.cc if served from the same origin). Defaults: keybindings 'codemirror', isAutoCompletionEnabled false, isPatternHighlightingEnabled true, isFlashEnabled true, isLineNumbersDisplayed true, theme 'strudelTheme', fontSize 18, fontFamily 'monospace'. initEditor reads it at construction. (2) `initTheme()`/`activateTheme(name)` add <style id='strudel-theme-vars'> setting `:root { --background, --foreground, --caret, ... !important }`, call draw's setTheme, and ADD or REMOVE the `dark` class on document.documentElement (this fights Tailwind dark mode). Some themes also inject a customStyle rule. (3) `cleanupDraw()` calls `getDrawContext()`, which creates and prepends a `<canvas id='test-canvas'>` to <body> with style 'pointer-events:none;width:100%;height:100%;position:fixed;top:0;left:0' plus a window resize listener. Non-inline `.pianoroll()`, `.scope()`, `.spiral()` etc. in learner code draw over the whole page. (4) document-level 'start-repl' CustomEvent is used for solo. (5) The root element gets style.display='block' and, when bgFill, background-color var(--background).

findings.topic: Adding our own CM6 extensions (gated autocomplete, lint, read-only regions)
findings.detail: Neither `initEditor({initialCode,onChange,onEvaluate,onStop,root,mondo})` nor StrudelMirror accepts extra extensions. Option A: after construction, `mirror.editor.dispatch({ effects: StateEffect.appendConfig.of([autocompletion({override:[oakSource]}), linter(oakLint), readOnlyRangesFilter, EditorView.updateListener.of(...)]) })`. This is standard CM6 API and works because @codemirror/* are externals in the codemirror dist, so our app and Strudel share one @codemirror/state, provided it is deduped. Option B (most control): build our own EditorView using exports from @strudel/codemirror@1.3.0. dist exports: BlockWidget, SliderWidget, StrudelMirror, Vim, activateTheme, addWidget, codemirrorSettings, compartments, defaultSettings, extensions, flash, flashField, highlightExtension, highlightMiniLocations, initEditor, initTheme, injectStyle, isFlashEnabled, isPatternHighlightingEnabled, markcss, parseBooleans, registerWidget, setFlash, setMiniLocations, setSliderWidgets, setWidget, settings, showMiniLocations, slider, sliderPlugin, sliderValues, sliderWithID, theme, themeColors, themes, toggle*Comment, updateMiniLocations, updateSliderWidgets, updateWidgets, widgetPlugin. NOT exported from 1.3.0 dist: basicSetup (exported only on main), autocomplete.mjs (strudelAutocomplete) and tooltip.mjs. Strudel's own autocomplete is reachable only via `extensions.isAutoCompletionEnabled(true)`. It is built from a jsdoc `doc.json` that is inlined (as JSON.parse of a string) into the 641 KB dist. doc.json is generated at build time (`jsdoc packages/ --template jsdoc-json`), gitignored, and not shipped as a file. Read-only regions: a CM6 `EditorState.changeFilter`/`transactionFilter` over a RangeSet StateField, or `EditorState.readOnly.of(true)` plus `EditorView.editable.of(false)` for fully read-only examples.

The transpiler (acorn, `locations:true`) emits `miniLocations` ([from,to] pairs for each mini-notation leaf in double-quoted or backtick strings; single quotes are plain strings) plus `widgets`. After eval, StrudelMirror calls `updateMiniLocations(view, locs)`, which dispatches the `setMiniLocations` effect and creates Decoration.mark ids 'from:to'. Every animation frame, the Drawer callback filters haps with `hap.isActive(time)` and calls `highlightMiniLocations(view, time, haps)` (the `showMiniLocations` effect). For each hap, `hap.context.locations` ({start,end}) are matched to the marks and styled with `hap.value.markcss` or `outline: solid 2px ${hap.value.color ?? 'var(--foreground)'}`. These StateEffects are exported, so our own editor can reuse the highlighting by adding `highlightExtension` and calling the two functions. The `markcss` control lets lesson code restyle highlights.

`repl({ defaultOutput, onEvalError, beforeEval, beforeStart, afterEval, getTime, transpiler, onToggle, editPattern, onUpdateState, sync=false, setInterval, clearInterval, id, mondo=false })` returns `{ scheduler, evaluate, start, stop, pause, setCps, setPattern, setCode, toggle, state }`. `state` has schedulerError, evalError, error (=evalError||schedulerError), code, activeCode, isDirty (code!==activeCode), pattern, miniLocations, widgets, pending and started; onUpdateState(state) fires on every change, including every keystroke via setCode. `evaluate(code, autostart=true, shouldHush=true)` does: updateState pending, `injectPatternMethods()` (redefines GLOBAL Pattern.prototype.p/q/d1-9/p1-9 and calls evalScope({all, each, hush, cpm, setCps, setcps, setCpm, setcpm, compileKabel})), setTime(()=>scheduler.now()), await beforeEval({code}), hush, transpile+eval via `Function()`, collect `$:` patterns (supports `S$:` solo and `_` mute prefixes) into stack(), apply each/all transforms, `editPattern(pattern)`, scheduler.setPattern(pattern, autostart), then afterEval({code, pattern, meta}). It returns the pattern, or undefined on error. Errors are CAUGHT: it logs `[eval] error: msg` with type 'error', sets state.evalError and calls onEvalError(err). It never rethrows. With `sync:true` and SharedWorker available it uses NeoCyclist; otherwise Cyclist.

Cyclist (core 1.2.6 cyclist.mjs): `cps=0.5` default (one cycle per 2 s, i.e. 120 BPM if a cycle is a 4/4 bar), `latency=0.1` s, clock from zyklus createClock(getTime, cb, duration=0.05 s, interval=0.1 s, overlap=0.1 s, setInterval, clearInterval). Methods: `start()` (awaits beforeStart; throws if no pattern), `stop()` (resets lastEnd=0, so the next start is at cycle 0), `pause()` (keeps position), `setPattern(pat, autostart)`, `setCps(cps)`, `now()` (current cycle as a float; returns 0 when not started; computed as lastBegin + (getTime()-lastTick-duration)*cps), plus fields `.started`, `.cps`, `.pattern`. Haps are triggered as `onTrigger(hap, deadline, duration, cps, targetTime)` with targetTime = (whole.begin - cyclesAtCpsChange)/cps + secondsAtCpsChange + latency. A `hap.value.cps` control changes the tempo mid-pattern. Host tempo control: `mirror.repl.setCps(x)` or `scheduler.setCps(x)`; in code: `setcps(x)`, `setcpm(x)` (=x/60 cps), `.cpm(x)`. Tempo PERSISTS on that scheduler across evaluations (the website's resetEditor calls `repl.setCps(0.5)`). Transport events: only onToggle(started) and onUpdateState. There is no per-cycle event, so poll `scheduler.now()` in requestAnimationFrame or use per-hap `pat.onTrigger((hap, currentTime, cps, targetTime)=>..., false)` (dominant=false keeps the sound). The official REPL passes `setInterval`/`clearInterval` from the `worker-timers` package to avoid background-tab throttling. Visual time from now() runs about 0.05 s ahead of scheduled audio (latency 0.1 vs tick duration 0.05), plus AudioContext output latency.

findings.topic: Error surfaces: evaluation vs runtime vs mini-notation
findings.detail: Eval-time: acorn SyntaxError (has .pos, .loc{line,column}, .raisedAt) or a runtime exception during pattern construction. Mini-notation errors are thrown as `new Error('[mini] parse error at line N: ...')`; the computed char region is NOT attached to the error, only the line number in the message (packages/mini/mini.mjs mini2ast). All of these reach onEvalError/state.evalError. Query and scheduler errors: Pattern.queryArc catches and calls `errorLogger(err,'query')` and returns []; Cyclist's tick catch calls errorLogger(e) and onError, but repl() in 1.2.6 does NOT pass onError, so state.schedulerError is never set. getTrigger catches output errors (e.g. superdough's `sound X not found! Is it loaded?`) as `[getTrigger] error:`. errorLogger calls `logger(msg)`, which dispatches `document` CustomEvent `'strudel.log'` with detail {message, type, data}. errorLogger messages have type undefined; eval errors have type 'error'. Identical messages within 1000 ms are debounced. Listen with `document.addEventListener('strudel.log', e => ...)` and parse prefixes like '[query] error:' and '[getTrigger] error:'. superdough has its own logger, routed into core's logger by webaudio's setLogger(logger). `[webaudio] skip hap: still loading` is logged when a sample buffer is not yet fetched.

findings.topic: Global/shared state across several repl instances
findings.detail: Several StrudelMirror/repl instances can coexist, but they share: schedulerState (setTime/getTime, setCpsFunc/getCps, setTriggerFunc, setPattern, setIsStarted: last writer wins; evaluate() calls setTime for its own scheduler), evalScope globals (every export is assigned to globalThis and strudelScope; core alone exports 883 names, including `focus` and `frames`, which overwrite window.focus and window.frames), Pattern.prototype.p/q/dN injected on each evaluate and closing over THAT repl's pattern registry, `reset_state()` on stop, superdough soundMap, the sample buffer cache, analysers, and one SuperdoughAudioController (orbits and global FX). @strudel/draw `Pattern.prototype.draw` uses the global getTime() and a global animationFrames map keyed by id. `cleanupDraw(clear, replID)` stops every animation whose key `startsWith(replID)`, and every animation when replID is undefined (bug #2128: 'repl1' also kills 'repl12_*'). Slider ids are `slider_${charPos}` in a global `sliderValues` map, not namespaced per editor. Because evaluate() is async (await injectPatternMethods/beforeEval), two concurrent evaluations can interleave and register `$:` patterns into the wrong repl.

superdough audioContext.mjs keeps a module singleton: `getAudioContext()` (lazily `new AudioContext()`), `setAudioContext(ctx)`, `setDefaultAudioContext()`, `getAudioContextCurrentTime()`, all re-exported by @strudel/webaudio. Every repl using `getTime: () => getAudioContext().currentTime` and `defaultOutput: webaudioOutput` shares one context and one output graph, so yes, multiple repls share one AudioContext. `webaudioRepl({audioContext?, ...})` (PR #1833 'External AudioContext Injection', in 1.3.0) calls setAudioContext. `initAudio({ disableWorklets=false, maxPolyphony, audioDeviceName, multiChannelOrbits=false })` loads the worklets (registerWorklet URLs plus the built-in workletsUrl) via `audioWorklet.addModule`. BUG in 1.3.0 and main: `if ((!audioCtx) instanceof OfflineAudioContext) await audioCtx.resume()` is always false, so initAudio never resumes a suspended context. `initAudioOnFirstClick(options)` only listens for `mousedown`, so keyboard-first users never resolve it. Other exports: `renderPatternAudio(pattern,cps,begin,end,sampleRate,maxPolyphony,multiChannelOrbits,downloadName)` for offline WAV export (it closes the live context and swaps in an OfflineAudioContext); `getAnalyserById`; `getAnalyzerData('time'|'frequency', id)`; `resetGlobalEffects`; `resetLoadedSounds`; `setDefaultValue(s)`; `aliasBank`; `soundAlias`; `registerSound(key, onTrigger, data)`; `soundMap` (nanostores map).

repl-component.mjs: calls initAudioOnFirstClick() at import. customElements.define('strudel-editor'), observedAttributes ['code'], with the code taken from an inner HTML comment. connectedCallback inserts a NEW div as a SIBLING after the element (no shadow DOM) and creates a StrudelMirror with defaultOutput webaudioOutput, getAudioContext time, transpiler, drawTime [-2,2], drawContext=getDrawContext() (the fullscreen canvas), prebake, solo, and sync — but NO id. It dispatches an 'update' CustomEvent with repl state, and `.editor` exposes the StrudelMirror. Its published prebake.mjs evalScopes core, draw, mini, tonal, webaudio, codemirror, hydra, soundfonts and midi, then registerSynthSounds, registerZZFXSounds, registerSoundfonts and samples from raw.githubusercontent.com/felixroos/dough-samples (tidal-drum-machines, piano, Dirt-Samples, vcsl, mridangam) plus tidalcycles/uzu-drumkit, and aliasBank from todepond/samples. It also defines Pattern.prototype.piano. The package's dist is a self-contained Vite lib build (rollup externals commented out, process.env.NODE_ENV replaced): dist/index.js IIFE about 2.2 MB, ESM chunks about 2.4 MB, and the ESM entry exports ONLY `prebake`. Bug #2128 (open; fix PR #2178 open 2026-11-09): two editors with inline widgets (._pianoroll) on one page share widget DOM id '_widget__pianoroll_0', and CodeMirror MutationObservers ping-pong the canvas until the script times out. The first play may show no pianoroll because of cleanupDraw prefix matching.

web.mjs re-exports core, webaudio, transpiler, mini and tonal. `initStrudel(options)` calls initAudioOnFirstClick() and miniAllStrings() (unless options.miniAllStrings===false), creates ONE `webaudioRepl({...replOptions, transpiler})`, runs defaultPrebake (evalScope core/mini/tonal/webaudio plus {hush, evaluate}, registerSynthSounds; soundfonts commented out) and then options.prebake, and returns a promise of the repl. `evaluate(code, autoplay=true)` and `hush()` (repl.stop()) are module-level; `Pattern.prototype.play()` is available. It sets `window.initStrudel = initStrudel` at import, which breaks SSR. The dist is self-contained (409 KB, all deps bundled), so mixing it with @strudel/codemirror loads core twice (core warns '@strudel/core was loaded more than once'). There is only one repl, no editor and no highlighting. Useful only for a headless player.

findings.topic: @strudel/draw: Drawer, onDraw/painters, pianoroll, punchcard, inline widgets
findings.detail: `new Drawer(onDraw, drawTime)` has start(scheduler), stop(), invalidate(scheduler, t?), setDrawTime([lookbehind, lookahead]) in cycles, and `.visibleHaps` and `.painters`. Each requestAnimationFrame it queries `scheduler.pattern.queryArc(max(lastFrame, phase-0.1), phase)` with phase = now()+lookahead, keeps haps with endClipped >= phase-lookbehind-lookahead, and calls onDraw(visibleHaps, time=now(), drawer, painters). StrudelMirror's user-facing signature is `onDraw(haps, time, painters)`; the default draws each painter as `painter(drawContext, time, haps, drawTime)`. `Pattern.prototype.onPaint(painter)` stores painters in state.controls.painters, and `pat.getPainters()` collects them. `.punchcard(opts)` = onPaint(getPunchcardPainter(opts)), synced to the Drawer. `.wordfall()` is a vertical labelled punchcard. `.pianoroll(opts)` instead uses `Pattern.prototype.draw` (its own requestAnimationFrame keyed by id, default ctx getDrawContext()). Pianoroll options: cycles=4, playhead=0.5, vertical, labels, flipTime, flipValues, overscan, hideNegative, smear, fold, active, inactive, background, playheadColor, fill, fillActive, stroke, strokeActive, hideInactive, colorizeInactive, fontFamily, minMidi=10, maxMidi=90, autorange, ctx, id. Low-level renderers: `__pianoroll({time,haps,ctx,...})` and `drawPianoroll({haps,time,ctx,drawTime,...})`. Inline widgets are registered in codemirror widget.mjs via `registerWidget(type, fn)`: `_pianoroll`, `_punchcard`, `_spiral`, `_scope`, `_pitchwheel`, `_spectrum`. They are canvas block widgets (default 500x60) with DOM id `${replId}_widget_${type}_${index}` from transpiler getWidgetID. Also exports spiral, pitchwheel, animate and color helpers, plus getTheme/setTheme.

findings.topic: Driving OUR piano-roll and staff renderers from live haps
findings.detail: Three verified hooks. (a) `onDraw(haps, time, painters)` on StrudelMirror: time is the current cycle (float). Caveat: after each eval StrudelMirror sets drawTime to [0,0] unless the pattern has painters, so without a painter you only get currently active haps. (b) The official pattern (website/src/docs/MiniRepl.jsx 'claviature') is `editPattern: pat => pat.onPaint((ctx, time, haps, drawTime) => render(haps, time))`. This keeps the configured drawTime (e.g. [-2,2] or [0,4]) and gives a lookbehind/lookahead window every frame. (c) Our own requestAnimationFrame loop: `t = mirror.repl.scheduler.now(); haps = mirror.repl.state.pattern.queryArc(Math.floor(t), Math.floor(t)+N)` gives whole-bar windows, which suit staff notation, and also works for static (non-playing) rendering after `await mirror.repl.evaluate(code, false)`. Hap API (core hap.mjs): `whole`/`part` TimeSpans with Fraction `.begin`/`.end` (use .valueOf()), `value` (object with note, n, freq, s, gain, velocity, color, etc.), `context.locations` [{start,end}] for linking notation back to code, `hasOnset()`, `isActive(t)`, `isInPast`/`isInFuture`, `duration`, `endClipped`, `hasTag(id)`. Pitch helpers from @strudel/core: noteToMidi, valueToMidi, midiToFreq, freqToMidi, getFreq, tokenizeNote, isNote, isNoteWithOctave, getAccidentalsOffset, cycleToSeconds.

@strudel/webaudio scope.mjs: `Pattern.prototype.tscope(config)` (alias `.scope`) and `.fscope(config)` call `this.analyze(id).draw(...)`, drawing `drawTimeScope(analysers[id], {align=true, color, thickness=3, scale=0.25, pos=0.75, trigger=0, ctx=getDrawContext(), id=1})` or `drawFrequencyScope`. spectrum.mjs: `.spectrum({thickness, speed, min=-80, max=0, ...})`. Inline versions are `_scope` and `_spectrum`. Data access for our own visuals: the `.analyze(id)` control routes audio into `getAnalyserById(id, fftSize=1024, smoothing=0.5)`; read it with `getAnalyzerData('time'|'frequency', id)` (Float32Array) or the live-binding `analysers` map exported by superdough.

website/src/repl/useReplContext.jsx (main), at module level in the browser: `audioReady = initAudioOnFirstClick({maxPolyphony, audioDeviceName, multiChannelOrbits})`; `modulesLoading = loadModules()`; `presets = prebake()`; `drawContext = getDrawContext()`. init() then creates `new StrudelMirror({ sync: isSyncEnabled, onSchedule (main; defaultOutput in 1.3.0-era) = webaudioOutput or superdirtOutput, getTime = getAudioContextCurrentTime (or getPerformanceTimeSeconds for OSC), setInterval/clearInterval from 'worker-timers', transpiler, autodraw:false, root, initialCode:'// LOADING', pattern: silence, drawTime:[-2,2], drawContext, prebake: async()=>{await Promise.all([modulesLoading,presets]); if(prebakeScript) return evaluate(prebakeScript,{addReturn:false})}, onUpdateState, onToggle (clearHydra on stop), beforeEval: ()=>audioReady, afterEval (persist code, update URL hash), bgFill:false })`. resetEditor = resetVoicings, resetDefaults, resetGlobalEffects, clearCanvas, clearHydra, resetLoadedSounds, `repl.setCps(0.5)`, then prebake() again. Export uses `evaluate(false)`, `scheduler.stop()`, `renderPatternAudio(...)`, then initAudio again. util.mjs `loadModules()` runs evalScope(settingPatterns {theme,fontFamily,fontSize}, core, draw, edo, tonal, mini, xen, webaudio, codemirror, hydra, serial, soundfonts, csound, tidal, gamepad, motion, mqtt, mondo, dough, plus midi and osc in the browser or desktopbridge under Tauri).

website/src/repl/prebake.mjs (same at the 1.3.0 tag and on main), awaited with Promise.all. (1) `registerSynthSounds()`: waveforms 'triangle', 'square', 'sawtooth', 'sine', 'user', 'one'; plus 'sbd', 'supersaw', 'bytebeat', 'pulse', 'bus'; noises 'pink', 'white', 'brown', 'crackle'; aliases tri, sqr, saw, sin. (2) `registerZZFXSounds()`: zzfx, z_sine, z_sawtooth, z_triangle, z_square, z_tan, z_noise. (3) `registerSamplesFromDB()` (user-uploaded IndexedDB samples). (4) `import('@strudel/soundfonts').then(m=>m.registerSoundfonts())`: 125 General MIDI instruments `gm_*` (gm_piano, gm_epiano1, gm_acoustic_bass, gm_electric_guitar_jazz, gm_alto_sax, gm_string_ensemble_1, etc.), lazily fetched from https://felixroos.github.io/webaudiofontdata/sound/{name}.js and `eval`'d (setSoundfontUrl changes the base). (5) samples() from baseCDN 'https://strudel.b-cdn.net': piano.json (base /piano/; Salamander Grand, CC-BY), vcsl.json (/VCSL/, CC0), tidal-drum-machines.json (/tidal-drum-machines/machines/, tag 'drum-machines'), uzu-drumkit.json (/uzu-drumkit/, tag), uzu-wavetables.json (/uzu-wavetables/), mridangam.json (/mrid/, tag). (6) An inline Dirt-Samples subset (casio, crow, insect, wind, jazz, metal, east, space, numbers, num) under /Dirt-Samples/. All are registered with `{prebake:true}`. (7) `aliasBank(baseCDN + '/tidal-drum-machines-alias.json')`. piano.mjs defines `Pattern.prototype.piano` (clip(1), s('piano'), release(.1), pan by pitch); files.mjs registers Tauri '~/music/' prefixes. `samples(map|url, baseUrl, {prebake, tag})` only REGISTERS sounds; buffers are fetched on first trigger. Explicit baseUrl overrides the JSON's `_base`. Checked 2026-11-10: strudel.b-cdn.net JSON returns 200 with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

This is the component strudel.cc's learn pages use for MANY small editors per page. Module level runs once: `prebaked = prebake(); modulesLoading = loadModules(); audioReady = initAudioOnFirstClick()`. Per instance: `id = useMemo(s4)`; `new StrudelMirror({ id, defaultOutput|onSchedule: webaudioOutput, getTime: () => getAudioContext().currentTime, transpiler, autodraw, root, initialCode:'// LOADING', pattern: silence, drawTime: punchcard ? [0,4] : [-2,2] (or [0,0] for the keyboard display), drawContext: a per-instance context or getDrawContext(), editPattern: pat => (onSchedule? pat.onSchedule(...)) / claviature? pat.onPaint(...) / punchcard? pat.punchcard({labels}), prebake: () => Promise.all([modulesLoading, prebaked]), onUpdateState: s => setReplState({...s}), beforeStart: () => audioReady, afterEval: ({code}) => setVersionDefaultsFrom(code), mondo })`, then `editor.setCode(code)`. The UI uses `editor.toggle()`, `editor.evaluate()`, `state.started`, `state.isDirty` and `state.error.message`. It initializes from a ref callback guarded by `if (!editorRef.current)`, not useEffect, and renders `
{code}
` until client-side.

findings.topic: Bundler compatibility: what is inside the published dists
findings.detail: All @strudel/* dists are Vite library-mode ESM (`target: esnext`) with package dependencies externalized (codemirror, core, draw, webaudio, etc.), except @strudel/repl and @strudel/web, which bundle everything. AudioWorklets: superdough (vite-plugin-bundle-audioworklet), supradough (`dough-worklet.mjs?audioworklet` at build time) and @kabelsalat/web all inline worklets as `data:text/javascript,...` strings passed to `audioWorklet.addModule`, so no asset URLs survive into the dists. Scan of main entries: no `?url` imports, no wasm, no import.meta.env. `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` appears only in core dist NeoCyclist: `new SharedWorker(new URL("" + new URL("assets/clockworker-ZDiUtESR.js", import.meta.url).href, import.meta.url))` with /* @vite-ignore */, reached only when `sync:true`. `process.env.NODE_ENV` remains in core (1), webaudio (2) and superdough (2) dists inside errorLogger. `Function()` is used by core safeEval (needs CSP 'unsafe-eval'); soundfonts uses `eval` on fetched font JS. Code-split dynamic imports exist in the prebakes (`import('@strudel/soundfonts')`). @strudel/codemirror source autocomplete.mjs imports '../../doc.json', but main points to dist, where it is inlined. webaudio imports the deep path 'superdough/superdoughoutput.mjs' (bundled into its dist). No package ships .d.ts files or a `types` field.
findings.evidence: vite.config.js of each package on unpkg; grep scan of unpkg.com/<pkg>@<ver>/dist/index.mjs; https://unpkg.com/supradough@1.2.4/index.mjs

findings.detail: @strudel/core@1.2.6 dist imports `{ SalatRepl } from '@kabelsalat/web'` (range ^0.4.1; latest 0.4.1). @kabelsalat/web@0.4.1 has "type":"module", "main":"dist/index.js" (an IIFE: `var kabelsalat=function(l){...}`), "module":"dist/index.mjs" (real ESM), and NO "exports". Browser bundlers that honor `module` (Vite, esbuild-style) get ESM. Resolvers that use `main` get the IIFE and fail with 'does not provide an export named SalatRepl'; this is the exact Vite SSR failure in issue #1921. Bun docs: 'At runtime Bun prefers "main" ... and uses "module" otherwise', so importing @strudel/core under `bun test` or the Bun server will likely hit this. Issue #1930 removed kabelsalat from core on main (not yet released).

Strudel builds its own packages with vite ^6.0.11, and strudel.cc is Astro+Vite. The official examples/codemirror-repl is a plain Vite vanilla app using @strudel/codemirror, so the granular packages are known to work under Vite (current Vite is 8.3.7, Rolldown-based; not separately verified). Vite app builds define process.env.NODE_ENV automatically. Bun: the docs describe `define` (keys like 'process.env.NODE_ENV') and `env: 'inline'|'PUBLIC_*'|'disable'` for Bun.build. The fullstack/HTML-imports docs document `[serve.static]` with `plugins`, `env` (default 'disable') and `sourcemap`, warn about 'ReferenceError: process is not defined', and document NO `define` key for HTML imports. They don't mention workers, `new URL(import.meta.url)` or wasm. Bun issue #2906 (2023) suggests worker and `new URL` asset graph support is limited. Because Strudel's dists avoid all of these except the sync-mode SharedWorker, Bun.build should work if process.env.NODE_ENV is defined or shimmed and `splitting:true` is used for the dynamic imports.

No upstream issue mentions StrictMode (Codeberg search returned none); issue #1351 notes the old @strudel.cycles/react hook (0.9.0, 2023) is unmaintained, and there is no @strudel/react. From source, the StrictMode hazards are: the StrudelMirror constructor immediately creates an EditorView appended to `root`, adds document listeners, starts the prebake, and may draw. A double mount without full cleanup leaves two editors in the same root and stale 'start-repl' listeners, and a running scheduler/Drawer keeps going after unmount because there is no destroy(). The official MiniRepl dodges this with a ref-callback guard instead of useEffect. SSR-unsafe at import: @strudel/web (`window.initStrudel=`), @strudel/repl (customElements/HTMLElement guarded, but initAudioOnFirstClick touches document), @strudel/soundfonts ('window is not defined', per a comment in the official prebake), and @kabelsalat/web via core 1.2.6 (main=IIFE). @strudel/draw and codemirror themes touch window/document only when called. Treat all Strudel modules as client-only (dynamic import after mount).
findings.evidence: codeberg issue search (react, StrictMode, ssr); https://codeberg.org/uzu/strudel/raw/branch/main/website/src/repl/prebake.mjs (comment); https://unpkg.com/@strudel/web@1.3.0/web.mjs; StrudelMirror source

findings.topic: Which embedding option gives the most control (comparison)
findings.detail: For Oak's needs (MANY small editors, one playing at a time; our own CM6 extensions; reading code; catching errors; transport events): (1) @strudel/codemirror StrudelMirror plus granular packages is the best choice. It has built-in solo via 'start-repl'; `.editor` is a real CM6 EditorView we can extend with appendConfig; `.code` and `.repl.state` are readable; onEvalError/state.evalError plus the 'strudel.log' event catch errors; onToggle/onUpdateState plus polling scheduler.now() give transport; it shares @codemirror/* and @strudel/core with our app. (2) A fully custom EditorView plus core `repl()` plus `Drawer` plus the exported highlight/widget/flash extensions gives maximum control: no localStorage settings, no theme side effects, our own autocomplete/lint/read-only from the start, our own destroy(). It costs reimplementing about 150 lines of StrudelMirror glue. (3) <strudel-editor> (@strudel/repl): little control, duplicate core/CM, bug #2128 with multiple editors, sibling DOM insertion; not suitable. (4) @strudel/web: headless single repl, no editor or highlighting, duplicate core if mixed; only useful for background playback such as ear-training drills, and even that is better done with a hidden core repl().
findings.evidence: Synthesis of the verified source above

risks: The npm release is stale (last published 2026-01-18), and main has unreleased BREAKING changes: repl() throws if `defaultOutput` is passed (it must be `onSchedule(hap,time,cps)`), doughTrigger/oscTrigger are renamed, kabelsalat is removed, cpm may become a global control (PR #2171), and several features were reverted. Upgrading later will break any code that calls the 1.2.6/1.3.0 repl API directly.
Docs and examples on main or strudel.cc may describe APIs that are not in npm 1.3.0. Example: examples/codemirror-repl uses `onSchedule`, which core 1.2.6 silently ignores, so nothing plays.

`process.env.NODE_ENV` in the core, superdough and webaudio dists (errorLogger) throws 'process is not defined' in browser bundles that don't define it (Bun HTML imports document no `define`). That turns every runtime or query error into an uncaught ReferenceError inside the scheduler tick.

@kabelsalat/web@0.4.1 (pulled in by core 1.2.6) resolves to an IIFE under `main`, so the Node and Bun runtimes (bun test, server-side exercise grading) will likely fail to import @strudel/core unless it is aliased.

Multiple editors: StrudelMirror passes an undefined `id` to the transpiler, so widget ids collide (#2128: page freeze with inline ._pianoroll in two editors). cleanupDraw's prefix match (`startsWith(replID)`) cancels other editors' draw loops (e.g. 'r1' kills 'r12_*'). Slider ids are not namespaced per editor. Fix PR #2178 is unmerged.

No destroy() on StrudelMirror (clear() only removes listeners). React StrictMode or route changes can leak EditorViews, requestAnimationFrame loops, document listeners and running schedulers unless the wrapper stops the scheduler and drawer and calls editor.destroy().

Global side effects: localStorage 'codemirror-settings' is shared by all mirrors; `:root` CSS variables with !important plus toggling the `dark` class on <html> clash with Tailwind and our own theming; a fullscreen fixed '#test-canvas' is prepended to <body> on the first eval/stop; evalScope assigns about 900+ globals, including overwriting window.focus and window.frames.

Shared global scheduler state (setTime/getTime, Pattern.prototype.p injection, trigger/cps functions) plus async evaluate() means concurrent evaluations in different editors (e.g. a hidden grading repl and a visible one) can interleave and corrupt `$:` registration or draw timing.

Audio unlock: initAudioOnFirstClick only listens for `mousedown`, and initAudio never calls resume() (operator-precedence bug), so a context created before a gesture (e.g. by our mic or tuner code) can stay suspended, and keyboard-only first plays can hang on `beforeStart: () => audioReady`.

Samples and soundfonts are fetched lazily from third-party hosts (strudel.b-cdn.net, felixroos.github.io, raw.githubusercontent.com); the first trigger may be skipped ('skip hap: still loading'). That hurts ear-training precision and local-first/offline use.
No TypeScript types ship with any @strudel package; the project needs hand-written .d.ts files for the surface we use, and they will drift as the API changes.
AGPL-3.0-or-later: fine for personal local use, but distributing or hosting Oak for others requires releasing the whole app under an AGPL-compatible license (official docs: 'Respect the license').
CSP: Strudel evaluates user code with Function(), and soundfonts eval() fetched JS; any strict CSP must allow 'unsafe-eval' and data: worklet modules.
recommendations: Pin exactly: @strudel/core@1.2.6, @strudel/mini@1.2.6, @strudel/transpiler@1.2.6, @strudel/tonal@1.2.6, @strudel/draw@1.2.6, @strudel/codemirror@1.3.0, @strudel/webaudio@1.3.0, @strudel/soundfonts@1.3.0 (plus transitive superdough@1.3.0 and supradough@1.2.4). Do NOT add @strudel/repl or @strudel/web. Dedupe @codemirror/state, @codemirror/view and @strudel/core (check for a single copy after bun install).

Wrap Strudel behind an `OakStrudel` adapter module (TypeScript, with our own .d.ts for the used surface). It is the only place that knows `defaultOutput` vs `onSchedule`, so the future upgrade becomes a one-file change.

Use StrudelMirror per lesson editor with an explicit unique `id` (e.g. `oak_${lessonId}_${n}_`, ending in a separator so the cleanupDraw prefix bug can't match siblings), `solo: true`, `defaultOutput: webaudioOutput`, `getTime: () => getAudioContext().currentTime`, `transpiler`, `setInterval`/`clearInterval` from worker-timers, `bgFill:false`, and a `prebake` that returns one SHARED module-level promise (follow website/src/docs/MiniRepl.jsx). If the side effects become painful, move to our own EditorView plus core repl() plus Drawer, reusing the exported highlightExtension, updateMiniLocations, highlightMiniLocations, flashField, widgetPlugin and sliderPlugin.

Add Oak's CM6 features with `mirror.editor.dispatch({effects: StateEffect.appendConfig.of([...])})`: `autocompletion({override:[unlockedFunctionsSource]})` (keep Strudel's isAutoCompletionEnabled false to avoid an 'override' config-merge conflict), `linter()` using acorn parse errors (.pos/.loc) plus our own 'function not unlocked yet' rule, and a transactionFilter for read-only regions. Author our own function catalog (name, signature, explanation, unlock level) rather than relying on the unexported doc.json.

Before constructing any mirror, call `codemirrorSettings.set({...defaultSettings, theme:'<ours>', isAutoCompletionEnabled:false, fontSize:..., keybindings:'codemirror'})`. After `initTheme`/`activateTheme`, re-assert our own `dark`/light class on <html>, or scope Tailwind dark mode to a different selector.

Pre-create `<canvas id='test-canvas'>` inside a controlled, hidden or visual-panel container (getDrawContext finds it by id) so non-inline `.pianoroll()`/`.scope()` in learner code renders into our panel instead of a fullscreen overlay.

Drive Oak's own piano roll and staff renderers with `editPattern: pat => pat.onPaint((ctx,time,haps,drawTime) => oakVisuals.update(haps,time))` (this keeps drawTime, e.g. [-2,2]). For static notation and exercise checking, evaluate without starting (`repl.evaluate(code,false)`) and use `state.pattern.queryArc(c, c+n)`, converting pitches with noteToMidi/valueToMidi and linking back to code via hap.context.locations.
Serialize ALL evaluations (visible editors plus any hidden grading or target repl) through a single async mutex, since repl.evaluate mutates global prototypes, scheduler time and globals.

Write a `dispose()` for each editor: `mirror.repl.scheduler.stop(); mirror.drawer.stop(); mirror.clear(); mirror.editor.destroy(); root.replaceChildren()`. In React (or any framework), create mirrors client-only after mount, guard against double init, and call dispose on cleanup.

Unlock audio explicitly: in our own Play button or first key handler, call `await getAudioContext().resume(); await initAudio({maxPolyphony:128})` and use that promise as `beforeStart`. Don't rely on initAudioOnFirstClick. Create or set the AudioContext (setAudioContext) once and reuse it for the mic pitch detector.

Bundler: in Bun.build set `define: {'process.env.NODE_ENV': JSON.stringify(mode)}` and `splitting: true`. For Bun HTML imports, where no define is documented, import a tiny first module that does `globalThis.process ??= { env: { NODE_ENV: 'production' } }` before any Strudel import. Alias `@kabelsalat/web` to `@kabelsalat/web/dist/index.mjs` (tsconfig paths or a bundler alias) for bun test and server-side use. Never set `sync:true` (SharedWorker asset URL).

Mirror the needed sample maps and audio locally (strudel.b-cdn.net JSONs plus files; VCSL CC0, Salamander piano CC-BY) through the Bun server, pass explicit baseUrl to `samples()`, and use `setSoundfontUrl()` for a local copy of the gm_* fonts. Preload buffers used in ear-training drills, because samples() only registers them.

Catch runtime errors by listening to `document.addEventListener('strudel.log', ...)` and parsing '[query] error:', '[getTrigger] error:' and '[cyclist] error:'. Use `onEvalError` for eval errors and parse '[mini] parse error at line N' to place lint markers.

Expose transport to the UI via onToggle plus a single requestAnimationFrame loop reading the active mirror's `repl.scheduler.now()` and `.cps`. Reset tempo deterministically per lesson (`repl.setCps(0.5)` in beforeEval) unless the lesson sets it.
Track upstream PR #2178 (multi-editor widget fix) and any 1.4/2.0 release; re-verify the onSchedule migration when it lands.
openQuestions: Does Bun 1.4's bundler (Bun.build target 'browser' and HTML imports) auto-define process.env.NODE_ENV, and does it prefer the `module` field over `main` for browser builds? The docs are silent; verify with a throwaway build once the project allows it.

Will the next Strudel npm release (with onSchedule, kabelsalat removed and the cpm changes) ship soon enough that Oak should target main via git dependencies instead of npm 1.3.0? That would trade stability for not having to migrate later.

Do we accept StrudelMirror's global side effects (localStorage settings, :root variables, the dark class, the test-canvas), or invest up front in a custom EditorView + repl() + Drawer wrapper for full isolation?
Licensing: is Oak strictly personal and local, or might it be published? AGPL-3.0 then applies to the whole app.

Should samples and soundfonts be vendored locally (offline-first, deterministic ear training) or loaded from strudel.b-cdn.net? Some sample sets have their own licenses (e.g. Salamander CC-BY attribution).

Exact audio-to-visual latency calibration (scheduler latency 0.1 s vs tick duration 0.05 s vs AudioContext.outputLatency) for tight rhythm and transcription feedback needs measurement in the target browser.

reports.summary:
Learner code can be graded without audio. The path is: @strudel/transpiler `transpiler()` rewrites the code, then @strudel/core `evaluate()` runs it with `Function()`. Double-quoted and untagged backtick strings become `m(str, offset)` mini calls. Labeled statements `x: expr` become `expr.p('x')`. The resulting Pattern is queried with `pattern.query(new State(new TimeSpan(Fraction(b), Fraction(e))))` or `queryArc(b, e)`. `Pattern.prototype.p` only exists when core's `repl()` injects it. Strudel's own test runtime (test/runtime.mjs) mocks `.p` as identity, so only the last labeled pattern survives there. A grader has to inject its own `.p` collector (copying repl.mjs: `$` gets an index suffix, `_x`/`x_` mutes, an `S` prefix solos) and `stack()` the collected patterns. The alternative is to instantiate core `repl()` with a no-op output and call `evaluate(code, false)`. Tempo is global scheduler state, not part of the pattern. Default cps is 0.5. `setcps`/`setcpm`/`all`/`each` exist only in repl scope, so a grader must stub them and capture the values. A per-hap `cps` control can also change tempo at playback time. Strudel has no bars: by convention setcpm(bpm/beatsPerCycle), so seconds = cycles/cps and beats = cycles*beatsPerCycle.

Environment: core, mini, tonal and transpiler do no DOM, AudioContext or navigator work at import time. speak.mjs wraps its `window` access in try/catch, and the mouse and keyboard listeners check `typeof window` first. All four can run in a module Web Worker. One blocker for Bun and Node: the latest npm release, @strudel/core@1.2.6 (2026-01-17), statically imports `{ SalatRepl }` from @kabelsalat/web@0.4.1. That package's `main` is an IIFE script (`dist/index.js`, type: module, no exports). Node, and the Bun runtime (Bun docs: 'At runtime Bun prefers "main"'), will fail to link the named import. Vite resolves the `module` field, which is why the browser and Strudel's vitest suite work. This was reported as issue #1921 and fixed on Codeberg main by removing kabelsalat from core (PR #1932, 2026-01-18), but no npm release has shipped since. Options: pin the whole family to 1.2.5, which has no kabelsalat dependency, or `bun patch @kabelsalat/web` to point main/exports at dist/index.mjs, or alias it to a stub. Main also renamed `repl({defaultOutput})` to `onSchedule` (passing defaultOutput now throws), split the transpiler into plugins, and fixed voicing `mode:'above'`/`'root'`. The grader should pin exact versions and avoid exact-octave voicing snapshots.

Pitch normalization: use core `valueToMidi(value)` (freq beats note; string note goes through noteToMidi with default octave 3, so 'c' = 48; number note passes through). Do not use `getPlayableNoteValue`, which has a bug. In superdough, `n` is a sample index and never pitch unless `.scale()` turned it into `note`. Synths default to midi 36 and s defaults to 'triangle'. `.bank(b)` makes the sample name `${b}_${s}`. tonal facts: `.scale()` turns {n} into {note:'E3'} strings and tags `context.scale`. `.voicing()` uses iReal-style symbols ('C', 'Am'/'C-', 'C^7'/'CM7', 'Cm7', 'C7', 'Co7', 'Ch7', 'Csus', 'C+'/'Caug'). 'Cmaj7', 'Cdim' and lowercase roots produce silence plus a log line, with no exception. Voicings are 4-5-note piano voicings with doubled notes, so grade on pitch-class sets.

findings.detail: npm latest: @strudel/core, mini, tonal, transpiler, draw @1.2.6 (published 2026-01-17); @strudel/webaudio, codemirror, repl, web and superdough @1.3.0 (2026-01-18). The source repo is codeberg.org/uzu/strudel, branch main, still active (last commit 2026-11-08), and package.json repository fields point there. @tonaljs/tonal 4.10.0 (scale-type 4.9.4), fraction.js 5.3.4 (core requires ^5.2.1), chord-voicings 0.0.1. The transpiler/mini/tonal peer pins are exact (e.g. transpiler@1.2.6 depends on "@strudel/core": "1.2.6"), so all versions must move together.

`export function transpiler(input, options = {})` with options `{ wrapAsync=false, addReturn=true, emitMiniLocations=true, emitWidgets=true, id }`. Returns `{ output, miniLocations, widgets }`, or `{ output }` when emitMiniLocations is false. It parses with acorn (ecmaVersion 2022, allowAwaitOutsideFunction), walks with estree-walker and regenerates with escodegen. Rewrites: a double-quoted Literal (raw[0]==='"') or an untagged TemplateLiteral becomes `m(value, node.start)` (the minilang can be overridden via registerLanguage('minilang')). Single-quoted strings are left alone. `/* mini-off */ ... // mini-on` comments disable the rewrite. `slider(v,min,max,step)` becomes `sliderWithID('slider_<pos>', v, ...)`. Methods registered via registerWidgetType (codemirror registers _pianoroll/_punchcard/_scope/...) get a widget id as their first argument. A bare `samples(...)` call gets `await`. A LabeledStatement becomes `expr.p('label')`. K(...) is compiled to kabelsalat `worklet(...)`. Tagged `tidal`/registered-language templates are handled separately. The last statement gets `return`, and the transpiler throws 'unexpected ast format without body expression' if the last statement is not an expression. Empty code yields `silence`. `export const evaluate = (code) => _evaluate(code, transpiler)` in index.mjs. Also exports registerWidgetType, registerLanguage and getWidgetID.

labelToP: `x: y` becomes `y.p('x')` (comment refs codeberg issue 990). `.p` is NOT defined in pattern.mjs; core repl() injects it in injectPatternMethods. In 1.2.6: an id starting or ending with '_' returns silence (mute). An id containing '$' becomes `${id}${anonymousIndex++}`. The pattern is stored in `pPatterns[id]` and returned. Getters `.d1..d9`/`.p1..p9` call `.p(i)`, and `.q`/`q1..q9` return silence. After eval, if pPatterns is non-empty: keys of length > 1 starting with 'S' solo (e.g. `S$:`, so other patterns are dropped). Each pattern gets `withState(s => s.setControls({id:key}))`; this goes in state.controls, not hap.context. Then `each` is applied per pattern, then `stack(...patterns)`, then every `all(fn)` transform. A non-Pattern result becomes `silence`. The unlabeled final expression is ignored when labels exist. `hush()` resets pPatterns before each eval.

`export const evalScope = async (...args)` runs Promise.allSettled over modules or promises. It copies every export onto `globalThis[name]` and `strudelScope[name]` and warns on rejected modules. `export const evaluate = async (code, transpiler, transpilerOptions)`: with a transpiler, code is replaced by `transpiled.output` and `meta = transpiled`. safeEval wraps the code as `(async ()=>{CODE})()` and runs `Function('"use strict";return (' + str + ')')()`. Returns `{ mode: 'javascript', pattern, meta }`. Without a transpiler it expects a single expression. Consequences: 'unsafe-eval' CSP is required; the scope is globalThis (one realm per worker); strict mode makes undeclared assignments throw.

findings.topic: What core repl() does with the evaluated result
findings.detail: `repl({ defaultOutput, onEvalError, beforeEval, beforeStart, afterEval, getTime, transpiler, onToggle, editPattern, onUpdateState, sync=false, setInterval, clearInterval, id, mondo=false })` returns `{ scheduler, evaluate, start, stop, pause, setCps, setPattern, setCode, toggle, state }`. Its `evaluate(code, autostart=true, shouldHush=true)` calls injectPatternMethods (defines .p and evalScopes all/each/hush/cpm/setCps/setcps/setCpm/setcpm/compileKabel), then beforeEval, then hush. It runs core evaluate, does the label stacking described above, then `editPattern`, then `scheduler.setPattern(pattern, autostart)`. It updates state with miniLocations, widgets and pattern, then calls `afterEval({code, pattern, meta})`. Errors are CAUGHT: it logs, sets state.evalError, calls onEvalError and returns undefined. The Cyclist constructor (cps=0.5) only builds a zyklus clock and does not start it unless autostart. So `repl({transpiler, defaultOutput: ()=>{}, getTime: ()=>0, onEvalError})` + `await r.evaluate(code, false)` + `r.scheduler.cps` works headlessly in 1.2.6. On main, defaultOutput throws and the callback is `onSchedule(hap, t, cps)`.

findings.topic: Import-time side effects per package (Worker/Bun suitability)
findings.detail: core: index.mjs re-exports speak.mjs (`window?.speechSynthesis` inside try/catch, so it only warns). signal.mjs adds a mousemove listener guarded by `typeof window`. ui.mjs touches `document` only inside functions. NeoCyclist uses `new SharedWorker(new URL('./clockworker.js', import.meta.url))` only when constructed with sync=true. logger uses performance.now() and dispatches a CustomEvent only if `document` exists. errorLogger reads `process.env.NODE_ENV` (left unreplaced in dist/index.mjs, so a raw-browser worker gets a ReferenceError on the error path unless the bundler defines it). mini: only krill parser + core. tonal: dist imports only @tonaljs/tonal, @strudel/core and chord-voicings (CJS); `webmidi` is a dependency but is not imported. transpiler: acorn, escodegen, estree-walker; pure. draw: window/document/requestAnimationFrame inside functions only. superdough: AudioContext created lazily via getAudioContext(); `typeof window` guarded listener. webaudio: imports superdough, supradough and draw, and calls registerWorklet at import; Strudel's tests still import it in Node with vite-plugin-bundle-audioworklet. @strudel/web@1.3.0 web.mjs runs `window.initStrudel = initStrudel` at top level, so it throws in a Worker/Node. codemirror: needs DOM. Conclusion: core+mini+tonal+transpiler are fine in a module Worker and in Bun/Node, apart from the kabelsalat link issue below.

findings.topic: BLOCKER: @strudel/core@1.2.6 cannot be imported by plain Node or the Bun runtime
findings.detail: core@1.2.6 dist/index.mjs line 2: `import { SalatRepl as Ge } from "@kabelsalat/web"`, and repl.mjs runs `new SalatRepl({localScope:true})`. @kabelsalat/web@0.4.1 package.json: {"type":"module","module":"dist/index.mjs","main":"dist/index.js"}, with no exports field. dist/index.js is an IIFE (`var kabelsalat=function(l){...`) with no ESM exports. Node ignores `module`. Bun docs: 'At runtime Bun prefers "main" ... and uses "module" otherwise'. So the named import fails to link (same error as issue #1921: "does not provide an export named 'SalatRepl'" under Vite SSR/Node). The fix was merged on main (issues #1930/#1932, 2026-01-18) but not released. core@1.2.5 (2025-10-27) depends only on fraction.js. Vite (browser) resolves `module`, so the browser app is unaffected. dist/index.mjs of kabelsalat/web has no top-level side effects (worklets are inlined data: URLs; AudioView's constructor only sets fields).

findings.topic: Querying: queryArc vs query vs firstCycle
findings.detail: `queryArc(begin, end, controls = {})` is `this.query(new State(new TimeSpan(begin, end), controls))` inside try/catch. On error it calls errorLogger and returns [], so errors are SILENTLY SWALLOWED. Examples: scaleTranspose without scale, an invalid scale step, a bad chord. `firstCycle(with_context=false)` calls `this.query(...)` directly, so errors propagate. It strips context unless with_context is true. Also: `firstCycleValues`, `showFirstCycle`, and `sortHapsByPart()` (a Pattern transform sorting by part.begin, then part.end, then whole). `onsetsOnly()` filters hap.hasOnset(). `discreteOnly()` drops haps without a whole (continuous signals). `defragmentHaps()` merges adjacent fragments ('only intended for use in tests'). `splitQueries()`. State is `{span, controls}`; the scheduler passes controls `{_cps, cyclist:'cyclist'}` and loopAt/fit read `state.controls._cps`. Exports: Pattern, State, TimeSpan, Hap, Fraction, stack, cat, seq, fastcat, slowcat, sequence, timeCat/stepcat, arrange, polymeter, silence, pure, reify, register, isPattern.

`class Hap { constructor(whole, part, value, context = {}, stateful = false) }`. whole is a TimeSpan, or undefined for continuous haps. part is a TimeSpan. `get duration` uses value.duration if numeric, else whole.end - whole.begin, multiplied by value.clip (legato is an alias of clip). `hasOnset()` = whole defined && whole.begin.equals(part.begin). `wholeOrPart()`, `show(compact)` gives e.g. '[ 0/1 → 1/2 | note:c4 ]', `showWhole(compact)`, `hasTag`, `combineContext` (concatenates locations). context.locations is an array of `{start, end}` absolute character offsets into the ORIGINAL user code; transpiler offset plus the leaf offset in the mini string, e.g. `note("c4 e4")` gives c4 at {start:6,end:8}. Pure function args add their locations too (register's __pure_loc). context.scale is set by .scale(). TimeSpan has begin and end (Fractions), spanCycles, duration, cycleArc(), intersection(), intersection_e(), midpoint(), equals(), show(). Fraction is fraction.js v5 with n/d/s as BigInt and no toJSON. Strudel adds sam, nextSam, cyclePos, lt/gt/lte/gte/eq/ne, min/max, show() → 's*n/d'. Use `.valueOf()` for a number or `.toFraction()` for 'a/b'. JSON.stringify(Fraction) throws (BigInt). Structured clone keeps BigInt fields but loses the prototype, so normalize before postMessage.

seq/sequence/fastcat squeeze n items into one cycle (slowcat(...)._fast(n)). cat/slowcat play one item per cycle, splitQueries at cycle boundaries, with an offset so sub-pattern cycles are not skipped. Mini `<a b>` is 'polymeter_slowcat' (stack of child._slow(weight)). stack: simultaneous, concatenated hap lists. slow(n)/fast(n) scale time, so a whole can span several cycles; when queried per cycle you get fragments where part ≠ whole and only the first has an onset. Euclid `x(3,8)` gives onsets at 0, 3/8, 3/4, each 1/8 long; euclidRot(3,8,2) gives 0, 1/4, 5/8. Mini ops: `*`/`/` (stretch fast/slow), `!` replicate, `@` weight (timeCat), `(k,n,r)` bjorklund, `?` degradeBy (seeded), `:` tail (array values, e.g. 'bd:3'), `..` range, `|` random choice, `{}` polymeter, `,` stack, `.` feet, `~`/`-` rest. Numeric atoms become numbers, everything else stays a string.

The tempo is global Cyclist state: `this.cps = 0.5` by default, changed by `setCps(cps)`. setcps/setcpm (setcpm(x) = setCps(x/60)) exist only via repl's evalScope. Strudel's own test runtime mocks them as identity. A hap value `cps` (registerControl('cps')) makes Cyclist switch tempo when that hap triggers (cyclist.mjs L72). `.cpm(n)` in repl scope is `pat._fast(cpm/60/scheduler.cps)`, a relative speed-up rather than a tempo change. The core fallback is `_fast(cpm/60/1)`. `getCps()` in schedulerState returns the scheduler cps only when a repl exists. The docs say Strudel has no bars, only cycles. For bpm in 4/4 use `setcpm(bpm/4)`. Default 0.5 cps = 30 cpm = 120 BPM at 4 beats per cycle. Conversions: seconds = cycle/cps (util.cycleToSeconds); beats = cycles × beatsPerCycle (lesson-defined).

findings.topic: How superdough resolves sounds (for completeness, not needed to grade)
findings.detail: `superdough(value, t, hapDuration, cps=0.5, cycle)`: s defaults to getDefaultValue('s') = 'triangle'. `if (bank && s) s = `${bank}_${s}``. Pitch is `valueToMidi(hapValue, 36)`: with an object bank keyed by note names, it picks the nearest key and repitches; with an array bank, transpose = midi-36. Oscillators use getFrequencyFromValue. findings.detail: `scale` is registered patternified (so `.scale("<C:major A:minor>")` works) and preserves steps. If the arg is an Array (from mini ':' syntax) it is joined with ' '. getScale replaces ':' with ' ' and calls tonal `Scale.get`. It throws 'Scale name ... is incomplete' or 'Invalid scale name'. A step value (number, or a string like '3#', '-2', '4bb') goes through `scaleStep`: the tonic defaults to 'C' and its octave to 3. Octave wrapping uses Interval.add; accidental suffixes add semitones via getAccidentalsOffset. With `anchor` in the value it uses stepInNamedScale. A note value (isNote) is snapped to the nearest scale note, preferring higher (_getNearestScaleNote). Output note strings are uppercase with octave ('E3'). The hap is tagged `context.scale`. Per-hap errors go through errorLogger and the hap is DROPPED (removeUndefineds), so you get no exception. A primitive value becomes a primitive note string.

`transpose`/`trans`: number note gives note + semitones (a string interval is converted via Interval.semitones). String note gives Note.transpose(note, Interval.fromSemitones(n) or interval string like '3M'/'5P'), so spelling is preserved. A non-note logs a warning and passes through. On main, octave-less notes are now handled differently. `scaleTranspose`/`scaleTrans`/`strans`: requires hap.context.scale (set by .scale()) or it throws 'can only use scaleTranspose after .scale'. It steps within the scale's pitch classes, carrying the octave at C.

In mini strings, spaces must be ':' ("C4:minor:pentatonic"). Names containing ' or # are unsafe in mini notation.

`voicing` is registered with arity 1, so it is called as `.voicing()`. A string value becomes {chord}. It destructures `{ dictionary = defaultDict ('ireal'), chord, anchor, offset, mode, n, octaves, ...rest }`. A string dictionary is looked up in voicingRegistry; an object is used inline with mode 'below' and anchor 'c5'. It calls `renderVoicing({...dict, chord, anchor, offset, mode, n, octaves})` and returns `stack(...notes).note().set(rest)`. Any error (unknown symbol or dict) goes to `logger('[voicing]: unknown chord ...')` and returns silence. renderVoicing defaults: offset=0, mode='below', anchor='c5', octaves=1. Because anchor/mode are passed explicitly as undefined, the registry's own mode/anchor (e.g. guidetones 'above', 'a4') are overridden by these defaults. An anchor without an octave defaults to octave 4; numbers are accepted. Modes: below (top note ≤ anchor), duck (below, with the anchor note removed), above (bottom ≥ anchor; BUGGY in 1.2.6, fixed on main, which adds 'oldabove'/'oldroot'), root. offset rotates through the voicing list with octave carry. n turns the voicing into a scale: `scaleStep(notes, n, octaves)` returns a MIDI number. tokenizeChord regex: /^([A-G][b#]*)([^/]*)[/]?([A-G][b#]*)?$/. The root must be uppercase; the slash bass is parsed but ignored. Output spellings are flats only (midi2note with the flats table).

rand, irand, `?`, sometimes, degradeBy and `|` are deterministic functions of query time (seeded hash). `useRNG('legacy'|'precise')` switches a module-global RNG_MODE ('legacy' is the default). `getRandsAtTime(t, n, seed)`. Mini `?` and `|` use `rand.early(0.0003*seed)`. The same query always gives the same haps, so snapshots of random patterns are stable within one version.

Bun supports the global `Worker` constructor with options `preload`, `smol` and `ref`. TS worker files run directly and `worker.terminate()` works, though the docs say 'The Worker API is still experimental (particularly for terminating workers)'. Browser: Vite module worker via `new Worker(new URL('./grader.worker.ts', import.meta.url), {type:'module'})`. A synchronous infinite loop in learner code or a huge query (e.g. `.fast(1e7)`) can only be stopped by terminate() from the parent, so every grade needs a parent-side setTimeout and a fresh worker after a kill.

Capture logger output (console.log in the worker) and use pattern.query or firstCycle so exceptions surface.

errorLogger references `process.env.NODE_ENV` unreplaced in dist. In a browser worker built without a define it throws a ReferenceError on the error path. Set define: {'process.env.NODE_ENV': ...} in Vite/Bun.build.

Global mutable state per realm: evalScope writes to globalThis; Pattern.prototype.p is injected; RNG_MODE; voicings' lastVoicing; the timelines in impure.mjs; and the globalThis._strudelLoaded double-load warning. Use one dedicated worker realm, reset state (resetVoicings(), useRNG('legacy'), clear the p-map) before every grade, and never evaluate two submissions concurrently in one realm.

Version drift: main has unreleased breaking changes (repl defaultOutput→onSchedule, transpiler plugin split, fixed voicing mode 'above'/'root', transpose octave logic). Snapshot tests on exact voicing octaves or note spellings will break on the next release. Pin exact versions with a lockfile, and grade on MIDI or pitch-class sets rather than spellings.

Pitch ambiguity: n without scale is a sample index, not pitch (a synth falls back to midi 36). Octave-less notes default to octave 3 ('c' = C3 = 48). The `octave` control shifts pitch at playback but is not reflected in the note. freq maps to fractional MIDI. Normalization must handle all of these explicitly.

Fragments: slow/cat/splitQueries can split one note into several haps with part ≠ whole. Count only hasOnset() haps and measure from whole, or use defragmentHaps(), or rhythm grading will double-count.

Unsupported methods in headless scope: pianoroll/punchcard/scope/_pianoroll, slider/sliderWithID, samples(), setcps, all/each, color/markcss and similar throw TypeError or ReferenceError unless stubbed. Lesson code copied from strudel.cc will hit these.

Function() eval needs CSP 'unsafe-eval'. Learner code runs with full worker privileges (fetch, dynamic import). That is acceptable for a local-first personal app, but don't reuse the grader worker for anything sensitive.
Licensing: Strudel is AGPL-3.0-or-later. Using it in a personal local app is fine; hosting it publicly as a network service triggers AGPL source-offer obligations.

Bun's Worker API is marked experimental, particularly terminate(). Verify that the timeout and kill path is reliable in Bun 1.4 and fall back to a subprocess (Bun.spawn plus kill) for test-suite sandboxes if needed.
recommendations: Pin the family and fix the Bun import. Either pin @strudel/core/mini/tonal/transpiler to exact 1.2.6 and run `bun patch @kabelsalat/web` to add `"exports": {".": "./dist/index.mjs"}` (or set main to dist/index.mjs), or alias '@kabelsalat/web' to a stub `export class SalatRepl { evaluate(){ throw new Error('kabelsalat disabled') } }` via a Bun onResolve plugin preloaded in bunfig [test] and a Vite resolve.alias. Pinning 1.2.5 is the fallback but loses the `S$:` solo and other 1.2.6 changes. Do not import @strudel/web, webaudio, superdough, draw or codemirror in the grader.

Grader worker setup, run once per realm: `import * as core from '@strudel/core'; import * as mini from '@strudel/mini'; import * as tonal from '@strudel/tonal'; import { transpiler } from '@strudel/transpiler';` then `await core.evalScope(core, mini, tonal, stubs)`. stubs = { setcps: v => (cps = v, core.silence), setcpm: v => (cps = v/60, core.silence), samples: async () => {}, sliderWithID: (_id, v) => core.pure(v), all: f => (allFns.push(f), core.silence), each: f => (eachFn = f, core.silence), hush: () => core.silence }. Also add identity stubs on Pattern.prototype for pianoroll, punchcard, spiral, pitchwheel, wordfall, scope, tscope, fscope, spectrum, _pianoroll, _punchcard, _scope, _spiral, _pitchwheel, _spectrum, markcss, color (if missing) and dough. Define `Pattern.prototype.p` by copying repl.mjs: mute ids starting or ending with '_', append an index to ids containing '$', store the pattern in a Map and return this.

Grading call: `const { pattern, meta } = await core.evaluate(code, transpiler, { emitWidgets: false })`. Build tracks = Map of label to pattern; apply the solo rule (keys starting with 'S'), then `final = tracks.size ? stack(...tracks.values()) : pattern`. Query each track separately for per-part feedback with `pat.query(new core.State(new core.TimeSpan(core.Fraction(0), core.Fraction(N)), { _cps: cps }))` so errors throw. Keep `h.whole && h.hasOnset()` haps and return plain JSON: { track, begin: whole.begin.valueOf(), end: whole.end.valueOf(), beginFrac: whole.begin.toFraction(), dur: h.duration.valueOf(), midi: tryMidi(h.value), s: value.s, bank: value.bank, n: value.n, locations: h.context.locations, raw: value }.

Pitch normalizer: if value is a number, treat it as MIDI. If it is a string and isNote, use noteToMidi. If it is an object: freq gives Math.round(freqToMidi), a string note gives noteToMidi, a number note gives the note. In both object note cases add 12*value.octave if present. If there is n but no note and no scale tag, return null and give the specific feedback 'n is a sample index — add .scale()'. Grade melodies on MIDI (or MIDI mod 12 for octave-agnostic tasks), chords on the pitch-class set of haps sharing the same whole, and rhythm on onset fractions (exact Fraction compare via toFraction()).

Error capture: wrap console.log/warn/error inside the worker during evaluate and query, and collect messages matching /^%c\[(tonal|voicing|mini|query|eval)\]/ or containing 'error'. Treat '[voicing]: unknown chord' and '[tonal]' errors as learner-facing hints. Map context.locations/meta.miniLocations back to CodeMirror ranges to highlight the exact offending token.

Timeouts: the parent owns the worker. Send {code, cycles}, start setTimeout(1500ms), and on expiry call worker.terminate(), spawn a fresh worker and report 'took too long (infinite loop or huge pattern?)'. Also cap the cycles queried and the hap count, e.g. abort if query returns more than 20k haps.

Tests in Bun: copy Strudel's runtime.mjs approach with your own `.p` collector. Use `queryCode(code, cycles) => final.sortHapsByPart().queryArc(0, cycles).map(h => h.show(true))` plus `expect(lines).toMatchSnapshot()` from bun:test, and apply roundFloatStrings for floats. Add equivalence tests in the style of `sameFirst(learnerPattern, referencePattern)`. For every exercise, keep (a) a reference solution and (b) known-wrong variants, and assert that the grader returns pass, fail and the expected hint.

Teach and lint the Strudel dialect explicitly: double quotes mean mini-notation; ':' replaces spaces in scale names; chord symbols are iReal-style (C^7/CM7, C-7/Cm7, Co7, Ch7, Csus, C+); middle C is c4 = 60 and 'c' alone is c3; use `setcpm(bpm/4)` for 4/4. A pre-grade lint pass on the AST (acorn is already a dependency) can catch 'Cmaj7', 'Cdim' and lowercase chord roots before evaluation.

Avoid deprecated `.voicings()` in course content; use `.voicing()`. For voicing exercises compare pitch-class sets or top-note and bass, not exact octaves, so the grader survives the mode 'above'/'root' fix on main.

reports.summary:
As of 2026-11-10 the latest npm release is still the January 2026 set: superdough@1.3.0, @strudel/webaudio@1.3.0, @strudel/soundfonts@1.3.0, @strudel/web@1.3.0, @strudel/repl@1.3.0, and @strudel/core/mini/tonal/transpiler/draw@1.2.6. All are AGPL-3.0-or-later. Codeberg main (codeberg.org/uzu/strudel) has unreleased breaking changes: `defaultOutput` was renamed to `onSchedule(hap, t, cps)`, `webaudioOutput` has a new signature, a ClockBridge was added, the node-pool context fix landed, and offline rendering is now chunked. Pin exact versions. superdough provides oscillators (triangle/square/sawtooth/sine + aliases tri/sqr/saw/sin, user via partials, one), supersaw, pulse, sbd, bytebeat, noises (white/pink/brown/crackle), zzfx (z_*), wavetables (wt_*), an 8-operator FM matrix, pitch/vibrato envelopes, and lp/hp/bp filters with ADSR envelopes and LFOs (12db/ladder/24db). Delay and reverb are per-orbit global effects. The reverb is generated algorithmically, so it needs no download. There is no master limiter. The strudel.cc REPL loads everything from strudel.b-cdn.net (CORS *, 30-day cache): Salamander piano (`piano`, 29 MP3s, 5.5 MB, CC-BY 3.0), VCSL (CC0, but multi-GB hi-res WAVs), tidal-drum-machines (71 banks, used via `.bank("RolandTR909")`), uzu-drumkit (default bd/sd/hh…, 2.6 MB, Unlicense), uzu-wavetables, mridangam (CC-BY-SA), a small Dirt-Samples subset (includes `jazz`), plus 125 lazily fetched `gm_*` WebAudioFont soundfonts from felixroos.github.io/webaudiofontdata (CORS *).

Local-first is very feasible. The two sound-source entry points (the `samples()` base URL / `_base` field, and `setSoundfontUrl()`) are the only remote hooks you need to change. AudioWorklets ship inline as data: URLs, so nothing is fetched for them. strudel.cc itself uses a Workbox CacheFirst runtime cache over exactly these hosts. A realistic self-hosted core set (piano, uzu-drumkit, 2–3 drum-machine banks, about 15 GM fonts) is roughly 20–25 MB. For audio-graph access, `getAudioContext()`/`setAudioContext()` and `getSuperdoughAudioController().output.destinationGain` give you a single master GainNode, which you can tap for a recorder, analyser or limiter. Per-pattern analysers come via `.analyze(id)` with `getAnalyserById`/`getAnalyzerData`.

Faster-than-realtime export exists as `renderPatternAudio()` (OfflineAudioContext → WAV). In 1.3.0 it closes the live AudioContext, always forces a browser download, and does not clear the node pools afterwards. That makes it hostile to a coexisting mic detector and to a post-export live session, so Oak should implement its own offline renderer modelled on it, or use realtime MediaRecorder. A mic pitch detector can share superdough's AudioContext if you follow these rules: never force a custom sampleRate (Firefox throws on rate mismatch); use echoCancellation/noiseSuppression/autoGainControl = false; recommend wired headphones (Bluetooth switches to HFP when the mic opens); and re-create the MediaStreamSource whenever the context is swapped. Two integration traps also need handling. First, initAudio() never actually resumes the context because of an operator-precedence bug, so call `resume()` yourself. Second, @strudel/web's dist is a self-contained bundle, so pairing it with @strudel/soundfonts creates two superdough instances and `gm_*` sounds go missing. Use the modular packages instead.

findings.topic: Synth controls: ADSR, filters + filter envelopes, FM, pitch env, vibrato
findings.detail: ADSR: attack/att, decay/dec, sustain/sus, release/rel, hold. getADSRValues smart defaults (e.g. only .decay set → decay-only env with sustain 0). Filters: lpf = cutoff (aliases ctf, lpf, lp; 'cutoff:resonance:lpenv' mini syntax), resonance/lpq; hpf = hcutoff (hpf, hp), hresonance/hpq; bandf (bpf, bp), bandq/bpq; ftype 0='12db' (biquad), 1='ladder' (worklet, uses drive default 0.69), 2='24db' (two biquads). Filter envelopes: lpenv/lpe (octaves, default 1 when any env param set), lpattack/lpa, lpdecay/lpd, lpsustain/lps, lprelease/lpr, fanchor; same for hp* (hpe,hpa,hpd,hps,hpr) and bp* (bpe,bpa,bpd,bps,bpr); filter env defaults [0.005,0.14,0,0.1] exponential. Filter LFOs: lprate, lpsync, lpdepth, lpdepthfrequency/lpdepthfreq, lpshape, lpdc, lpskew (+hp*/bp*). FM: fm/fmi (index), fmh (harmonicity ratio), fmwave ('sine' default), fmenv ('exp' default | 'lin'), fmattack/fmdecay/fmsustain/fmrelease, numbered fm2…fm8 / fmh2… and matrix fmi{i}{j} (alias fm{i}{j}) for operator routing; FM works on oscillators, supersaw, pulse. Pitch env: penv (semitones), pattack/patt, pdecay/pdec, psustain/psus, prelease/prel, pcurve, panchor. Vibrato: vib/vibrato/v (Hz), vibmod/vmod (semitones, default 0.5). Note: 'leslie','lrate','lsize','amp' are registered controls but NOT implemented in superdough (0 occurrences in superdough dist).

Per-voice chain order in superdough(): source → [stretch phase-vocoder] → [transient] → gain stage (gain default 0.8 × velocity/vel; setGainCurve() can make it quadratic) → lpf → hpf → bpf → vowel ('a','e','i','o','u') → coarse → crush (bits) → shape (deprecated, 'shape:shapevol') → distort/dist ('amount:postgain:type'; distortvol/distvol; distorttype/disttype ∈ scurve, soft, hard, cubic, diode, asym, fold, sinefold, chebyshev) → tremolo/trem (+tremolosync, tremolodepth, tremoloshape, tremoloskew, tremolophase) → compressor ('threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release', defaults -3:10:10:0.005:0.05; per-voice DynamicsCompressorNode) → pan (0..1) → phaser/phaserrate (+phaserdepth default .75, phasercenter, phasersweep) → postgain. Sends: delay ('delay:delaytime:delayfeedback'; delaytime/delayt/dt, delayfeedback/delayfb/dfb clamped 0.98, delaysync default 3/16 cycle), room ('room:size'; roomsize/size/sz/rsize 0–10, roomfade/rfade, roomlp/rlp, roomdim/rdim, ir + irspeed/irbegin for sample impulse responses). delay & room are per-ORBIT global effects (orbit/o, default 1) — patterns on the same orbit share one reverb/delay; FX arrays allow per-voice inserts. Also: djf (DJ filter per orbit), duckorbit/duck + duckdepth/duckonset/duckattack (sidechain ducking of target orbits), bus/busgain, dry, cut (cut groups), clip/legato, begin/end/loop/speed, channels. Reverb is algorithmically generated (reverbGen.mjs, ctx.createReverb) — no IR download.
