findings.detail: Remote endpoints in shipped code: superdough sampler — raw.githubusercontent.com (github: prefix), shabda.ndre.gr, http://localhost:5432 (local:), Bubobubobubobubo GitHub (bubo:) — all only when those prefixes are used. @strudel/soundfonts — https://felixroos.github.io/webaudiofontdata/sound (setSoundfontUrl overrides). Sample JSONs contain `_base` pointing at raw.githubusercontent.com (overridden by an explicit baseUrl arg). AudioWorklets (superdough worklets.mjs, supradough) are inlined as data:text/javascript;base64 URLs in dist — no fetch, but CSP must allow data: for script/worklet. @strudel/core's NeoCyclist uses new SharedWorker(new URL('./clockworker.js', import.meta.url)) only when sync:true (default Cyclist uses setInterval). Caching precedent: strudel.cc's AstroPWA/Workbox config uses runtimeCaching CacheFirst (cacheName 'external-samples', maxEntries 5000, 30 days, statuses [0,200]) for raw.githubusercontent.com, strudel.b-cdn.net, freesound, shabda, felixroos.github.io/webaudiofontdata, and precaches *.{wav,mp3,ogg,json} up to 4 MB each. Decoded AudioBuffers are cached only in memory (loadCache/bufferCache per URL); persistent caching must happen at HTTP/Cache API level (decoding repeats each session). The REPL also stores user samples in IndexedDB and registers them via URL.createObjectURL (idbutils.mjs) — Blob/object URLs work as sample URLs.

findings.topic: Self-hosting recipe on a Bun server
findings.detail: Mirror the needed files under e.g. /sounds/ and serve statically from Bun. Then: samples('/sounds/piano.json', '/sounds/piano/'); samples('/sounds/uzu-drumkit.json', '/sounds/uzu-drumkit/'); samples('/sounds/tidal-drum-machines.json', '/sounds/tidal-drum-machines/machines/') (or a pruned JSON with only the banks you teach); aliasBank('/sounds/tidal-drum-machines-alias.json'); setSoundfontUrl('/sounds/webaudiofontdata') before first gm_* trigger; registerSynthSounds(); registerZZFXSounds(); registerSoundfonts(). Alternatively registerSamplesPrefix('oak:', async (url) => [json, '/sounds/x/']) for a custom scheme. Approximate core download: piano 5.5 MB + uzu-drumkit 2.6 MB + TR909 4.9 MB + ~15 GM fonts (~3–6 MB) ≈ 20 MB; avoid VCSL (GBs) unless transcoded to Opus/MP3. Add a Service Worker CacheFirst for /sounds/* for offline-after-first-load, or pre-warm by fetching the URL list on install.

findings.topic: Audio graph: context, master node, analysers
findings.detail: audioContext.mjs: getAudioContext() lazily does new AudioContext() (no options); setAudioContext(ctx); setDefaultAudioContext(); getAudioContextCurrentTime(). webaudioRepl(options) calls options.audioContext ?? getAudioContext() immediately, so pass your own context there (or call setAudioContext first). Master path (superdoughoutput.mjs): per-hap chain → post GainNode → Orbit.summingNode (→ optional djf worklet) → Orbit.output (stereo GainNode) → StereoPannerNode → ChannelSplitterNode → SuperdoughOutput.channelMerger → SuperdoughOutput.destinationGain (GainNode) → ctx.destination. Access: getSuperdoughAudioController().output.destinationGain (master), .nodes[orbitNum] (Orbit with reverbNode/delayNode/output), .getBus(n). controller.reset()/resetGlobalEffects() recreates destinationGain (re-attach taps afterwards). No master limiter/compressor exists. Analysers: pattern `.analyze(id)` sends post-gain into getAnalyserById(id, fftSize=2**(fft+5), smoothing); read with getAnalyzerData('time'|'frequency', id); exported `analysers` map. Visuals in @strudel/webaudio: .scope()/.tscope(), .fscope(), .spectrum() (and drawTimeScope/drawFrequencyScope) — draw into @strudel/draw's getDrawContext() canvas. Analysers are skipped in OfflineAudioContext.
findings.evidence: superdough@1.3.0/audioContext.mjs, superdoughoutput.mjs, superdough.mjs (getAnalyserById, getAnalyzerData, resetGlobalEffects); @strudel/webaudio@1.3.0/webaudio.mjs, scope.mjs, spectrum.mjs

findings.topic: Recording for the album: realtime and offline options
findings.detail: Realtime: const ctx = getAudioContext(); const dest = ctx.createMediaStreamDestination(); getSuperdoughAudioController().output.destinationGain.connect(dest); new MediaRecorder(dest.stream, { mimeType }) (Chrome/Firefox audio/webm;codecs=opus, Safari audio/mp4) — captures everything superdough plays (not the mic unless you route it). Offline (faster than realtime): @strudel/webaudio exports renderPatternAudio(pattern, cps, begin, end, sampleRate, maxPolyphony, multiChannelOrbits, downloadName) — awaits getAudioContext().close(), creates new OfflineAudioContext(2, ((end-begin)/cps)*sampleRate, sampleRate), setAudioContext + setSuperdoughAudioController(new SuperdoughAudioController(ctx)), initAudio(), queries pattern.queryArc(begin,end,{_cps:cps}) sorted by onset, awaits superdough() for each onset hap (so all samples load before rendering), startRendering(), encodes 16-bit WAV (internal audioBufferToWav, not exported), ALWAYS triggers an <a download> click (no Blob returned), then setAudioContext(null), setSuperdoughAudioController(null), resetGlobalEffects(). strudel.cc's export (handleExport) stops the scheduler first and re-runs initAudio afterwards.

(1) It closes the live AudioContext → any mic MediaStreamSource/AnalyserNode on it dies. (2) superdough@1.3.0 nodePools.mjs has no clearNodePool and setAudioContext doesn't clear pools, so pooled BiquadFilter/DynamicsCompressor/supersaw AudioWorkletNodes created in one context can be reused in the next (live→offline→live) → likely 'cannot connect nodes from different AudioContext' errors; main branch fixes this (setAudioContext calls clearNodePool() and closes the previous context). (3) Download-only output. (4) Firefox lacks OfflineAudioContext.suspend (main renders whole, 1.3.0 always whole). Oak should implement its own offline renderer (same ~40 lines) that returns the AudioBuffer/WAV Blob to store in IndexedDB/OPFS or POST to Bun, ideally after a page-level 'render mode' or with a vendored clearNodePool patch.

findings.topic: initAudio() resume bug and init sequence
findings.detail: initAudio(options {disableWorklets, maxPolyphony, audioDeviceName, multiChannelOrbits}) contains `if ((!audioCtx) instanceof OfflineAudioContext) { await audioCtx.resume(); }` — operator precedence makes this always false, so the context is never resumed by superdough (bug present in 1.3.0 dist and Codeberg main). initAudioOnFirstClick() only listens for 'mousedown' (not keydown/touch). Oak should call `await getAudioContext().resume()` in its own user-gesture handler, then `await initAudio()` (loads worklets via audioWorklet.addModule). If audioDeviceName is set to a non-default device, initAudio calls getAudioDevices() → navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio:true}) with default constraints (AEC on) just to read labels — leave it default when running a pitch detector.
findings.evidence: superdough@1.3.0/superdough.mjs lines 168-178, 259-318; superdough@1.3.0/dist/index.mjs ('if (!c instanceof OfflineAudioContext && await c.resume(), t)'); main superdough.mjs line 304

findings.topic: Package composition trap: @strudel/web vs modular packages
findings.detail: @strudel/web@1.3.0 dist/index.mjs (850 KB) is fully self-contained (no import statements) and bundles its own superdough. @strudel/soundfonts' dist imports from '@strudel/webaudio' and 'sfumato'; @strudel/webaudio's dist imports 'superdough'. Combining @strudel/web with @strudel/soundfonts therefore yields two superdough module instances and registerSoundfonts() registers gm_* into a soundMap the player never reads ('sound gm_piano not found'). Use modular packages (@strudel/core, mini, tonal, transpiler, webaudio, soundfonts, draw, codemirror) with a single deduped superdough, as strudel.cc does. Also: `n()` on gm_* sounds selects the font variant; scale() removes n and sets note, so `n('0 2 4').scale('C:major').s('gm_piano')` is safe but bare `n()` doesn't set pitch.
findings.evidence: import scan of unpkg dists for @strudel/web@1.3.0, @strudel/soundfonts@1.3.0, @strudel/webaudio@1.3.0; @strudel/tonal@1.2.6/tonal.mjs (scale)

findings.detail: @strudel/soundfonts also exports loadSoundfont(url) (sfumato + soundfont2, MIT) and Pattern.prototype.soundfont(sf, presetIndex) which plays via startPresetNote(ctx, preset, midi, deadline) through onTrigger — this bypasses superdough's chain (no gain/filters/room/orbit and not routed via destinationGain, so a destinationGain recorder won't capture it). Usable to load a better .sf2 (e.g. a brush kit) but needs wrapping in registerSound to integrate with effects/recording.
findings.evidence: @strudel/soundfonts@1.3.0/sfumato.mjs, index.mjs; npm view sfumato (0.3.0 latest, dep ^0.1.2)

findings.topic: Mic pitch detector on the same AudioContext
findings.detail: Sharing superdough's context is fine: const src = getAudioContext().createMediaStreamSource(stream) → AnalyserNode or a lightweight AudioWorklet (YIN/MPM); never connect it to destination or into superdough orbits. Do not construct the AudioContext with a custom sampleRate: Firefox throws NotSupportedError when a MediaStreamSource's rate differs from the context's (bug 1725336, workaround per bug 1388586: use the default rate) and Firefox doesn't implement the getUserMedia sampleRate constraint (bug 1674892). Use getUserMedia({ audio: { echoCancellation: false, noiseSuppression: false, autoGainControl: false, channelCount: 1 } }) — AEC/NS/AGC distort sustained sung pitches, and on Safari/macOS echoCancellation:true engages voice processing that can duck playback (WebKit 294623, 215965; disabling may not fully remove initial ducking). With Bluetooth headsets, opening the mic switches them from A2DP to HFP (mono 8–16 kHz) for BOTH directions, degrading Strudel playback — recommend wired headphones or a separate mic. Any context swap (renderPatternAudio, setAudioContext) invalidates the source node → rebuild it. For rhythm/sing-along grading compensate scheduler latency (0.1 s) + ctx.baseLatency/outputLatency + input latency.

findings.topic: Polyphony / orbits / defaults relevant to lessons
findings.detail: DEFAULT_MAX_POLYPHONY 128 (setMaxPolyphony; oldest voices faded over 0.25 s). Default values: s 'triangle', gain 0.8, postgain 1, orbit 1, delayfeedback 0.5, delaysync 3/16, velocity 1, release 0.01, fft 8, channels [1,2]. setDefault(control, value)/resetDefaults(). multiChannelOrbits maps orbit n to output channels 2n-1/2n. registerSound(key, onTrigger(t, value, onended, cps), data) lowercases keys and replaces spaces with '_' — usable to register custom instruments (e.g. a WebAudioFont drum kit). soundAlias(original, alias) and aliasBank(map | url | bank, alias) for friendly names (e.g. 'rhodes' → gm_epiano1).

risks: AGPL-3.0-or-later on all Strudel packages: fine for a personal local app. If Oak is ever hosted or distributed to others, the whole client must be offered under AGPL-compatible terms.

Sample licensing is mixed. Salamander piano is CC-BY 3.0 (attribution needed), VCSL is CC0, uzu-drumkit is Unlicense, mridangam is CC-BY-SA 4.0. tidal-drum-machines and Dirt-Samples declare no license (GitHub API returns null). webaudiofontdata is MIT, but its source SF2s have mixed provenance (JCLive/Aspirin/Chaos/SBLive unclear; FluidR3 MIT; GeneralUser GS has its own permissive license). Fine for personal use, but don't redistribute the mirrors publicly.

Codeberg main contains unreleased breaking changes (defaultOutput → onSchedule, new webaudioOutput signature, ClockBridge, chunked offline render). A future npm release could break integration code. Pin exact versions and wrap Strudel behind an adapter module.

renderPatternAudio in 1.3.0 closes the live AudioContext, does not clear node pools (cross-context node reuse), and only triggers a download. Using it as-is for album export will break mic detection and may break live playback until reload.

initAudio() never resumes the AudioContext (precedence bug), and initAudioOnFirstClick only listens for mousedown. Without an explicit ctx.resume() in a gesture handler, keyboard-first users or Safari may hear silence.

First trigger of an uncached sample or soundfont pitch can be silently dropped (superdough skips haps whose async load finishes after their start time). Ear-training drills and assessments need an explicit preload step (loadBuffer / getFontBufferSource per pitch) before playing.
gm_electric_bass_finger:1 points at a misspelled file ('…_sf2_fible') that returns 404 in 1.3.0. Avoid that index or patch gm.mjs.

The soundfont loader uses eval (1.3.0) or new Function (main), and worklets load from data: URLs. A strict CSP needs 'unsafe-eval' and data: for scripts/worklets. The Strudel transpiler also evaluates user code dynamically.
Mixing @strudel/web (a self-contained bundle) with @strudel/soundfonts or other modular packages creates duplicate superdough instances, so gm_* sounds won't be found.
VCSL files are huge uncompressed WAVs (e.g. steinway 42 notes = 256 MB). Including VCSL instruments in lessons would blow the offline cache budget unless transcoded.

There is no master limiter: stacked parts plus distort/room can clip the master bus and exported tracks. Insert a DynamicsCompressor/limiter after destinationGain, and re-insert it after resetGlobalEffects().
Several registered controls are silently no-ops in superdough (leslie, lrate, lsize, amp, and many SuperDirt-only ones such as squiz, triode, ring). Lessons must not teach them as audible effects.
Bluetooth headphones combined with mic use drop all audio to HFP quality. Safari's voice processing can duck playback even with echoCancellation:false on first use.
Mic-detector AudioWorklet DSP shares the render thread with superdough worklets (supersaw, pulse, ladder, distort, crush). Heavy pitch detection there can cause audio glitches.
recommendations: Use the modular packages pinned to exact versions (@strudel/core/mini/tonal/transpiler/draw 1.2.6; @strudel/webaudio, superdough, @strudel/soundfonts, @strudel/codemirror 1.3.0) with a single deduped superdough. Do not use @strudel/web's bundled dist.

Create one AudioContext yourself, `new AudioContext({ latencyHint: 'interactive' })` with no sampleRate. Call setAudioContext(ctx) before anything else, pass it to webaudioRepl({ audioContext: ctx, transpiler, ... }), and on the first user gesture run `await ctx.resume(); await initAudio({ maxPolyphony: 128 })`.

Write an Oak prebake that mirrors strudel.cc but points at the Bun server: registerSynthSounds(), registerZZFXSounds(), registerSoundfonts() + setSoundfontUrl('/sounds/webaudiofontdata'), samples('/sounds/piano.json','/sounds/piano/'), samples('/sounds/uzu-drumkit.json','/sounds/uzu-drumkit/'), a pruned tidal-drum-machines.json with about 5 banks (TR909, TR808, LinnDrum, AkaiLinn, TR707) plus aliasBank. Re-implement the `.piano()` helper (s('piano').clip(1).release(0.1) plus pan-by-pitch). Rewrite every JSON `_base` to a local path that ends in '/'.

Write a one-off Bun script that mirrors the chosen files from strudel.b-cdn.net and felixroos.github.io/webaudiofontdata into /sounds (about 20–25 MB). Add a Service Worker with CacheFirst on /sounds/* (Workbox-style, as strudel.cc does) so the app works fully offline after first load.

Define curated Oak instrument aliases with soundAlias/registerSound so lessons stay stable and readable. For example: rhodes → gm_epiano1 (choose the variant by ear), upright → gm_acoustic_bass:1, ebass → gm_electric_bass_pick:0, jazzgtr → gm_electric_guitar_jazz, cleangtr → gm_electric_guitar_clean:5, crunch → gm_overdriven_guitar:4, organ → gm_drawbar_organ, tenor → gm_tenor_sax, horns → gm_brass_section. Unlock them progressively as part of the 'toolbox'.

For jazz drums, either register WebAudioFont GM percussion files (e.g. 128NN_12_JCLive_sf2_file.js) through a small custom registerSound or a pre-extracted WAV sample map, or self-host a CC0/CC-BY brush kit as a strudel.json map. Fall back to Dirt-Samples 'jazz' plus VCSL hihat/sus_cymbal/snare.

Build a preloader: for each lesson, list its sounds and pitches, then warm loadBuffer(url, ctx) for samples and getFontBufferSource(font, {note}, ctx) for each needed soundfont pitch before enabling Play or starting a drill.

Ear-training drills: call superdough(value, ctx.currentTime + 0.05, dur) directly with internal control names (cutoff, roomsize, etc.) instead of going through the pattern scheduler. Use `piano` for timbre realism and sine/triangle for pure-pitch drills.

Album export v1: a realtime MediaRecorder on a MediaStreamDestination tapped from getSuperdoughAudioController().output.destinationGain, with a limiter inserted before both the destination and the recorder. v2: Oak's own offline renderer modelled on renderPatternAudio that returns a WAV Blob (stored in IndexedDB/OPFS or posted to the Bun server), run in a dedicated render mode that stops the mic and rebuilds the live context and node pools afterwards (or vendor the main-branch clearNodePool fix).

Mic: getUserMedia({ audio: { echoCancellation: false, noiseSuppression: false, autoGainControl: false, channelCount: 1 } }), a MediaStreamSource on the shared context, and AnalyserNode or Worker-based pitch detection (keep any AudioWorklet light). Recreate the source after any context change. Show a setup check that warns about Bluetooth headsets and recommends wired headphones. Leave initAudio's audioDeviceName at its default.
Wrap all Strudel-facing calls in a single adapter module (getContext, play, stop, preload, record, renderOffline, analyser) so a future onSchedule/ClockBridge release only touches one file.
openQuestions: Does decodeAudioData on a context that renderPatternAudio has closed reject, and do cached AudioBuffers fully survive the live → offline → live swap in practice? This needs a quick browser test.
Which gm_epiano1 / gm_acoustic_bass / gm_piano variants actually sound best? Indices were verified but not auditioned. A listening pass is needed before freezing the curated aliases.
Exact list of GM percussion kits in WebAudioFont (kit numbers 0/4/12/16/18 seen for notes 35–51). Is there a usable brush kit, and what is its licence?
Will a Strudel 1.4/2.0 npm release (shipping onSchedule, ClockBridge, node-pool fix, chunked render) land soon enough to target instead of patching 1.3.0?

Does Bun's bundler handle the superdough/@strudel dists cleanly (data: URL worklets; the new URL('./clockworker.js', import.meta.url) worker only used with sync:true), or should the frontend use Vite while Bun stays the runtime/server?
The user's actual browser and headphone setup (Chrome vs Safari vs Firefox; wired vs AirPods) decides how much of the mic-coexistence mitigation is mandatory.

reports.summary:
Recommended approach: "sound → code → symbol" with three synchronized representations (Strudel code ↔ piano roll ↔ staff). Each concept goes Predict → Run → Investigate → Modify → Make (PRIMM). The Predict step doubles as inner-hearing practice: the learner hums what the code will sound like before pressing play. Teach pitch by scale degree from the start. Hooktheory and the pop/jazz units of Open Music Theory v2 both work this way, and it maps straight onto Roman numerals, Nashville numbers and Strudel's `n(...).scale("C:major")`. One trap: Strudel's scale index starts at 0 (degree − 1), so this must be taught explicitly. Standard notation comes after the sound and code, but it comes early: rhythm notation in unit 1, treble clef in unit 2, key signatures in unit 3, bass clef and the grand staff in unit 5, lead sheets in unit 7. Move minor/Aeolian and the 12-bar blues earlier than classical curricula do, because both are central to the target genres. Teach common progressions as named schemas (four-chord, doo-wop, Aeolian, Mixolydian, blues, ii–V–I). These named chunks are what make chord dictation fast. The proposed core is about 125 concept lessons plus about 12 checkpoints and about 25 capstone sessions (≈160 sessions of 20 min). Advanced tracks add about 75 sessions (jazz harmony ≈34, advanced rhythm ≈20, arrangement & sound ≈20), so ≈235 sessions in total, roughly 10–12 months at 5–6 sessions a week. Milestones: composing simple songs after ≈80 sessions; transcribing diatonic pop (bass, chords, melody) after ≈130–160; transcribing jazz standards and reharmonizing after ≈230. Transcription practice should continue after the last lesson.

Ear training should work inside a key first, in the style of the Functional Ear Trainer: a cadence sets the key, the learner names the scale degree, then sings it resolving to the tonic. Change the key, register and instrument sound on every question. Interval drills come second: teach intervals as distances between scale degrees in a key, and keep isolated-interval drills as a minor deck. Interleave categories once each has been introduced against a contrast. Wong, Chen & Lim 2021 found a robust interleaving advantage for interval learning when singing and reference-song aids were absent. Little et al. 2019 found that alternating practice with passive listening produced learning where continuous practice alone did not. For chord progressions, transcribe the bass line first: sing the bass as scale degrees, infer the roots, then the chord qualities, then the Roman numerals. A 2021 Music Theory Online pilot study supports bass lines plus schemata. Singing should be used daily and graded by microphone pitch detection (pitchy 4.1.0, McLeod Pitch Method). Most drills can be graded automatically: theory facts, scale-degree, interval and chord-quality ID, rhythmic and melodic dictation (compare Strudel events from `pattern.queryArc`, ignoring transposition), harmonic dictation, and singing (cents error). Compositions get rule-based checks plus formative feedback from Claude. Transcriptions of the learner's own audio cannot be strictly graded and are self-checked by A/B playback against the original.

Learning science: use FSRS (ts-fsrs 6.0.0 has a new `DefaultScheduler` API with FSRS-7 as the default) for both facts and perceptual "skill families". Each due perceptual family is reviewed as a short set of freshly generated trials, so the learner never memorizes a single clip. Interleave by default and tell the learner why, because people misjudge blocked practice as better. Use mastery gates (about 85–90%), adaptive difficulty targeting about 85% success, worked examples that fade, and PRIMM / Use-Modify-Create for code. Gamification only helps when rewards carry information. Sailer & Homner's 2020 meta-analysis found small positive effects (g = .49 on learning, .36 on motivation, .25 on behaviour), and expected tangible rewards undermine intrinsic motivation (Deci et al. 1999). In practice: unlocks are real Strudel tools gated by mastery; the skill map decays honestly with FSRS recall probability; the capstone album serves as an identity-building portfolio; every session ends with a saved musical sketch; streaks are forgiving and repairable, because broken streaks reduce later engagement (Silverman & Barasch 2023). Copyright-safe repertoire: in the US, all compositions published in 1930 or earlier are public domain as of 2026, including I Got Rhythm, Body and Soul, Georgia on My Mind, Embraceable You and On the Sunny Side of the Street. Add traditional folk songs, spirituals, blues and ragtime. For modern songs, the learner loads their own audio locally; it is never redistributed and never sent to Claude.

findings.topic: Established curricula: Open Music Theory v2 — order of topics
findings.detail: Fundamentals, in this order: notation → clefs → keyboard & grand staff → half/whole steps & accidentals → American Standard Pitch Notation (e.g. C4) → rhythm notation → simple meter → compound meter → major scales/degrees/key signatures → minor scales → intro to modes & chromatic scale → sight-singing & dictation basics → intervals → triads → seventh chords → inversion → Roman numerals → figured bass → SATB. Diatonic harmony is taught through the phrase model (T–PD–D–T): cadences → V7 → strong predominants → embellishing tones → cadential 6/4 → … → tonicization → modulation. Chromatic: modal mixture → Neapolitan → augmented sixths → … Jazz unit: Swing Rhythms → Chord Symbols → Jazz Voicings → ii–V–I → Embellishing Chords → Substitutions → Chord-Scale Theory → Blues Harmony → Blues Melodies & Blues Scale. Popular-music unit: Rhythm & Meter in Pop → Drumbeats → Melody & Phrasing → Form (AABA/Strophic, Verse-Chorus) → Texture → Harmonic Schemas (Blues-Based, Four-Chord, Classical-in-pop, Puff, Modal) → Pentatonic Harmony → Fragile/Absent/Emergent Tonics. Also has Hypermeter, Metrical Dissonance and Orchestration chapters. Takeaway: reuse OMT's pop 'schemas' framing for progressions, its jazz unit order, and its phrase-model approach to function. Skip species counterpoint, galant schemas, SATB and set theory: they don't serve the goals.
findings.evidence: https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/ (TOC HTML extracted 2026-11-10; v2, stable URLs since 2021-07-01)

findings.detail: Hooktheory I: 1 Building Blocks, 2 Harmony I, 3 Melody, 4 Harmony II, 5 Inversions, 6 Conclusion. It has 88 audiovisual examples and 41 exercises and uses piano-roll notation with no sheet music. Chords are labelled by Roman numeral / scale degree, not letter name, with 'six basic chords' (I ii iii IV V vi) and stable vs unstable degrees. Hooktheory II: 1 Seventh Chords, 2 Secondary Chords, 3 Embellishments, 4 Creative Techniques, 5 Songs in Minor, 6 Modes and Modal Mixture. Takeaway: harmony comes before melody, and functional (relative) labels come before staff notation; this works well for adult pop learners. Oak should keep that, but (a) bring minor in earlier (Hooktheory leaves it to Book II; indie and pop rely heavily on Aeolian) and (b) add staff notation alongside, because the learner wants it.

musictheory.net (39 lessons): Basics (staff/clefs, durations, measures/time signature, rests, dots/ties, steps/accidentals) → Rhythm & Meter (simple/compound, odd) → Scales & Key Signatures (major, minor, scale degrees, key signatures, calculation) → Intervals (generic, specific, writing, inversion) → Chords (triads, inversion, 7ths) → Diatonic Chords (triads, RN triads, diatonic 7ths, RN 7ths, minor, voicing) → Progressions (non-chord tones, phrases & cadences, circle progressions, common progressions, 6 and 6/4 chords) → Neapolitan. This is the classic notation-first order: symbols come long before sound. Levine, The Jazz Theory Book: Part I Theory: Chords and Scales (1 Basic Theory [intervals, inversions, triads], 2 The Major Scale and the II-V-I, 3 Chord/Scale Theory [major, melodic minor, diminished, whole-tone harmony], 4 How to Practice Scales, 5 Slash Chords). Part II Improvisation (6 From Scales to Music, 7 Bebop Scales, 8 Playing Outside, 9 Pentatonic Scales, 10 The Blues, 11 Rhythm Changes, 12 Practice). Part III Reharmonization (13 Basic, 14 Advanced, 15 Coltrane Changes, 16 Three Reharmonizations incl. 'Body and Soul'). Levine puts ii–V–I in chapter 2 and leaves reharmonization for last; Oak's jazz track should do the same. Berklee's Ear Training core: movable-do sight-singing plus transcribing rhythms, melodies and harmonies. ET1 covers 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 including 16ths and the tonic triad. ET4 covers chromatic pitches, 5/8, 7/8, 9/8 and secondary dominants.

findings.detail: pulse → subdivision → meter → rhythm notation. pitch/octave → half/whole steps → note names & keyboard → treble staff. half/whole → major scale → scale degrees (1–7, movable) → keys/key signatures/circle of 5ths. scale degrees → intervals (first as degree pairs in a key) → triads (quality) → chord symbols & inversions → bass clef/grand staff. triads + degrees → diatonic chords & Roman numerals → function (T/PD/D) & cadences → pop schemas. RN + rhythm → bass lines. degrees + chords → melody (chord tones vs non-chord tones, motif, phrase). meter + phrase → song form. major → minor (relative/parallel → harmonic/melodic). minor + degrees → pentatonic/blues scales. dominant-7 quality → 12-bar blues. triads → 7th chords → ii–V–I. diatonic + minor → modes (parallel/characteristic-tone approach). function + 7ths → secondary dominants → tonicization → modulation. minor + diatonic → borrowed chords/modal interchange. Jazz: 7ths → extensions/alterations → ii–V–I major & minor → guide tones/shells → rootless voicings → turnarounds/rhythm changes → tritone sub/backdoor → reharmonization. Rhythm: subdivision → syncopation → swing → 16th-note funk → compound meter/triplets → odd meters → polyrhythm/polymeter → clave/Euclidean rhythms. Arrangement: instrument roles need bass lines + voicing + form. Sound design (oscillators, filters, envelopes) has no theory prerequisites, so sprinkle it in early for motivation.

findings.topic: Recommended core sequence with lesson counts (~20-minute lessons)
findings.detail: U0 Onboarding & Strudel basics, headphone/mic calibration, vocal range: 3. U1 Pulse, tempo (setcpm), subdivision via mini-notation, meter, backbeat, rhythm notation, counting 1-e-&-a, rhythmic echo/dictation: 9. U2 Pitch/octaves, half/whole steps, note names, keyboard, accidentals, treble clef, pitch matching by voice: 8. U3 Major scale, degrees 1–7 (with movable-do syllables), keys as a parameter, key signatures, circle of 5ths, scale-degree ear training (1-3-5 → +2,4 → +6,7), first melodies & by-ear transcription of folk tunes: 10. U4 Intervals (generic/specific/quality, inversion, consonance), in-key interval hearing: 6. U5 Triads, quality, chord symbols, inversions & voice leading written by hand (before unlocking voicing()), bass clef, chord quality M/m → dim/aug: 8. U6 Diatonic chords, Roman numerals, T/PD/D function, cadences (authentic, half, plagal, deceptive), pop schemas (I–V–vi–IV, vi–IV–I–V, I–vi–IV–V, I–IV–V), bass-line-first chord dictation: 12. U7 Melody: contour, range, step/leap, motif & variation (rev/add/scaleTranspose), chord tones on strong beats, non-chord tones (passing, neighbor, appoggiatura, suspension), antecedent/consequent, call & response, reading lead sheets: 9. U8 Bass lines: root/5th/octave, approach tones, locking bass to kick, syncopated bass: 5. U9 Song form: phrase/section, verse-chorus, AABA, strophic, hypermeter, energy curve, arranging sections in Strudel: 5. U10 Minor: natural/relative/parallel, Aeolian pop (i–VI–III–VII), harmonic minor V, Andalusian cadence, melodic minor, minor-key degrees (b3 b6 b7): 9. U11 Major/minor pentatonic, blues scale, dominant 7, 12-bar & quick-change, turnaround, shuffle (swingBy), riffs: 8. U12 Seventh chords (maj7, 7, m7, m7b5, dim7), diatonic 7ths, guide-tone preview: 6. U13 Rhythm II: syncopation/anticipations, 16th grid, ties, 6/8 & 12/8, triplets: 6. U14 Modes via characteristic tone (Dorian ♮6, Mixolydian b7, Lydian #4, Phrygian b2), modal vamps: 6. U15 Secondary dominants & tonicization, chromatic scale degrees: 6. U16 Borrowed chords (iv, bVI, bVII, bIII; bVI–bVII–I): 5. U17 Modulation (pivot chord, direct, 'truck-driver' key change up a step for the last chorus): 4. findings.detail: Jazz harmony (~26 lessons + ~8 capstone sessions): chord-symbol conventions (Strudel/iReal: ^7, -7, ø, alterations) → extensions 9/11/13 and alterations → chord-scale basics → major ii–V–I in 12 keys → minor iiø–V7alt–i → guide-tone lines (3rds and 7ths) → shell voicings → rootless A/B voicings, drop-2 → turnarounds (I–vi–ii–V, iii–VI–ii–V) → jazz blues → rhythm changes → tritone substitution → backdoor (iv–bVII7) → secondary ii–Vs, diminished passing chords → reharmonization (follows Levine ch. 13–14) → optional Coltrane changes. Advanced rhythm (~16 + 4): syncopation hierarchy, swing ratios (swingBy amount), 16th-note funk (ghost notes, 'the one'), metric displacement, odd meters grouped as 2+2+3 etc., hemiola, 3:2 and 4:3 polyrhythm, polymeter, tresillo/cinquillo/son and rumba clave (3-2 and 2-3), Euclidean rhythms (Toussaint 2005: E(3,8)=tresillo, E(5,8)=cinquillo), metric modulation. Arrangement & sound (~16 + 4): instrument roles and frequency space, the harmonic series (why low thirds turn muddy and why voicing spacing matters), density/texture/energy curves, counter-melody, re-voicing per section, synthesis (oscillator, filter cutoff/resonance, ADSR), effects (reverb, delay), gain/pan basics, sampling, re-arranging a song in another genre. Advanced total ≈75 sessions.

findings.topic: Strudel features that matter for pedagogy (toolbox mapping) and traps
findings.detail: Verified in the tonal docs: `n("0 2 4 6 4 2").scale("C:major")`. The scale index starts at 0, so degree 1 = n 0. Teach this explicitly as 'array index = degree − 1' and show 1-based degree labels in the piano roll and staff. Also verified: `transpose(semitones)`, `scaleTranspose(steps)`, `rootNotes(octave=2)` (unlock with bass lines), and `chord("<C Am F G>").voicing()` with controls `dict`, `anchor` (default c5), `mode` (below|above|duck|root, e.g. "root:g2"), `offset`, and `n` (index into the voicing). Chord symbols follow iReal conventions: `-` = m, `^` = maj7, `+` = aug. Trap: `voicing()` does voice leading automatically and hides inversions, so lock it until the learner has voiced inversions by hand with note lists. The docs include a jazz-blues-in-F example where one `chord()` pattern drives melody, comping and bass with `.set(chords)`; it is ideal for J2. `swingBy(x, n)` splits each cycle into n slices and delays the second half of each slice by x relative to the half-slice. `swing(n)` = `swingBy(1/3, n)`, so with 1 cycle = one 4/4 bar, `swingBy(1/3,4)` gives triplet-swung 8ths. `pattern.queryArc(begin, end)` and `firstCycle()` return the events (haps) for automatic grading. Convention trap: Strudel has no built-in meter (a cycle is not necessarily a bar). Lessons should enforce 1 cycle = 1 bar and setcpm(bpm/beatsPerBar).

Primary label: scale-degree numbers relative to the tonic with accidentals (1 2 b3 4 5 b6 b7, #4 …). They line up with Roman numerals (bVII, bVI), Nashville numbers, modes, borrowed chords and jazz chord tones. Sung aid: movable-do with do-based minor (do re me fa sol le te), because one-syllable names are easier to sing than 'flat three'. Evidence on fixed vs movable do is mixed. Hung 2012 (85 college music majors) favored fixed-do for sight-singing accuracy. Older work (Buchanan 1946) and a child study (Holmes 2009) favored movable-do for amateurs and beginners. Choir experience predicted success better than the system did. Berklee's ET core uses movable-do. For an adult whose goals are functional (Roman-numeral transcription, composing), relative labels win on fit with the goals rather than on head-to-head evidence.
findings.evidence: https://repository.usfca.edu/diss/38 (Hung 2012) ; journals.ou.edu/jmtp (Larson on minor-mode solfège) ; https://college.berklee.edu/node/2464596

findings.topic: Ear training: tonal context first (Functional Ear Trainer method)
findings.detail: FET (Alain Benbassat): the user picks a key, the app plays a cadence to establish it, then a random note; the user names the scale degree. The goal is to learn each degree's 'personality' (scale-degree qualia) within a key, starting with a few degrees and expanding; sessions of about 10 min a day are recommended. Recommended Oak drill: I–IV–V–I cadence (vary voicing and instrument sound) → target note → answer → app plays the melodic resolution to the tonic and the learner SINGS it (graded by mic). Introduce degrees as 1/3/5 → +2/4 → +6/7 → minor b3/b6/b7 → chromatic. Change the key every question so the learner cannot rely on absolute pitch. Theory support: tonal hierarchy / key profiles (Krumhansl & Kessler 1982, Psychological Review 89(4)); scale-degree qualia and expectation (Huron, Sweet Anticipation, 2006). Known failure: users report 95–100% in-app scores yet weak ability with real music, so add tasks on real music (folk tunes, standards, the learner's own songs) and vary instrument sound, register, tempo and density.

findings.topic: Interval recognition: pros, cons and evidence
findings.detail: Pros: needed to name and notate, to spell chords and to hear leaps in melodies; context-free, so useful for jazz and chromatic lines. Cons: isolated intervals do not transfer well to hearing in a key; reference-song crutches ('Here Comes the Bride' = P4) are slow to use in real time. Evidence: Wong, Chen & Lim 2021 (Psychology of Music, doi 10.1177/0305735620922595): with reference songs and singing as aids, interleaved and blocked practice performed about the same; without aids, interleaving robustly beat blocking, and most learners wrongly judged blocking as more effective. Little, Cheng & Wright 2019 (Atten Percept Psychophys 81:344–357): continuous practice alone produced NO learning in interval comparison, but alternating practice with passive exposure did, and the gain carried over to an untrained interval-identification task. Recommendation: teach intervals as degree pairs in a key; keep a secondary isolated-interval deck (melodic ascending → descending → harmonic); interleave; add short passive 'listen-only' exposure blocks between drill sets.

findings.topic: Chord-quality and progression dictation: bass line first, schemas as chunks
findings.detail: Order for chord quality: M vs m (root position, close voicing), then dim and aug, then 7th qualities (maj7, 7, m7, m7b5, dim7), then inversions, then extensions. Randomize voicing, register and instrument sound so the learner hears quality rather than surface cues. Progression dictation protocol: (1) find and sing the tonic; (2) sing the bass line as degrees; (3) infer roots and qualities; (4) write Roman numerals; (5) check against the melody's chord tones. Evidence: 'What Are the Truly Aural Skills?' (Music Theory Online 27.2, 2021) argues Roman-numeral labelling can get in the way of perception; its pilot study suggests bass lines + schemata make harmonic dictation more perceptual. AP Music Theory guidance: start with the bass line only. Stevens (JMTP) warns that inferring chords from both outer voices breaks down when those voices are notated wrong, so grade the bass step separately to catch errors early. Teach named schemas (OMT: Four-Chord, Puff, Blues-based, Modal; I–V–vi–IV; ii–V–I) as whole chunks. Scaffold with partially completed dictations (Baylor open ear-training text, Unit 12).

findings.topic: Melodic and rhythmic dictation; difficulty modelling
findings.detail: Melodic dictation, following Karpinski's model (Aural Skills Acquisition, OUP 2000: hearing → short-term memory → understanding → notation): set the key and meter first; keep fragments short enough to memorize (start with 3–5 notes / 1–2 bars, stepwise, then add leaps); always sing the fragment back before writing it; limit the number of replays as a difficulty setting. Baker's 2019 LSU dissertation 'Modeling Melodic Dictation': computed melodic features approximate, but do not perfectly predict, teachers' difficulty ratings. So generate graded difficulty from features such as note count, leap size, chromaticism, rhythmic density and tonal ambiguity, then adapt it from the learner's actual success rate. Rhythm: tap or clap first (the app checks onsets via keyboard or mic), then write it in mini-notation, then pick or produce standard notation.
findings.evidence: https://repository.lsu.edu/gradschool_dissertations/4960/ ; https://davidjohnbaker1.github.io/document/computation-chapter.html ; Karpinski 2000 (cited via MTO 27.2 and JMTP literature)

findings.topic: Singing: why it speeds up learning, and how to grade it
findings.detail: Rationale: producing pitch forces the learner to commit to a category and makes errors visible. It builds inner hearing ('audiation' in Gordon's Music Learning Theory; Kodály's 'sound before symbol'). Berklee's ET core is built on sight-singing. In Wong et al. 2021, singing plus reference songs closed the gap between practice schedules. Uses in Oak: echo-singing, singing the tonic after a cadence, singing the resolution after each FET answer, singing bass lines before writing chord dictation, sight-singing from staff/code, and humming the PRIMM 'Predict' before pressing Run. Grading: pitchy 4.1.0 (McLeod Pitch Method; `PitchDetector.forFloat32Array(n)`, `findPitch(input, sampleRate)` returns [Hz, clarity]). Pipeline: reject frames below a clarity threshold → median-filter → convert to cents relative to the target → fold octaves (different voice ranges) → segment notes by onset/stability. Tolerance starts around ±50 cents and tightens to ±25. Require headphones to stop the app's own audio leaking into the mic.

findings.detail: L1 drum-loop rhythms generated by Strudel → L2 bass lines of generated loops (roots, diatonic) → L3 4-chord loops (bass first, then quality) → L4 2–4-bar melodies (stepwise, then leaps, then non-chord tones) → L5 public-domain folk songs, melody plus chords (Twinkle, Ode to Joy, Amazing Grace, Shenandoah, Scarborough Fair in Dorian, Drunken Sailor in Dorian, House of the Rising Sun trad.) → L6 blues and public-domain standards, melody plus changes as a lead sheet → L7 the learner's own recordings: bass → chords → melody, A/B-ing the Strudel transcription against the looped, slowed original (HTMLMediaElement.playbackRate with preservesPitch) → L8 full arrangement: drums, bass, chords, melody and a form map. Every level is answered in Strudel code, so the answer plays back for comparison. Generated levels (L1–L4) have exact answer keys; L5–L6 answer keys are authored by hand and checked programmatically (tonal 6.5.1).

findings.topic: What can be auto-graded, and how
findings.detail: Exact: theory facts (spelling, key signatures, RN ↔ chord in key; check with tonal 6.5.1); scale-degree, interval and chord-quality ID; schema ID. Rhythmic dictation: compare the learner pattern's `queryArc(0, bars)` onset set with the target, with tolerance and partial credit by onset F-measure. Melodic dictation: align the sequence of (pitch, onset) pairs, ignoring transposition (compare degrees), with edit-distance partial credit; separate pitch and rhythm scores. Harmonic dictation: score the bass line, root, quality and RN for each chord separately. Singing: cents error and timing via pitchy. Composition: rule checks on the events (ends on the tonic, cadence type at phrase ends, share of chord tones on strong beats, range/tessitura, using the required device such as a secondary dominant) plus formative feedback from Claude (comments only, never a gate). The learner's own transcriptions: no ground truth, so use A/B self-assessment. An optional rough reference: @spotify/basic-pitch 1.0.1 (audio→MIDI with ML; TF.js, heavy) for bass and melody. essentia.js 0.1.3 (last published 2022, stale) for key/chord estimates. Use both only as hints, never as answer keys.

findings.topic: Spaced repetition: FSRS via ts-fsrs 6.0.0 (API changed)
findings.detail: ts-fsrs 6.0.0 (npm modified 2026-10-28) supports FSRS-3/4/4.5/5/6/7 and defaults to FSRS-7. New API: `const scheduler = await DefaultScheduler({ version:'FSRS-7', desiredRetention:0.9, enableShortTerm:true, learningSteps:['1m','10m'], relearningSteps:['10m'], enableFuzz:false, maximumInterval:36500 })`; `scheduler.newCard({now})`; `scheduler.preview({card, now})` (Again/Hard/Good/Easy); `scheduler.review({card, grade: Rating.Good, now})` returns {card, revlog} without mutating the input card; `scheduler.model.forgettingCurve(card, elapsedDays)` gives recall probability (retrievability); `defineScheduler({model, chrono}).use(middleware).create({config})` for custom setups. The README says Node >=24 is required; Bun compatibility is unverified. The older `fsrs()`/`createEmptyCard()` API seen in many tutorials is out of date. Proposed adaptation for perceptual skills: a card is a skill FAMILY (e.g., 'degree 6 in major', 'm7 quality', 'I–V–vi–IV'). A review is a mini-set of 5–10 freshly generated trials (random key, register, instrument sound). Map to a grade: <70% Again, 70–89% Hard, ≥90% Good, ≥90% and fast median response time Easy. Use desiredRetention ≈0.9 for facts and ≈0.85 for perceptual families to keep daily load inside a 20-minute session. Note that FSRS parameters were fitted on flashcard recall, not perceptual learning.

findings.topic: Learning science: retrieval, spacing, interleaving, mastery, difficulty
findings.detail: Retrieval practice beats restudy for long-term retention (Roediger & Karpicke 2006, Psychological Science 17(3)). Dunlosky et al. 2013 (PSPI 14(1)) rate practice testing and distributed practice 'high utility' and interleaving 'moderate'. Spacing: Cepeda et al. 2008 (Psych Sci 19(11)) found a 'temporal ridgeline': the optimal gap between sessions grows with the retention interval, but as a fraction it shrinks (about 20–40% of a 1-week retention interval, far smaller at 1 year), so there is no fixed ratio and an adaptive scheduler is justified. Interleaving: Kornell & Bjork 2008 (learning categories such as painting styles, the analogue of chord qualities and genres); Rohrer & Taylor 2007 (math); Carter & Grahn 2016 (Frontiers in Psychology, doi 10.3389/fpsyg.2016.01251: clarinetists' interleaved-practice pieces were rated higher, with better goal setting and error detection); Wong et al. 2021 (intervals). Introduce new categories blocked in a small contrast set, then interleave. Mastery learning: Bloom; Kulik, Kulik & Bangert-Drowns 1990 (RER 60(2):265–299, 108 evaluations, average effect ≈0.52 SD reported secondhand, larger for weaker students). Use gates of about 85–90% on unit checks. Optimal difficulty: Wilson et al. 2019 (Nature Communications 10:4646): about 85% accuracy is optimal for gradient-based learners; the evidence is from models, but it is a reasonable target for adaptive drills. Deliberate practice: Ericsson et al. 1993, tempered by Macnamara, Hambrick & Oswald 2014 (Psych Sci 25(8), doi 10.1177/0956797614535810: practice explains about 21% of variance in music, about 12% overall). Feedback-rich, targeted practice matters but promises no guarantees. Citations without URLs here were not re-fetched this session.

findings.topic: Teaching through code: PRIMM, Use-Modify-Create, worked examples
findings.detail: PRIMM (Predict, Run, Investigate, Modify, Make; Sentance, Waite & Kallia 2019, Computer Science Education 29(2–3), doi 10.1080/08993408.2019.1608781): 13 schools, 493 students aged 11–14, 8–12 weeks; teachers reported that all learners made progress in mixed-ability classes. Use-Modify-Create (Lee et al. 2011, ACM Inroads). Worked examples, then faded examples, then open tasks (Sweller's worked-example effect; Kalyuga et al. 2003 expertise reversal: drop the scaffolds as skill grows). Parsons-style ordering puzzles work as 'arrange these chord blocks into a cadence' or 'order these bars into an antecedent/consequent'. Music-plus-code precedent: EarSketch (Magerko et al. 2016, ACM TOCE 16(4) art. 14) uses code-driven remixing to raise engagement, identity and belonging. Oak's micro-structure: Predict (hum or say what the code will sound like; partly gradable by mic) → Run → Investigate (toggle layers, view piano roll and staff) → Modify (targeted edit with an automatic check) → Make (a small original piece saved to the sketchbook). Present code, piano roll and staff together (Ainsworth 2006 DeFT framework: multiple representations help only when the links between them are made explicit, e.g. synchronized highlighting).

findings.topic: Gamification: what supports learning vs what is shallow
findings.detail: Sailer & Homner 2020 (Educational Psychology Review 32) meta-analysis: small positive effects; cognitive g=.49 (k=19, N=1686), motivational g=.36, behavioral g=.25. Game fiction and social interaction moderated the behavioral effect. Motivational and behavioral effects were less stable in the most rigorous studies. Deci, Koestner & Ryan 1999 (Psych Bull 125(6)): expected tangible rewards undermine intrinsic motivation; informational positive feedback does not. Self-determination theory: autonomy, competence, relatedness. Streaks: Silverman & Barasch 2023 (JCR 49(6):1095–1117, doi 10.1093/jcr/ucac029): seeing a broken streak lowers later engagement, more so when the person blames themselves; being able to repair the streak weakens the effect. Goal-gradient (Kivetz et al. 2006) and endowed progress (Nunes & Drèze 2006): effort rises as a goal gets closer, and a progress bar that starts partly filled helps. Supportive designs: (1) unlocks are REAL capabilities (e.g. `.scale()` after U3, `chord().voicing()` after hand-voiced inversions, `rootNotes` after U8, `swingBy` after the swing lesson, Euclidean rhythms after clave); (2) the skill map is shaded by FSRS recall probability, so it fades honestly and gives a real reason to come back; (3) an album/portfolio of capstones with auto-generated liner notes listing the theory used; (4) a 'can-do' ledger ('I can hear I–V–vi–IV in real songs'); (5) every session ends with a saved musical sketch; (6) a forgiving streak (count days with ≥1 review set, weekly freeze tokens, repair by doing an extra set, no shaming); (7) choice of genre flavour for each capstone (autonomy); (8) Claude as an engaged listener (relatedness). Shallow designs to avoid: XP per click or per minute, badges for time spent in the app, punishing streak loss, leaderboards (meaningless for a single user).

Minutes 0–5: warm-up of due FSRS items, interleaved across facts, perception and singing, in mini-sets; always start with something the learner will get right. Minutes 5–15: new concept via PRIMM in Strudel with 2–4 embedded automatic checks. Minutes 15–19: a 'Make' task producing a saved 4–8 bar sketch. Minute 19–20: can-do update, a preview of the next unlock (goal-gradient) and an optional Claude listening comment. Every 8–10 lessons: a timed challenge or mastery checkpoint (gates the next unit at ≥85–90%). Every unit: a 2–4 session capstone. After U6: an optional 'transcription gym' session type the learner can choose in place of a new lesson.
findings.evidence: Design synthesis from the learning-science findings above

findings.detail: C1 First Loop (after U1–U2, 1 session): 4-bar beat + root bass. C2 Four-Chord Song (after U6–U7, 2 sessions): I–V–vi–IV or vi–IV–I–V, 8 bars, original melody with ≥60% chord tones on strong beats, ending on a cadence. C3 Verse–Chorus Demo (after U9, 3–4 sessions): contrast via register, density and harmonic rhythm; ≥1:30; staff lead sheet exported. C4 Minor Indie Ballad (after U10, 2–3 sessions): Aeolian i–VI–III–VII verse, harmonic-minor V at the chorus cadence. C5 12-Bar Shuffle (after U11, 2 sessions): riff, swing, turnaround, call & response. C6 Modal Vamp (after U14, 2 sessions): Mixolydian rock (I–bVII–IV) or Dorian indie/funk (i7–IV7). C7 Chromatic Color (after U15–U17, 3 sessions): one secondary dominant, bVI–bVII–I, truck-driver final chorus. Core Finale (4 sessions): an original 'album single' + a full transcription of a public-domain song (melody, changes, form) arranged in Strudel.

J1 Guide Tones in 12 Keys (2 sessions): 3rd/7th lines over ii–V–I, using transposition in code to cover every key. J2 Jazz Blues in F (2–3 sessions): head + shell comping + walking bass; start from the docs example where one chord pattern drives melody, comping and bass. J3 Rhythm Changes Contrafact (3 sessions): new melody over the I Got Rhythm changes (the 1930 composition is now US public domain). J4 Reharmonize a Standard (3 sessions): Georgia on My Mind or Body and Soul (both 1930, public domain) with tritone subs, secondary ii–Vs and backdoor; compare with Levine ch. 16's analysis of reharmonized 'Body and Soul'. F1 16th-Note Funk (2 sessions): one-chord Dorian m7 vamp, ghost-note drums, syncopated bass, horn stabs. F2 Clave & Polyrhythm (2 sessions): son clave 3-2, tresillo bass, 3:2 layer, Euclidean percussion. F3 Neo-Soul Ballad (3 sessions): maj9/m11 voicings, swung 16ths, voice leading via anchor/mode. A1 One Tune, Two Genres (3 sessions): arrange St. Louis Blues (1914) or Sweet Georgia Brown (1925) as indie and as funk.

Rule: US compositions published in 1930 or earlier are public domain (1930 works entered on 2026-01-01; 1931 works enter on 2027-01-01). Duke's 1930 list includes: I Got Rhythm, I've Got a Crush on You, But Not for Me, Embraceable You (Gershwin); Georgia on My Mind (Carmichael/Gorrell); Dream a Little Dream of Me (registered 1930); On the Sunny Side of the Street; Body and Soul; Just a Gigolo; You're Driving Me Crazy; Beyond the Blue Horizon. Recordings from 1925 entered too, including Sweet Georgia Brown (Ben Bernie), St. Louis Blues (Bessie Smith with Louis Armstrong), Fascinating Rhythm (Whiteman), Nobody Knows the Trouble I've Seen (Marian Anderson). Caveats: only the composition is free; later recordings (e.g. Ray Charles's 'Georgia', 1960) stay copyrighted. Mood Indigo has 1931 sheet music, so it is free only from 2027. US sound recordings from 1930 are free only from 2031 (except recordings in 1930 films). Other public-domain material: earlier standards (anything published ≤1930, e.g. ragtime such as Maple Leaf Rag 1899 and The Entertainer 1902; St. Louis Blues 1914; Tiger Rag 1917; Tea for Two 1924; Bye Bye Blackbird 1926; Ain't Misbehavin' and Honeysuckle Rose 1929), traditional folk songs and spirituals, and 12-bar blues forms. Oak should ship ONLY its own Strudel renditions and lead sheets, never third-party audio. Watch for copyrighted modern ARRANGEMENTS of traditional songs (e.g. the Animals' House of the Rising Sun, Simon & Garfunkel's Scarborough Fair): transcribe the traditional melody. Outside the US, terms differ (e.g. life+70 years: Ira Gershwin died 1983, so his lyrics are protected in the EU until 2053).

The learner picks a local file (File System Access API or <input type=file>). It is decoded and played in the browser only: loop A–B, slow down with pitch preserved (HTMLMediaElement.playbackRate + preservesPitch), transpose for singing, and A/B or overlay against the learner's Strudel transcription. The audio stays in local storage (IndexedDB/OPFS), is never uploaded, and is never sent to the Claude server: send only the learner's transcription as code or events plus song metadata. Personal study use is plausibly fair use in the US, but this is not legal advice; the UI should state 'your files stay on this device'. Since Oak cannot know the ground truth, grade by self-assessment checklists (bass matches? chord changes line up? melody contour right?) plus optional basic-pitch hints.

Proposed: core ≈160 sessions (≈125 lessons + ≈12 checkpoints + ≈25 capstone sessions) + advanced ≈75 sessions (jazz ≈34, rhythm ≈20, arrangement ≈20) ≈ 235 × 20 min ≈ 80 h, plus ongoing reviews. Calibration: Hooktheory I+II = 12 chapters (I has 41 exercises), a pop-only scope of very roughly 15–25 h. musictheory.net = 39 short lessons, written theory only. A US college core is 4 semesters of theory + 4 of aural skills (Berklee ET1–4), several hundred contact hours with a wider scope (counterpoint, SATB, post-tonal). Oak sits between them by design. Expected milestones at 5–6 sessions a week: composes simple diatonic songs after ≈80 sessions (~3–4 months); transcribes diatonic pop bass, chords and melody after ≈130–160 (~6–7 months); transcribes jazz standards and reharmonizes after ≈230 (~10–12 months). Hearing is the slowest skill to build, so keep daily 'transcription gym' and FSRS reviews going after the last lesson.

findings.topic: Ear-training stage plan (runs alongside the theory units)
findings.detail: Stage A (U1–U2): higher/lower, same/different, pitch matching, rhythmic echo, finding the tonic after a cadence. B (U3): degrees 1-3-5 → +2,4 → +6,7 in major, FET-style, answers sung. C (U4, U7): degree pairs and intervals in a key; 3–5-note melodies sung back, then written. D (U5–U6): chord quality M/m → dim/aug; bass-degree dictation on 4-chord loops; schema ID. E (U10–U12): minor degrees b3/b6/b7, the Mixolydian b7 and Dorian ♮6 sounds, 7th-chord qualities, blues forms. F (U15–U17): chromatic degrees (#4, b2, #5, b7 as V/IV), recognizing secondary dominants and borrowed chords, detecting modulations. G (jazz): ii–V–I in major and minor, guide-tone singing, extension colour (9, #11, 13, alt), turnarounds. H (rhythm): syncopation positions, swing ratio, 16th placement, clave direction, odd-meter grouping.
findings.evidence: Design synthesis informed by Berklee ET1–4 topics and FET ordering

risks: Strudel's `n().scale()` index starts at 0 while scale degrees and Roman numerals start at 1. Without explicit teaching (and 1-based labels in the piano roll and staff) learners will mislabel degrees all the time.
Strudel has no notion of meter or bars; tempo is set in cycles. If lessons don't enforce '1 cycle = 1 bar' and setcpm(bpm/beatsPerBar), rhythm notation and Strudel code will disagree.
`voicing()` does voice leading automatically and hides inversions and chord spelling. Unlocked too early, it cuts out the learning of voicing by hand.
Strudel/iReal chord-symbol conventions (^7, -7, + for aug) differ from common lead-sheet symbols (maj7, m7, Δ). Show both and teach the mapping.

Ear-training scores can climb in the app without carrying over to real music (FET users report this). Without real-music tasks and varied instrument sounds, keys and registers, the app will look like it's working when it isn't.
FSRS was fitted to flashcard recall, not perceptual learning. Treating a skill family as one card is untested; watch whether daily review load stays inside 20 minutes.
ts-fsrs 6.0.0 changed its API (async DefaultScheduler, FSRS-7 default) and declares Node >=24; Bun compatibility is unverified. Tutorials using fsrs()/createEmptyCard() are out of date.

Mic pitch detection on untrained adult voices: octave errors, breathy/low-clarity frames, the app's own audio bleeding in without headphones, latency. Grading that is too strict will put a non-singer off; start with tolerant thresholds and fold octaves.
Strict mastery gates can frustrate; loose ones produce shallow knowledge. Gate perceptual drills on performance across ≥2 separate days, and never block creative sketching.
Gamification can turn into grinding for XP, and streak loss can hurt motivation (Silverman & Barasch 2023). Streaks must be repairable and rewards must carry information.

Copyright: the public-domain status is US-only; the user's country may differ (e.g. EU life+70). Modern arrangements of traditional songs and post-1925 recordings are still protected; never ship third-party audio.

Lesson content written by Claude can contain musical errors (wrong spellings, mislabelled Roman numerals). Every exercise and answer key needs programmatic checks (e.g. tonal 6.5.1) and render-and-listen QA.
Scope: ≈235 authored sessions plus generators is a lot of authoring. Lean on procedural generation for drills and keep the hand-authored content to the concept lessons and capstones.
basic-pitch (TF.js) is heavy and imprecise on dense mixes, and essentia.js is stale (0.1.3 from 2022). Grading of the learner's own audio can only ever be hints.
recommendations: Order each concept as sound → code → symbol: hear and play it in Strudel first, then name it, then see it on the staff. Keep code, piano roll and staff synchronized, with highlighting that links them.
Use scale-degree numbers (with b/#) as the main pitch language and movable-do syllables (do-based minor) as the singing aid. Teach Strudel's 0-based scale index explicitly as 'degree − 1'.
Run each lesson as PRIMM (Predict → Run → Investigate → Modify → Make). Make Predict a hum or sing step to train inner hearing, and make Make produce a saved sketch every session.

Teach minor/Aeolian right after diatonic major chords, and pentatonic, blues and the 12-bar form before seventh-chord theory. Treat common progressions as named schemas (four-chord, doo-wop, Aeolian, Mixolydian, blues, ii–V–I).
Ear-train in a key first (cadence → scale degree → sung resolution to the tonic), changing the key on every question. Keep interval drills secondary and in-key; transcribe chords bass-line first.

Build a transcription ladder from generated loops → public-domain folk songs → public-domain standards (1930 and earlier) → the learner's own audio. Every answer is written in Strudel code so it can be A/B'd against the original.

Auto-grade everything that has ground truth: compare Strudel events from `queryArc`, align melodies ignoring transposition, score Roman numerals per chord, measure singing in cents with pitchy. Use Claude only for formative, non-gating feedback on compositions.

Use ts-fsrs 6.x (DefaultScheduler, FSRS-7) for facts, and 'skill-family' cards for perceptual drills, each reviewed as a mini-set of freshly generated trials. Interleave by default and show the learner why.
Gate units at 85–90% mastery; keep adaptive drills near 85% success; fade worked examples as skill grows (expertise reversal).

Make rewards carry information: real Strudel tools as unlocks, a skill map that fades with FSRS recall probability, a capstone album with liner notes, a can-do ledger, a forgiving and repairable streak, and genre choice for each capstone. No XP for time spent.
Plan ≈160 core sessions and ≈75 advanced sessions. Show milestones ('you can now compose…', 'you can now transcribe…') so progress is felt along the way, not only at the end.
Ship only Oak's own Strudel renditions. Keep the learner's own audio local and never send it to the tutor server; send only the transcription and metadata.
openQuestions: Which country is the user in? Public-domain status of the jazz standards (e.g. the Gershwin lyrics) depends on it.
How comfortable is the user singing, and what is their vocal range? This sets how central graded singing is and the default octave and tolerance.
Will the user have a MIDI keyboard or a computer-keyboard piano for input, or only code + mic? This affects dictation input and how fast drills go.
How much hand-written staff notation does the user want (read-only vs writing via a click-to-place staff editor), versus writing notation as code with staff rendering?
Solfège preference: numbers only, movable-do syllables, or both? For minor: do-based or la-based?
How strict should gates be? Hard mastery gates or soft gates (proceed while the skill map flags weak nodes)?
Realistic days per week? This changes the timeline (≈235 sessions) and the FSRS desiredRetention needed to keep review load inside 20 minutes.
Which modern songs (the learner's own audio) does the user most want to transcribe? These anchor motivation and could set the order of transcription-gym targets.

reports.summary:
I checked current versions against the npm registry on 2026-11-10 and read the published sources and typings. Several facts differ from what memory would suggest. wavesurfer.js is now v8 (8.0.5; 8.0.0 shipped 2026-09-23), not v7. ts-fsrs 6.0.0 (2026-10-28) replaced createEmptyCard/fsrs().repeat/next with an async `DefaultScheduler()` that uses FSRS-7 by default; the old calls are deprecated. Vite is 8.3.7 and is built on Rolldown. Vitest is 5.1.0, React 19.3.1, Jotai 3.0.2 and TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler). ml5 1.4.0 no longer has pitch detection. VexFlow has had no release since 5.0.0 in March 2025, although the repo is still active. Strudel's GitHub repo is archived. The @strudel/* npm packages are at 1.3.0, last published 2026-01-18. The published superdough dist embeds its AudioWorklets as `data:` URLs, so it works with any bundler. Strudel's source on Codeberg instead uses a Vite-only `./worklets.mjs?audioworklet` import.

Recommended stack:
- **Pitch detection:** pitchy 4.1.0 (McLeod method, MIT, pure ESM, only dependency fft.js), running inside an AudioWorklet. Turn off the browser's mic processing (echo cancellation, noise suppression, auto gain). Use a clarity threshold, a median filter and octave-tolerant grading.
- **Staff notation:** generate it from an internal TypeScript model. Strudel haps carry exact fraction.js times, and tonal 6.5.1 can spell notes in the right key. Render that model as ABC text with abcjs 6.7.2 (MIT, 512KB min). abcjs handles chord symbols, ties, beaming by adjacency, grand staff and line wrapping. It also supports click listeners, dragging notes to change pitch, `foregroundColor` and `TimingCallbacks`. Use VexFlow 5 only for custom micro-widgets. OSMD 2.3.0 needs MusicXML input. Verovio 6.4.1 has the best engraving and a time map, but it is 7.4MB and LGPL; load it lazily if ever needed.
- **Transcription:** wavesurfer.js 8 with its regions, spectrogram and timeline plugins, used only for display. Playback goes through signalsmith-stretch 1.3.2 (MIT, one 114KB file with inlined WASM and worklet). It provides `rate`, `semitones` and `loopStart`/`loopEnd` for A-B loops directly. `wavesurfer.setPlaybackRate(rate, true)`, which uses preservesPitch, is a simple fallback. Essentia.js (AGPL; npm release is from 2022) is optional for key, chord and chroma hints.
- **Spaced repetition and storage:** ts-fsrs 6 wrapped in our own module; Dexie 4.4.7 with useLiveQuery and dexie-export-import for backups.

On tooling, Bun 1.4.4's own bundler cannot yet bundle `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` workers or worklets (oven-sh/bun#18601 is still open). It also has no plugin layer compatible with Vite/Rollup. bun-plugin-tailwind ships its own copy of Tailwind 4.1.14, while the latest Tailwind is 4.3.5. There is no first-party React Compiler or MDX plugin for Bun. My recommendation is Vite 8 run on the Bun runtime (`bunx --bun vite`) for the frontend: React 19.3 with React Compiler, TanStack Router, Tailwind via @tailwindcss/vite, MDX via @mdx-js/rollup. Load our own worklets with `?worker&url`. Bun.serve runs the local Claude tutor API, with the Vite dev server proxying `/api` to it. For tests: bun test for pure logic, Vitest 5 browser mode for code that needs audio, and Playwright 1.65 with Chromium's fake-microphone WAV flags for end-to-end singing tests.

findings.topic: Pitch detection architecture for singing (AnalyserNode vs AudioWorklet)
findings.detail:
**AnalyserNode** (`getFloatTimeDomainData` polled from requestAnimationFrame) is simple. But it samples about every 16.7ms, frames are not gapless and they depend on the display. It is fine for a tuner needle but weak for grading note onsets.

**AudioWorklet** (recommended): accumulate 128-frame render quanta in a ring buffer and run MPM every hop. Suggested window is 2048 samples at 48kHz (42.7ms), which covers about 2 periods of E2 (82Hz). Suggested hop is 512 samples (about 94 estimates/s). Post `{t: currentTime, hz, clarity, rms}` back through `port.postMessage`. SharedArrayBuffer would require COOP/COEP cross-origin isolation; it is not needed at this message rate.

Turn off the browser's voice processing with `getUserMedia({audio:{echoCancellation:false, noiseSuppression:false, autoGainControl:false}})`. Headphones are needed so Strudel playback does not bleed into the mic.

Voice-specific handling:
- Treat a frame as voiced only when clarity is at least about 0.9.
- Apply a median-of-5 filter and hysteresis before committing a note change.
- Correct octave errors with a continuity prior (prefer the octave nearest the previous note).
- Grade by pitch class and cents with octave folding, so a learner can sing in their own octave.
- When grading timing against Strudel's scheduled haps, compensate with `AudioContext.outputLatency`/`baseLatency` plus input latency.
findings.evidence: MDN AudioWorklet / AnalyserNode / MediaTrackConstraints; pitchy docs (clarityThreshold)

findings.detail:
vexflow@5.0.0, MIT, released 2025-03-05 and still the latest tag. Repo pushed 2026-10-29, 42 open issues.

Entry points:
- `vexflow`: all fonts (Bravura, Academico, Gonville, Petaluma, Petaluma Script), CJS min 1.13MB.
- `vexflow/bravura`: 728KB.
- `vexflow/core`: 337KB, no fonts; load them yourself.

Useful APIs: `Accidental.applyAccidentals(voices, keySignature)` decides which accidentals to show given the key, `Beam.generateBeams(notes, config)`, `Beam.applyAndGetBeams(voice, stemDirection, groups)`, `Element.setStyle({fillStyle, strokeStyle})`, `addClass`, `getSVGElement()` and `setAttribute`. It also has StaveTie, Tuplet, ChordSymbol, KeySignature, StaveConnector (brace, for grand staff) and the Formatter.

What it does not do: quantize, split measures, insert ties across beats or barlines, or lay out multiple lines. The app must build all of that. Highlighting and selection are straightforward by toggling classes on the SVG element of each note.

abcjs@6.7.2, MIT, published 2026-10-16, 2.4k stars. dist/abcjs-basic-min.js is 512KB.

`renderAbc(target, abc, params): TuneObjectArray`. Params include `add_classes`, `clickListener(abcElem, tuneNumber, classes, analysis, drag)`, `dragging` (drag a note to change its pitch, useful for transcription input), `selectTypes`, `selectionColor`, `foregroundColor` (dark mode), `responsive`, `jazzchords`, `visualTranspose`, `oneSvgPerLine` and `wrap`.

`TimingCallbacks(visualObj, options)` provides start, pause, setProgress, currentMillisecond and noteTimings. `synth.getMidiFile`, `CreateSynth` and `SynthController` exist, but Oak would play through Strudel instead.

ABC notation itself covers key signatures (K:), meter, chord symbols ("Am7"), ties (-), tuplets ((3), beaming by writing notes adjacent, and multi-staff/grand staff (%%score). Line layout is automatic. The generator must still split durations across barlines and choose spellings and accidentals per bar.

opensheetmusicdisplay@2.3.0, BSD-3, published 2026-11-07 (repo pushed 2026-11-10). build/opensheetmusicdisplay.min.js is 1.46MB, built on VexFlow. Input is MusicXML only, which is verbose to generate from code.

OSMDOptions include `darkMode` (sets defaultColorMusic and PageBackgroundColor), `defaultColorMusic`, `pageBackgroundColor`, `autoBeam`/`autoBeamOptions`, `followCursor`, `cursorsOptions`, `drawingParameters`, `renderSingleHorizontalStaffline` and `newSystemFromXML`. There is a built-in cursor API. Skyline calculation has been geometric by default since 2.0.

verovio@6.4.1, LGPL-3.0-only, published 2026-11-03.

Exports:
- `verovio/wasm`: dist/verovio-module.mjs, 7.4MB.
- `verovio/wasm-hum`: 13MB, adds Humdrum.
- `verovio/esm`: the VerovioToolkit.

It reads MEI, MusicXML, Humdrum, ABC and PAE. Engraving and automatic layout are the best of the four, and getElementsAtTime makes it easy to highlight the playing note. The cost is bundle weight.

Usage: `Bun.serve({ routes: { '/': indexHtml, '/api/x': { GET, POST } }, development: { hmr: true, console: true } })`. HTML imports are scanned with HTMLRewriter and bundled with Bun's JS/CSS bundler. It supports a Vite-compatible `import.meta.hot` API and React Fast Refresh.

- Bundler plugins can only be configured in bunfig.toml under `[serve.static] plugins = [...]`.
- bun-plugin-tailwind 0.1.2 (maintained by the Bun team, 27MB, no dependencies) contains its own bundled copy of Tailwind 4.1.14, while the latest is 4.3.5.
- React Compiler needs the third-party bun-plugin-react-compiler 0.3.9.

- CSS Modules with HTMLBundle: issue #18258 is still open.
- The request for a Vite/Rollup plugin compatibility layer (#39976) was closed as a duplicate; it is not implemented.

findings.detail:
oven-sh/bun#18601 ('support bundling workers in bun build and dev server') is open, last updated 2026-09-22. In the issue's words, `new URL(constant string, import.meta.url)` "does not lower to anything special". Neither `new Worker(new URL(...))` nor `import.meta.resolve` creates a chunk, so worker and worklet entry files are not bundled or emitted.

In the dev server, `import.meta.url` would point at the bundled chunk, so a relative worklet URL would likely return 404 (inferred).

The `type: 'file'` import attribute copies a file as-is and returns its path, without transpiling it. Workarounds:
- a separate `Bun.build({entrypoints:['src/audio/pitch.worklet.ts'], target:'browser', format:'esm'})` served from a route;
- inlining the source as a string and loading it through a Blob URL.

Vite only treats `new URL()` as a worker when it appears directly inside `new Worker(...)`. Anywhere else it is a static asset: copied and hashed, not bundled or transpiled. Known pitfalls:
- `new URL('./x.ts', import.meta.url)` passed to anything other than `new Worker` gets inlined as `data:video/mp2t`, because .ts is also a video extension (vitejs/vite#11823, open).
- `?url` does not bundle the file's imports (#6757, open).
- Paint worklets imported as `.ts?url` break in production builds (#6979, open).

The right pattern for our own TypeScript worklets: `import pitchWorkletUrl from './pitch.worklet.ts?worker&url'; await ctx.audioWorklet.addModule(pitchWorkletUrl)`. This form is documented in features.md. Set `worker.format: 'es'`.

Dependencies that use `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` used to break under optimizeDeps (#8427). That was fixed by PR #21434 (closed 2026-02-10) in the Rolldown-based optimizer. The fallback is `optimizeDeps.exclude`.

@vitejs/plugin-react 6 offers React Compiler two ways:
- Rust: `react({ compiler: true })` using oxc-transform-react@0.158.0 as an optional peer. It is marked experimental and accepts options such as compilationMode and logDiagnostics.
- Babel: `plugins: [react(), babel({ presets: [reactCompilerPreset()] })]` with @rolldown/plugin-babel@0.3.1, @babel/core and babel-plugin-react-compiler@1.0.0.

MDX with fast refresh: `[{ enforce: 'pre', ...mdx() }, react({ include: /\.(mdx|js|jsx|ts|tsx)$/ })]`.

bun test: fast and Jest-like, good for pure logic (theory engine, quantizer and speller, FSRS wrapper, MPM on synthetic sine and voice buffers). It does not apply Vite transforms (`?worker&url`, MDX). There are some vi.* compatibility gaps: oven-sh/bun#47657 (vi.clearAllTimers) and #46549 (Vitest import mapping), both open. For a DOM it uses @happy-dom/global-registrator 21.0.4, which has no AudioContext.

Vitest 5.1.0 browser mode with @vitest/browser-playwright runs in a real Chromium, so AudioContext and worklets work.

Playwright 1.65.0 for end-to-end tests: grant `permissions: ['microphone']` and launch Chromium with `--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream --use-fake-device-for-media-stream --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture=<sung.wav> --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`. That makes singing exercises testable deterministically.
