risks: ts-fsrs 6.0.0 is 13 days old and has a new async API (`DefaultScheduler`) with FSRS-7 as the default. The legacy createEmptyCard/fsrs()/repeat/next calls are deprecated. Pin the exact version and wrap it behind Oak's own SRS interface. Card JSON stored now (FSRS-7 adds stabilityFast) would need migration if we change model version later.
VexFlow's only stable release in 20 months is 5.0.0 (March 2025), even though the repo is active. It has no auto measure-splitting, ties or line layout, so we would build those.

Bun's bundler cannot chunk `new URL()`/`new Worker()`/AudioWorklet entries (#18601 open). It has no Vite/Rollup plugin compatibility layer. bun-plugin-tailwind bundles its own Tailwind 4.1.14, behind the latest 4.3.5. React Compiler and MDX have only third-party or alpha Bun plugins. Going Bun-only means extra custom build steps.
Vite worklet pitfalls: `new URL('./x.ts')` outside `new Worker` gets inlined as data:video/mp2t (#11823), and `?url` does not bundle imports (#6757). Always use `?worker&url` for our own worklets.

Strudel from Codeberg source uses Vite-only `?audioworklet` imports. The npm dist (1.3.0, January 2026) is bundler-agnostic but may lag Codeberg main. Strudel is AGPL-3.0-or-later, so the whole app becomes AGPL if ever distributed.

Licenses: Essentia.js is AGPL-3.0, pitchfinder GPL-3 and aubio GPL-3. rubberband-wasm is listed as 'GPLv2'; if that means GPLv2-only, it is incompatible with Strudel's AGPL-3. Verovio is LGPL-3. None of this matters for personal local use, but it would if the app is shared.

Voice pitch detection risks: octave errors with MPM/YIN on breathy or low voices; browser voice processing (AGC, noise suppression) distorting the signal unless disabled; Bluetooth headphones adding roughly 150–300ms of output latency, which skews timing grades (inferred). ML detectors (SwiftF0/CREPE) have no maintained JS wrapper, and SwiftF0's figures are self-reported.
Essentia.js has had no npm release since 2022 (0.1.3). Its WASM payload is about 2MB, so only lazy-load it for optional key/chord hints.

There are several brand-new majors: Vite 8 (Rolldown), Vitest 5, Jotai 3, TypeScript 7 (native). Tools that rely on the TypeScript JS compiler API may need TypeScript 6 installed alongside (inferred). Solid 2 is still RC, so avoid it.
recommendations: Frontend build: run Vite 8.3 with `bunx --bun vite`, using @vitejs/plugin-react 6 with React Compiler. Prefer the Babel path, `babel({presets:[reactCompilerPreset()]})`; the oxc path is experimental. Add @tanstack/router-plugin/vite, @tailwindcss/vite 4.3 and @mdx-js/rollup (enforce 'pre'). Run Bun.serve as a separate local API process for the Claude tutor, with Vite `server.proxy['/api']` pointing to it. For production, serve the built dist/ from the same Bun.serve.

UI stack: React 19.3 + TanStack Router 1.170. Zustand 5 for ephemeral UI and session state. XState 5 for the exercise and lesson flow state machines (prompt → attempt → grade → feedback → SRS update). Dexie liveQuery/useLiveQuery for everything persisted. Lazy-mount CodeMirror/StrudelMirror editors offscreen with IntersectionObserver. Framework choice matters little for CodeMirror 6, which is imperative and mounts via a ref.

Pitch: write `pitch.worklet.ts`, which accumulates a ring buffer, runs pitchy's `PitchDetector.forFloat32Array(2048)` every 512-sample hop and posts {time, hz, clarity, rms}. Load it via `?worker&url`. Call getUserMedia with echoCancellation, noiseSuppression and autoGainControl all false. Smooth with clarity ≥0.9, a median-of-5 filter and note-change hysteresis. Grade in cents with optional octave folding. Keep a detector interface so SwiftF0 (onnxruntime-web) can be swapped in later if accuracy falls short.

Notation: build a pure-TypeScript NotationModel from Strudel haps (exact Fractions from queryArc) covering bar splitting, ties, beam groups by meter and key-aware spelling via tonal 6.5. Render it to ABC with abcjs 6.7: lead sheets, chord symbols, grand staff, automatic wrap, `add_classes` and `clickListener` to map SVG elements back to the model, `dragging` for transcription answers, and `foregroundColor` for dark mode. Drive the playing-note highlight from Strudel's own scheduler callbacks, not abcjs synth. Keep VexFlow 5 for a few bespoke widgets. Lazy-load Verovio only if engraving quality becomes a priority.

Transcription workbench: decode the file with `AudioContext.decodeAudioData`. Feed the channels to signalsmith-stretch with `addBuffers`, and drive rate (0.25–1.0), semitones and loopStart/loopEnd from the UI. Use wavesurfer 8 for display only: pass `peaks` + duration or the decoded buffer, sync the cursor from `stretch.inputTime`, use the Regions plugin for A-B loops, and use Spectrogram (scale logarithmic) plus Timeline/Zoom. Keep `wavesurfer.setPlaybackRate(rate, true)` as the fallback. Lazy-load Essentia.js (KeyExtractor, HPCP/Chromagram, ChordsDetection) only as an opt-in hint.

SRS: in `srs.ts`, call `await DefaultScheduler({version:'FSRS-7', desiredRetention:0.9, enableFuzz:true, learningSteps:['1m','10m'], relearningSteps:['10m']})`. Persist the `review()` card and revlog as plain JSON in Dexie, and store `scheduler.definition.model.name` with each card so a future model migration is possible. Pin ts-fsrs to exactly 6.0.0.

Persistence: Dexie 4.4 schema with versioned `.upgrade()` migrations. Call `navigator.storage.persist()` on first run. Provide a backup/restore screen using dexie-export-import: `exportDB(db, {prettyJson:true})` and `importInto(db, blob, {clearTablesBeforeImport:true, acceptVersionDiff:true})`. Store imported audio as Blobs in their own table, skipped from backups with `skipTables` unless the user opts in.

Testing: bun test for pure logic (fastest). Vitest 5 browser mode (@vitest/browser-playwright) for worklet and AudioContext units. Playwright 1.65 end-to-end tests with Chromium's fake-mic flags feeding recorded or synthesized WAVs to test singing exercises deterministically.

Use the published npm @strudel/* 1.3.0 dist (bundler-agnostic worklets) unless a feature that exists only on Codeberg main is needed. If it is, Vite plus vite-plugin-bundle-audioworklet is required. This is another reason to choose Vite over a Bun-only build.
openQuestions: Target browsers: is a Chromium-only experience acceptable, or must Safari and Firefox be supported for mic, worklets and the File System Access API?
Will Oak ever be shared or hosted publicly? This decides whether AGPL (Strudel, Essentia) and GPL components matter.
Headphone type: Bluetooth latency affects rhythm and singing grading. Should there be a latency calibration step (clap or sing-along test)?

Lesson content format: typed TypeScript lesson objects (type-safe, testable) versus MDX prose with embedded components? Or a hybrid where MDX holds prose and TypeScript holds exercises and validators?
Should Oak consume Strudel from npm 1.3.0 (January 2026) or track Codeberg main? The latter forces Vite plus vite-plugin-bundle-audioworklet.
Notation engraving bar: is abcjs's quality acceptable for transcription answer keys, or should Verovio (7.4MB, best engraving) be lazy-loaded for long scores?
Should pitch grading be octave-agnostic by default (sing in your own range) or require the exact octave once the learner has studied registers?

result.critique:
The five reports cover the Strudel APIs well. The editor and repl surface, headless evaluation and hap shapes, the onDraw/onPaint hooks, sample self-hosting entry points, audio-context sharing, pitchy, abcjs/VexFlow/Verovio and ts-fsrs 6 are all verified in source. Most of the curriculum material is labelled 'inferred' because it is design synthesis, which is acceptable. Five gaps or conflicts would still block a concrete implementation plan.

(1) MISSING ENTIRELY: the Claude tutor server. The design calls the tutor 'central', but no report covers the Anthropic SDK, model IDs, streaming relay from Bun.serve, prompt caching, tool use or structured outputs. Two quick npm checks for this critique: @anthropic-ai/sdk latest is 1.8.0 (a major version beyond the familiar 0.x line; modified 2026-11-10) and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk is 0.3.322. Neither has been researched.

(2) UNRESOLVED BUILD/TEST TOOLCHAIN. The reports disagree on how to build:
- strudel-embed says Bun.build 'should work' with a NODE_ENV shim.
- browser-tech recommends Vite 8 on Bun and notes Bun cannot bundle worklets (#18601).
- strudel-headless calls the @kabelsalat/web IIFE link failure under the Bun runtime a BLOCKER, but marks it only 'inferred'.

Checked for this critique:
- Bun's docs/runtime/module-resolution.mdx line 238 says 'At runtime Bun prefers "main" … and uses "module" otherwise'. That makes failures in bun test and in server-side @strudel/core imports very likely (documented).
- @strudel/core@1.2.6 does ship dist/assets/clockworker-ZDiUtESR.js, so the `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` asset exists.

Still not verified:
- Bun.build's main-field order and NODE_ENV defaults for target 'browser' and for HTML imports.
- In Vite 8.3.7 (Rolldown): mainFields, whether optimizeDeps defines process.env.NODE_ENV in dev, CJS interop for chord-voicings, and how new URL is handled inside node_modules.
- Whether Vitest 5 in node mode externalizes @strudel/core, which would reproduce issue #1921.
- Whether pinning 1.2.5 is a viable fallback.
This decides where the grader can run (browser worker vs Bun server vs tests) and is the precondition for Claude tool use that evaluates Strudel code server-side.

(3) The notation and theory engine is inferred. Two reports lean on 'tonal 6.5.1' (I confirmed it exists, modified 2026-10-14) for spelling, Roman numerals and answer keys, but nobody verified its API. The hap→ABC conversion (ties, tuplets, %%score grand staff, iReal-to-lead-sheet chord symbols, key/mode K: lines) and the mapping back from abcjs elements (startChar/endChar, add_classes) to Strudel hap.context.locations are assumed, not checked. Staff notation is a core teaching pillar and the transcription-answer UI.

(4) Smaller items that can be settled during implementation:
- The React 19 StrictMode hazards around StrudelMirror (inferred; the mitigation is clear).
- The instrument palette needs a listening pass.
- Latency calibration for tap and sing grading. outputLatency/getOutputTimestamp support is unverified, but a calibration UX is a design choice either way.
- The doc.json function catalog is inlined in the @strudel/codemirror dist and could be extracted at build time for the toolbox and the Claude context.
- Minor inconsistencies: the @strudel/web dist is reported as 409 KB vs 850 KB, and enableFuzz is true in one report and false in another.

followUps.summary:
Main result: one bug decides almost the whole matrix, the resolution of @kabelsalat/web. That package has type:module, main=dist/index.js (an IIFE that starts with `var kabelsalat=function(l){...}({})` and exports nothing) and module=dist/index.mjs. Every bundler that targets the browser picks `module`, so all browser rows pass: Vite 8.3.7 dev and build, Bun.build target browser, Bun HTML imports, and Vitest browser mode. Every place that runs node_modules natively picks `main`, so these rows fail at import time with "does not provide an export named 'SalatRepl'": Bun runtime (bun test, a Bun.serve grader), Node (Vitest node externalization) and Vite SSR externalization. In Bun 1.4.4 this is in the source: the runtime sets `resolver.prefer_module_field = false` (src/runtime/jsc_hooks.rs), so `main` wins over `module`. Bun.build and the dev server keep the default `true`, so `module` wins there. Upstream fixed it on Codeberg in PR #1932 ("move kabelsalat web to superdough", merged 2026-01-18 22:27 +01:00). That was after the last npm publish (2026-01-18 03:14Z), so no npm release has the fix. The smallest fix that works everywhere is one line in `bun patch @kabelsalat/web`: "main": "dist/index.mjs".

Other columns:
- **process.env.NODE_ENV:** replaced automatically by all four browser pipelines. Vite does it in the Rolldown optimizer define, clientInjections in dev and the define plugin in build. Bun does it through `defines_from_transform_options` (from the NODE_ENV env var, otherwise "development"). The HTML-import paths force development, or "production" when development:false. The node/Bun runtime rows already have `process`, so nothing is needed there.
- **Clockworker `new URL`:** handled correctly by Vite in both dev and build. The optimizer rewrites the URL relative to .vite/deps, and the build plugin assetImportMetaUrl emits the file as an asset. The outer `new SharedWorker(new URL("" + ...))` does not match Vite's worker regex, so it passes through with no warning. Bun.build passes it through silently without copying the asset, so it would 404, but only when sync:true. In Node and Bun it never runs, because SharedWorker is undefined.
- **chord-voicings:** works everywhere. It is CJS with `exports.__esModule=true; exports["default"]={...}`, and @strudel/tonal defensively does `_voicings.default || _voicings`.
- **Own TypeScript AudioWorklet:** works in Vite via `?worker&url` (the type is declared in vite/client.d.ts). It does not work in Bun's bundler (oven-sh/bun#18601 is still open). Work around it with a separate Bun.build entrypoint or a Bun.serve route that builds the worklet.

Recommended toolchain:
- **Patch:** bun patch the kabelsalat `main` field.
- **Frontend:** Vite 8.3.7 for dev and build, running on Node 26 through `bun run` scripts.
- **Server:** Bun.serve for the AI-tutor API, the headless grader, and serving dist/ in production.
- **Tests:** `bun test` for curriculum logic, the grader and pure-TS DSP. Optionally Vitest 5.1 browser mode (Playwright Chromium) for Web Audio, CodeMirror and worklet integration.

Pinning @strudel/core 1.2.5 only works as a whole matching 1.2.5-era set: core/mini/tonal/transpiler/draw@1.2.5 plus superdough/webaudio/codemirror/soundfonts@1.2.6, all published 2025-10-27, all pinning core 1.2.5 exactly. Mixing it with the 1.3.0 packages installs two copies of core. The set is usable, but it loses features that 1.2.6 added.

assetImportMetaUrlRE = /\bnew\s+URL\s*\(\s*('[^']+'|"[^"]+"|`[^`]+`)\s*,\s*import\.meta\.url\s*(?:,\s*)?\)/dg. It only applies when consumer==='client', and it also transforms node_modules files. If the file exists, fileToUrl emits it as an asset; if not, it logs warnOnce("... doesn't exist at build time ...").

followUps.summary:
For Oak, use the plain Messages API through @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.8.0 (published 2026-11-10), not the Claude Agent SDK. The SDK README lists Bun 1.0 or later as a supported runtime. `new Anthropic()` reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and Bun loads .env files automatically, so the key never needs to be in code. SDK 1.0.0 (2026-10-21; the last 0.x was 0.137.0) moved every request to API version 2026-10-21. That version has four main breaking changes: temperature, top_p and top_k now return a 400; `MessageParam` became a union of user, assistant and system message types; the key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; and a client may hold only one credential. To stream to the browser, call `client.messages.stream(params, {signal})`, return either `stream.toReadableStream()` (newline-delimited JSON that the browser reads with `MessageStream.fromReadableStream`) or app-level SSE from an async-generator Response, and call `server.timeout(req, 0)`. Without that call, Bun's default 10-second idleTimeout closes the connection during thinking pauses.

Models (official overview, 2026-11-10): claude-opus-5-5 costs $4/$20 per million tokens (MTok) with a 1M context window and 128K max output. Thinking is always on and default effort is medium. Forced tool_choice `any` or `tool` returns a 400. claude-sonnet-5-5 costs $2/$10. claude-haiku-5-5 costs $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens and $0.50/$2.50 above that. claude-fable-5-2 costs $8/$40. Recommendations: claude-opus-5-5 for tutoring dialogue (the docs call it the default starting model), and claude-haiku-5-5 at effort `low` with structured outputs for high-volume feedback. The prompt-cache minimum is 512 tokens on all of these models. Cache writes cost 1.25x base input for the 5-minute TTL and 2x for the 1-hour TTL. Cache reads cost 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and 0.1x on Haiku 5.5. Render order is tools, then system, then messages. A static prefix of roughly 30–50K tokens (syllabus, a 300-function catalog and the persona) should end in an explicit breakpoint with `ttl:"1h"`, with a top-level automatic 5-minute `cache_control` for the conversation tail. A 1-hour entry before a 5-minute entry is allowed; the reverse is not. Each model has its own cache, so the Opus and Haiku routes cache the prefix separately. Changing `output_config.format` also invalidates the cache, so keep one fixed schema per route.

Tool use: tools are JSON-Schema objects with `strict: true` (all objects need `additionalProperties: false`), `tool_choice` takes auto, any, tool or none and has `disable_parallel_tool_use`, and all parallel `tool_result` blocks go back in one user message. On Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, use `tool_choice: {type:"auto"}` plus `strict: true`, and use `output_config.format` (SDK helper `zodOutputFormat` with `client.messages.parse` → `parsed_output`) for exercise variants and machine-readable feedback. Strict schemas cannot use minimum, maximum or minLength. Other limits: 20 strict tools, 24 optional parameters and 16 union-typed parameters per request.

The Agent SDK (0.3.322) wraps a native Claude Code binary that runs as a subprocess per session (an idle pre-warmed spare holds about 230–260 MB). Its in-process tools use `tool()` and `createSdkMcpServer()`, and its `executable` option accepts 'bun'. Anthropic's docs say third-party developers may not offer claude.ai login or subscription rate limits in their products, and should authenticate with an API key instead. Given that, the subprocess overhead and the loss of caching control, the Agent SDK is the wrong fit for Oak.

findings.detail: @anthropic-ai/sdk latest is 1.8.0 (2026-11-10). 1.0.0 shipped 2026-10-21 and the last 0.x was 0.137.0. The 1.0.0 changelog's only BREAKING entry is 'add support for new API version 2026-10-21'. Effects for TypeScript: (1) requests send anthropic-version 2026-10-21, so `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` return a 400 even at their defaults (the fields are also gone from the types), a `document` block directly in an assistant message returns a 400, and a user `text` block with non-empty `citations` returns a 400; (2) `MessageParam` is now `UserMessageParam | AssistantMessageParam | SystemMessageParam` (the same split applies to the Beta types), so `interface X extends MessageParam` must become `type X = MessageParam & {...}`, and `BetaMessageParam.content` can be undefined; (3) the tool runner's `compactionControl` option is removed (use `betas:["compact-2026-01-12"]` and `context_management.edits:[{type:"compact_20260112", trigger:{type:"input_tokens", value}}]`); (4) Text Completions is removed; (5) `betas` is removed from `client.models.*` (use `client.beta.models.*`); (6) the API key is sent as `Authorization: Bearer` instead of X-Api-Key; (7) a client holds exactly one credential: passing two of apiKey/authToken/credentials/config/profile throws a TypeError; (8) the license is now Apache-2.0. 1.5.0 added error classes per HTTP status and API error code, plus `apiMessage`, `errorCode` and `details` on APIError. 1.7.0 added the claude-fable-5-2 and claude-mythos-5-2 model IDs.

The README's Requirements section lists Node.js 20 LTS+, Deno 1.28+, Bun 1.0 or later, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge and Nitro, and requires TypeScript 5.0 or later. Browsers are blocked unless `dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true` is set. package.json for 1.8.0 has no `engines` field. Dependencies are @opentelemetry/api, standardwebhooks and json-schema-to-ts, with zod as an optional peer dependency (^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0). The package is dual CJS/ESM, and `./lib/*` subpaths are exported (for example @anthropic-ai/sdk/lib/MessageStream).

findings.topic: Client construction, API key env var, .env loading
findings.detail: `import Anthropic from "@anthropic-ai/sdk"; const client = new Anthropic({ maxRetries?, timeout?, logLevel?, baseURL?, defaultHeaders?, fetchOptions? })`. With no credential passed, the client tries these in order: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, the profile ANTHROPIC_PROFILE names, Workload Identity Federation env vars, then the active profile on disk from `ant auth login`. It logs a warning if both of the first two are set. The base URL comes from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Default timeout is 600000 ms and default maxRetries is 2. Bun loads .env, .env.{NODE_ENV}, .env.local and .env.{NODE_ENV}.local automatically, so ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local works with a zero-argument `new Anthropic()` under `bun run`. The Agent SDK, by contrast, does not load .env itself.

From @anthropic-ai/sdk@1.8.0/resources/messages/messages.d.ts: `create(params: MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming, options?: RequestOptions): APIPromise<Message>` and `create(params: MessageCreateParamsStreaming, options?): APIPromise<Stream<RawMessageStreamEvent>>`, which is low-memory and does not accumulate a message. `stream<Params extends MessageStreamParams>(body: Params, options?: RequestOptions): MessageStream<...>` is the accumulating helper. `parse<Params extends MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming>(params, options?): APIPromise<ParsedMessage<...>>` returns `.parsed_output`. `countTokens(params: MessageCountTokensParams, options?): APIPromise<MessageTokensCount>` returns `{ input_tokens }`. RequestOptions include `signal`, `timeout`, `maxRetries` and `headers`. Every APIPromise supports `.withResponse()`, which returns `{data, response, request_id}`, and `.asResponse()`. Responses carry `_request_id`.

findings.topic: Stream event types and MessageStream helpers
findings.detail: Raw SSE events are message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta, content_block_stop, message_delta (carries stop_reason and usage) and message_stop, plus `ping` and in-stream `error` events (for example overloaded_error). Delta types are text_delta, input_json_delta (partial_json), thinking_delta, signature_delta and citations_delta. Code must ignore unknown event types. MessageStream supports `.on(event, cb)` for connect, streamEvent(event, snapshot), text(delta, snapshot), citation, inputJson(partialJson, jsonSnapshot), thinking(delta, snapshot), signature, message, contentBlock, finalMessage, error, abort(APIUserAbortError) and end. Methods and properties: `finalMessage()`, `finalText()`, `done()`, `abort()`, `currentMessage`, `controller` (AbortController), `ended`, `errored`, `aborted`, `request_id`, `withResponse()`, `toReadableStream()` and `static fromReadableStream(stream)`. Thinking display is 'omitted' by default on Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5: thinking blocks stream with empty text, so a reply can open with a silent pause. Set `thinking:{type:"adaptive", display:"summarized"}` to stream summaries instead.

findings.topic: Relaying a stream from Bun.serve and handling aborts
findings.detail:
Option A (SDK-native): `const s = client.messages.stream(params, { signal: req.signal }); return new Response(s.toReadableStream(), {headers:{'Content-Type':'application/x-ndjson'}})`. `toReadableStream()` writes each event as `JSON.stringify(event)+'
'`. Its cancel() calls `iter.return()`, which calls `MessageStream.abort()`, so the upstream request is cancelled when Bun cancels the body on client disconnect. In the browser, `MessageStream.fromReadableStream(res.body)` from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/lib/MessageStream' gives the same `.on('text')` and `finalMessage()` API. Option B (better for a tool loop): return `new Response(async function* () { try { ... yield `event: text
data: ${JSON.stringify(d)}

` } finally { stream.abort() } }, {headers:{'Content-Type':'text/event-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache'}})`. Bun runs the generator's finally block on disconnect, and calls ReadableStream.cancel() on disconnect. Bun.serve closes connections that are idle for 10 s by default (idleTimeout maximum 255; 0 disables it). Call `server.timeout(req, 0)` on SSE routes or emit heartbeat comments. EventSource only does GET, so a POST body needs fetch() plus a reader on the client. Passing the `signal` option to `stream()` is wired to the stream's internal controller.

findings.topic: Current model IDs, limits and pricing
findings.detail: From the models overview and pricing pages, as of 2026-11-10. Columns: input / output / 5m cache write / 1h cache write / cache read, all per MTok. claude-fable-5-2: $8 / $40 / $10 / $16 / $0.20; 1M context, 128K output, default effort high, thinking always on. claude-opus-5-5: $4 / $20 / $5 / $8 / $0.20; 1M context, 128K output, thinking always on (disabled and budget_tokens both 400), default effort medium. claude-sonnet-5-5: $2 / $10 / $2.50 / $4 / $0.10; 1M context, 128K output, default effort high. claude-haiku-5-5: $0.10 / $0.50 / $0.125 / $0.20 / $0.01 for prompts up to 100K tokens, and $0.50 / $2.50 / $0.625 / $1 / $0.05 above 100K; 1M context, 128K output, default effort medium. Batch API is 50% off. All four share a June 2026 knowledge cutoff. The Claude 4.7+ tokenizer produces about 30% more tokens than older models. Live limits are available from `client.models.retrieve(id)`, which returns `max_input_tokens`, `max_tokens` and `capabilities`.

findings.topic: Model-specific API constraints relevant to Oak
findings.detail: Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 return a 400 for `tool_choice` {type:'any'} or {type:'tool'}. Use 'auto' with `strict:true` and a prompt that names the tool, or use output_config.format. Haiku 5.5 accepts a forced tool_choice, but the forced call then skips thinking. Prefill returns a 400 on all current models. Effort is set with `output_config:{effort:'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'|'max'}`. Changing thinking or effort between requests invalidates the messages cache, so pin them per route. Preserved thinking: pass thinking blocks back unchanged and keep history append-only. Editing earlier turns invalidates replayed thinking, and the skill reference says accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 are enforced on this check. A mid-conversation `{role:'system', content}` message, with no beta header, is supported on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 and injects per-turn context without breaking the cached prefix.
findings.evidence: claude-api skill (bundled 2.1.321) shared/model-migration.md + SKILL.md; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors.md (Forced tool use not supported / Thinking cannot be disabled sections)

findings.detail: The block-level form is `cache_control: {type:'ephemeral'}` (5-minute default) or `{type:'ephemeral', ttl:'1h'}`; the type is `CacheControlEphemeral { ttl?: '5m'|'1h' }`. It can go on tool definitions, system text blocks and message content blocks. Top-level `cache_control` on the request enables automatic caching: the breakpoint goes on the last cacheable block, moves forward as the conversation grows, and uses one of the 4 breakpoint slots. The prefix is matched in order tools → system → messages. A write happens only at a breakpoint. Reads look back at most 20 blocks, with consecutive tool_use runs and tool_result runs each counting as one position. A 1h entry must appear before any 5m entry. Automatic caching returns a 400 if the last block has an explicit marker with a different TTL or if 4 explicit markers already exist. The minimum cacheable length is 512 tokens on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.2 (1,024 on Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5; 4,096 on Haiku 4.5); a shorter prefix silently is not cached. Writes cost 1.25x base input (5m) or 2x (1h). Reads cost 0.1x, except 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 and 0.025x on Fable 5.2. A read refreshes the TTL at no extra cost. A cache entry becomes readable only once the first response starts streaming. Pre-warm with `max_tokens: 0`; that is rejected together with stream:true or output_config.format. Check `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`, `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` and `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`. Changing output_config.format invalidates the prompt cache.

findings.topic: Caching applied to Oak's static prefix (cost estimate)
findings.detail: Assume the prefix (persona, syllabus and a 300-function Strudel catalog) is about 40K tokens; measure the real size with `client.messages.countTokens`. Opus 5.5 per request: $0.16 uncached, $0.20 for a 5m write, $0.32 for a 1h write, $0.008 for a read. Sonnet 5.5: $0.08 / $0.10 / $0.16 / $0.004. Haiku 5.5, which stays in the ≤100K price tier: $0.004 / $0.005 / $0.008 / $0.0004. A 20-minute daily session with about 15 Opus tutor turns costs roughly $0.32 for the 1h write plus 14 × $0.008 in reads, about $0.43 per day for the prefix, plus output at $20/MTok. Gaps between tutor calls can exceed 5 minutes (the learner is composing), so the 1h TTL on the static prefix fits. An alternative is the 5m TTL plus a `max_tokens:0` keep-alive every ~4.5 minutes, which is cheap because Opus 5.5 reads cost 0.05x.

findings.topic: Tool definition schema and tool_choice (SDK 1.8.0 types)
findings.detail: `interface Tool { name: string; input_schema: { type:'object'; properties?; required?; [k:string]:unknown }; description?: string; strict?: boolean; eager_input_streaming?: boolean|null; cache_control?: CacheControlEphemeral|null; defer_loading?: boolean; input_examples?: object[]; allowed_callers?: (...)[]; type?: 'custom'|null }`. `ToolChoice = {type:'auto', disable_parallel_tool_use?} | {type:'any', disable_parallel_tool_use?} | {type:'tool', name, disable_parallel_tool_use?} | {type:'none'}`. With `disable_parallel_tool_use:true` and auto, the model makes at most one tool call per turn. Parallel calls are on by default: run them concurrently and return all `tool_result` blocks (`{type:'tool_result', tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`) in a single user message. Splitting them across messages trains the model away from parallel calls. When streaming with client tools, set `eager_input_streaming:true` and validate each parsed input against its schema yourself, because the server stops validating.

Manual loop: `while(true){ const s = client.messages.stream({model:'claude-opus-5-5', max_tokens:16000, system, tools, messages, cache_control:{type:'ephemeral'}}, {signal}); relay s.on('text'); const m = await s.finalMessage(); if (m.stop_reason==='end_turn'||m.stop_reason==='refusal') break; if (m.stop_reason==='pause_turn'){messages.push({role:'assistant',content:m.content}); continue;} if (m.stop_reason==='max_tokens' && hasToolUse) throw; messages.push({role:'assistant', content:m.content}); const results = await Promise.all(toolUses.map(run)); messages.push({role:'user', content:results}); }`. Push the full `m.content` back, including thinking blocks. Example tools: `evaluate_strudel` {code:string, cycles:integer} with strict:true and additionalProperties:false. Clamp `cycles` server-side because strict schemas cannot express minimum or maximum. It returns `{haps:[{onset, duration, midi, s}], error?}`. `get_learner_progress` takes an empty object schema `{type:'object', properties:{}, additionalProperties:false}`. Alternative: `client.beta.messages.toolRunner({..., tools:[betaZodTool({name, description, inputSchema, run})], stream:true})` from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/beta/zod', which validates inputs against the Zod schema. It is a beta API and uses Beta* types.

findings.detail: Request parameter: `output_config: { format: { type:'json_schema', schema:{...} }, effort? }`. The SDK type is `OutputConfig { effort?, format?: JSONOutputFormat|null }`; the older `output_format` is deprecated. The helper is `zodOutputFormat(zodSchema)` from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/zod', used with `client.messages.parse({... output_config:{format: zodOutputFormat(S)}})`; the result is on `response.parsed_output`, which is null if parsing fails. The SDK moves unsupported constraints (minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength) into field descriptions and checks them after the response. For tools, `strict: true` sits on the tool itself, not on tool_choice. Schema limits: every object needs `additionalProperties:false`; no recursive schemas; no numeric or string length constraints; array `minItems` only 0 or 1; at most 20 strict tools, 24 optional parameters and 16 union-typed parameters across all strict schemas in a request. Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours, so the first use of a schema is slower and the compile timeout is 180 s. Structured outputs work with streaming, batches, token counting and thinking (the grammar does not constrain thinking). They are incompatible with citations (400) and prefill.

The endpoint is `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`, called as `client.messages.countTokens({ model, messages, system?, tools?, thinking?, ... })`, which returns `{ input_tokens }`. It takes the same inputs as messages.create (system, tools, images and PDFs as base64, server tools) and counts per model. The count is an estimate and can include system-added tokens that are not billed. Do not use tiktoken. Use it to measure the static prefix, to check it meets the 512-token cache minimum, and to keep the Haiku route under the 100K-token price tier.

Responses include `retry-after` (seconds; not on every 429, and never on a spend-cap 429), `anthropic-ratelimit-requests-{limit,remaining,reset}`, `anthropic-ratelimit-tokens-{limit,remaining,reset}` (the most restrictive limit in effect), `anthropic-ratelimit-input-tokens-{...}`, `anthropic-ratelimit-output-tokens-{...}` (reset values are RFC 3339; token counts rounded to the nearest thousand), plus `request-id` and `anthropic-workspace-id`. Limits are RPM, ITPM and OTPM per model class. Cache reads do not count toward ITPM on most models. In the SDK, read headers with `.withResponse()` → `response.headers`, or from `err.headers` on an APIError.

findings.topic: Errors and retry behaviour in the SDK
findings.detail: Error classes in 1.8.0 (core/error.d.ts): AnthropicError, APIError (status, headers, error, requestID, workspaceID, apiMessage, type, errorCode, details), APIUserAbortError, APIConnectionError, APIConnectionTimeoutError, BadRequestError(400), AuthenticationError(401), PermissionDeniedError(403), NotFoundError(404), RequestTimeoutError(408), ConflictError(409), PreconditionFailedError(412), ContentTooLargeError(413), UnprocessableEntityError(422), RateLimitError(429), RequestHeaderFieldsTooLargeError(431), ClientClosedRequestError(499), InternalServerError(>=500) with subclasses NotImplementedError, ServiceUnavailableError, GatewayTimeoutError and OverloadedError(529). `shouldRetry` checks the `x-should-retry` header first (true or false wins), then retries 408, 409, 429, >=500 and connection errors. It also retries a 401 once after refreshing a cached bearer token. The delay comes from `retry-after-ms`, otherwise `retry-after` (seconds or an HTTP date), otherwise exponential backoff from 0.5 s capped at 8 s with up to 25% jitter. Defaults are 2 retries and a 10-minute timeout. Both can be overridden per request with `{maxRetries, timeout}` in milliseconds. A timeout throws APIConnectionTimeoutError and timeouts are retried. A non-streaming request expected to take more than about 10 minutes throws unless you stream or set `timeout`. An `error` event mid-stream (such as overloaded_error) after HTTP 200 is not retried automatically.

findings.topic: Claude Agent SDK: what it is and its API
findings.detail: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.322 packages Claude Code as a library. It ships a native Claude Code binary through platform optionalDependencies (darwin-arm64 and others), and SDK 0.3.N bundles Claude Code 2.1.N. Peer dependencies: zod ^4, @anthropic-ai/sdk >=0.93.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.29.0. It requires Node 18.14+. Its license points to Anthropic's Commercial Terms. `query({prompt: string | AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>, options?: Options}): Query` returns an async iterable of SDK messages. Options include model, systemPrompt (string, or `{type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append?}`), tools, allowedTools, disallowedTools, mcpServers, permissionMode, canUseTool, maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, effort, thinking, outputFormat `{type:'json_schema', schema}`, includePartialMessages, abortController, env (replaces process.env), settingSources, persistSession, cwd, `executable: 'bun'|'deno'|'node'` and pathToClaudeCodeExecutable. Also available: `startup()` and `prewarm()` (alpha; an idle spare holds about 230–260 MB). Custom tools: `tool(name, description, zodRawShape, handler(args, extra) => Promise<CallToolResult>, extras?)` and `createSdkMcpServer({name, version?, instructions?, tools?, alwaysLoad?, timeout?})`, passed in `mcpServers`. Their names become `mcp__{server}__{tool}` and must be listed in `allowedTools` to be pre-approved; the server runs in-process. Tool search defers SDK MCP tool schemas by default. Each `query()` spawns a `claude` CLI subprocess over stdio that writes JSONL transcripts to disk, so it runs inside a Bun server process. `bun build --compile` requires `extractFromBunfs()` from '@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/extract' plus `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`.

findings.topic: Agent SDK authentication: API key vs subscription login
findings.detail: The Agent SDK quickstart says to set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from a Claude Console key. It also supports Bedrock (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1), Claude Platform on AWS (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1), Vertex (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1) and Foundry (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1). The overview and quickstart say Anthropic "does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits" in their products, including Agent SDK agents, unless previously approved, and point to API keys instead. Paraphrasing Claude Code's legal-and-compliance page: OAuth (subscription) authentication is meant for subscribers' ordinary use of Claude Code and Anthropic's native apps. Developers building products or services, including with the Agent SDK, should use Console API keys or a cloud provider. Developers may not offer Claude.ai login in their own apps, route requests through Free, Pro, Max or Ultra credentials on behalf of users, or collect or intermediate Claude.ai tokens. The same page says advertised plan limits assume ordinary individual use of Claude Code and the Agent SDK, and that an end user may sign in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription. Mechanically, the bundled CLI would accept CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (from `claude setup-token`) or a /login session, which sit below ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and apiKeyHelper in its precedence order. Whether a sole developer-user may power a personal app this way is not explicitly addressed; the documented guidance points to API keys.

findings.topic: Agent SDK vs plain Messages API for Oak
findings.detail: Oak needs a few custom tools (evaluate_strudel, progress), precise control over the cached prefix layout, structured outputs per route, low-latency streaming relayed to a React UI, and no filesystem or shell access. The Messages API covers all of these with one HTTP call per turn. The Agent SDK adds a subprocess per session with a large memory footprint, Claude Code's built-in tools and permission model (which Oak would need to disable), its own system prompt and caching behaviour (only partly controllable through the systemPrompt array and SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY), and on-disk session transcripts. It still requires an API key under Anthropic's guidance. The Agent SDK fits agents that edit files or run commands; Oak's tutor is a tool-using chat. Recommendation: Messages API with a manual loop, or the beta toolRunner.

findings.topic: Keeping the API key out of the browser
findings.detail: The authentication docs say to call the Claude API from your own back end, because anyone using a web page can read a key in its code. Direct browser calls are CORS requests that need the `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access: true` header, which the TS SDK sends only when `dangerouslyAllowBrowser:true` is set. Organizations with ZDR or the Compliance API get a 401 for any request that carries an `Origin` header. A back end should therefore create a fresh request to Claude rather than forwarding the browser's request with its Origin header. The SDK throws in browser-like environments unless dangerouslyAllowBrowser is set. Bun's frontend bundler does not inline env vars by default (`env = "disable"`). `env = "PUBLIC_*"` or `BUN_PUBLIC_*` patterns inline only prefixed vars, so never set `env: "inline"` for the SPA build.

findings.topic: Server-side refusal fallback (optional) and stop reasons
findings.detail: Stop reasons are end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn and refusal. `stop_details` (type, category, explanation) is populated only when the stop reason is refusal. For Opus 5.5 the skill suggests the server-side fallback: `client.beta.messages.create({ betas:['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01'], fallbacks:'default', ... })`. Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback. A refusal is unlikely in a music tutor, but code should check `stop_reason` before reading `content`.

risks: API version 2026-10-21 (SDK 1.x) rejects `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` with a 400, so exercise-variant variety cannot come from sampling settings. Use prompt-level variation (seed motifs, explicit constraints) and deduplicate on the server.
Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 return a 400 for a forced tool_choice (`any` or `tool`). Use auto with strict tools, or use output_config.format for JSON-only routes. Haiku 5.5 accepts a forced tool_choice.
Bun.serve's default idleTimeout of 10 s closes SSE connections while Opus is thinking silently (display defaults to 'omitted'). Call server.timeout(req, 0) and/or send `: ping` comments.

Silent cache invalidators: a timestamp, learner name or progress JSON in the top-level system prompt; tool lists that are not deterministic; switching effort, thinking or output_config.format mid-conversation; switching models (caches are per model). Each one turns every request into a full-price write with no error.

Preserved thinking: trimming or editing earlier turns, or deleting injected reminders, invalidates replayed thinking blocks and the cache. Keep history append-only and send `response.content` back verbatim.

evaluate_strudel runs JavaScript (Strudel code) that Claude writes. Running it in the Bun server process gives model-generated code access to the filesystem, network and the API key in process.env. Sandbox it (a Worker with no capabilities, an isolated VM, or evaluate in the browser and return the haps).

A strict schema cannot express numeric ranges (cycles, MIDI 0-127, bar numbers), so tool inputs and parsed outputs still need server-side validation. The first request with each new schema is slower while its grammar compiles.
Errors that arrive mid-stream (overloaded_error after HTTP 200) are not retried by the SDK. The relay must surface them and let the UI offer a retry.
Haiku 5.5 price jumps 5x (to $0.50/$2.50) once a prompt exceeds 100K tokens. If the cached prefix plus history grows past that, the cheap tier is lost.

Agent SDK: using subscription OAuth (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or /login) to power a self-built app goes against the documented developer guidance and could be enforced against without notice. Its subprocess model also adds about 230–260 MB per session and native-binary packaging problems under `bun build --compile`.
Exposure on localhost: a local server holding the key can be reached by any web page the user visits (cross-site POST or DNS rebinding) unless it checks Origin/Host and binds to 127.0.0.1.
recommendations: Use @anthropic-ai/sdk ^1.8.0 (plain Messages API) and zod ^4. Construct `new Anthropic({ maxRetries: 2 })` once at server start. Put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in `.env.local`, which Bun loads automatically, and gitignore it. Never set dangerouslyAllowBrowser. Keep Bun's frontend env inlining disabled or limited to the PUBLIC_* prefix.

Bind Bun.serve to hostname '127.0.0.1'. On every /api route, reject requests whose Origin is not the app's own origin and whose Host is not localhost. Never return the key; /api/health reports only whether a key is configured.

Endpoint 1, `POST /api/tutor/chat` (SSE): stream claude-opus-5-5 with thinking `{type:'adaptive', display:'summarized'}` (optional) and `output_config:{effort:'medium'}` set explicitly. Run a manual tool loop with `client.messages.stream(params, {signal: req.signal})` and `finalMessage()`. Emit app-level SSE events (text, thinking, tool_start, tool_result, done with usage, error) from an async-generator Response. Call `server.timeout(req, 0)` and call `stream.abort()` in the generator's finally block. Store each conversation append-only in bun:sqlite, keyed by session id.

Tutor tool list: `evaluate_strudel{code:string, cycles:integer}` → haps [{onset, duration, midi, s}] plus error, run in a sandboxed Worker with cycles clamped to 1–16. `get_learner_progress{}` → skills, mastery, recent errors, unlocked toolbox. `get_lesson_context{lesson_id:string}` → objectives, rubric, target haps reference. `compare_haps{learner_code:string, target_id:string}` → a deterministic diff of pitch, onset and duration accuracy computed in code, which Claude only explains. `record_observation{concept_id:string, kind:enum, note:string}` → writes to the learner model. Give every tool `strict:true` and `additionalProperties:false`. Sort the list by name and keep it identical on every request. Use tool_choice auto, and say in the prompt when each tool should be used.

Cache layout for the Opus tutor (render order tools → system → messages): no marker on tools; system = [persona and pedagogy block] + [syllabus vN] + [Strudel catalog vN, generated deterministically and sorted, with `cache_control:{type:'ephemeral', ttl:'1h'}`]. Add top-level `cache_control:{type:'ephemeral'}` for the growing conversation (a 1h entry before 5m entries is valid). Put volatile context such as current lesson, progress snapshot and the learner's current code in the newest user message or a mid-conversation `{role:'system'}` message, never in top-level system. Assert in a test that a second identical request has `usage.cache_read_input_tokens > 0`.

Endpoint 2, `POST /api/feedback` (JSON, high volume): `client.messages.parse({ model:'claude-haiku-5-5', max_tokens: 2048, output_config:{ effort:'low', format: zodOutputFormat(FeedbackSchema) }, system:[...static rubric and catalog with cache_control...], messages:[learner code, haps, deterministic diff] })`. FeedbackSchema is { verdict: enum, concepts:[{id, status: enum}], issues:[{bar:int, beat:number, kind: enum, message}], hint, next_step }. Send no tools. Grade pass or fail deterministically in code and let the model write the explanation.

Endpoint 3, `POST /api/exercises/variants` (JSON): `messages.parse` with claude-sonnet-5-5 (or Haiku for drills) and an ExerciseVariant schema { prompt, starter_code, solution_code, concepts[], difficulty: enum }. Before accepting each variant, run its solution through the headless Strudel evaluator and regenerate on failure (capped). For pre-generating large drill pools offline, use the Message Batches API at 50% off.

Endpoint 4, `POST /api/session/warm`: at the start of a daily session, send a non-streaming `max_tokens: 0` request with the same tools, system, thinking and effort as real traffic, so the first tutor turn reads from the cache. Endpoint 5, `POST /api/dev/count-tokens` (dev only): `client.messages.countTokens` to size the prefix and keep the Haiku route under 100K tokens.

Error handling: catch from most specific to least: RateLimitError (read err.headers['retry-after'] and show a cooldown), OverloadedError or InternalServerError, AuthenticationError (missing or invalid key → setup screen), BadRequestError (log err.errorCode, err.details and err.requestID), then APIConnectionError and APIUserAbortError (ignore user cancels). Log `_request_id` and the usage fields for each call.
Do not use the Claude Agent SDK for Oak. If it is ever used for a dev-time tool, such as authoring course content in the repo, authenticate it with an API key and not subscription OAuth.

Since the static prefix is about 30–50K tokens, keep the persona and pedagogy block first and stable, version the syllabus and catalog blocks, and regenerate them only on deploys. Every regeneration costs one cache write per model.
openQuestions: Does Anthropic allow a single developer, who is also the only user, to power a personal Agent SDK app with their own Pro, Max or Ultra subscription (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN)? The docs prohibit offering claude.ai login in third-party products and send developers to API keys, but they do not say so explicitly for personal, non-distributed use. Confirm with Anthropic sales or support if this matters.

Does Bun 1.4.4 abort `req.signal` when the client disconnects? Bun's docs only document the generator `finally` block and ReadableStream `cancel()` on disconnect. Rely on those, and treat passing req.signal as best effort.

What is the actual token size of the syllabus plus the 300-function Strudel catalog? Measure it with countTokens; it decides whether the catalog stays in the prefix or moves behind a lookup tool or tool search.

Is Haiku 5.5 at effort low good enough for music-theory feedback, such as voice-leading or chord-function explanations, or does the feedback route need Sonnet 5.5? This needs a small eval set built from real learner submissions.
Should the tutor stream summarized thinking (`display:'summarized'`) to make the waits on Opus 5.5's always-on thinking feel shorter, or show a progress indicator instead? This is a UX choice.

The new account's creation date determines whether the preserved-thinking history-editing check is enforced (the skill reference names accounts created on or after 2026-08-31). Assume it is enforced and keep history append-only.

followUps.summary:
I checked everything against the published package source on 2026-11-10: tonal@6.5.1 (released 2026-10-14, MIT), its @tonaljs/* subpackages, @strudel/tonal@1.2.6, @strudel/core@1.2.6 and abcjs@6.7.2 (released 2026-10-16, MIT). The planned pipeline (hap → NotationModel → ABC → abcjs, graded with tonal) is workable. Five facts change the design. (1) Strudel's spelling rules are mostly the same as tonal 6.5.1's. A fresh install of @strudel/tonal pulls @tonaljs/tonal@4.10.0, whose caret ranges resolve to the same @tonaljs/note@4.12.3, scale@4.13.6, key@4.11.4, roman-numeral@4.9.3 and progression@4.9.4 that tonal 6.5.1 pins exactly. Strudel only uses Note, Interval and Scale from tonal, so scale() output is spelled the same way. They differ only in Chord/ChordType (chord 4.10.2 vs 6.2.1: no slash chords, no maj11/-maj7 aliases) and Interval (4.8.2 vs 5.1.1). (2) Strudel's real spelling hazards come from its own code, not tonal. `voicing()` always produces flat-spelled names through its own midi2note, so D^7 gives Gb rather than F#. Notes can be written with 's'/'f' accidentals and default to octave 3; tonal rejects 's'/'f' and returns midi null for a note with no octave. Numeric transpose on note strings goes through Interval.fromSemitones, so a minor 2nd, a diminished 5th or a minor 6th is chosen, and spellings like Fb or Bbb can appear. Strudel's iReal chord symbols are matched against its own voicing dictionary, not tonal. (3) For answer keys: tonal accepts ^7, -7, h7, o7, +, - and bare root symbols. It rejects h9, -add9, -b6, 7susadd3 and 7b13sus, and it also rejects 'ø7' and '∆7'. abcjs displays '^7' as '∆7' (U+2206), turns 'o' into '°' and '0' into 'ø', and prints 'h7', '-7' and 'maj7' exactly as written. So display and grading each need a normalization layer. Progression.fromRomanNumerals ignores numeral case: 'ii7' in C gives 'D7'. Grade by tonic, chroma and bass, not by strings.

(4) abcjs has what Oak needs for code↔notation mapping. The click listener is `(abcElem, tuneNumber, classes, analysis, drag, mouseEvent)`. abcElem has startChar, endChar, el_type, abselem, pitches, duration and `averagepitch` (lowercase). midiPitches is filled in only after `setUpAudio()`. Since 6.7.0 you can write `!class=foo!` before a note and abcjs adds foo to that note's SVG group, but only when `add_classes` is true. That is the most robust way to link note IDs to SVG elements. TimingCallbacks runs on its own performance.now()/requestAnimationFrame clock and has no hook for an external clock. You can only re-seek it with setProgress(sec, 'seconds'), so highlighting should run from Strudel's clock and toggle CSS classes directly. Dragging returns only a step count (`drag.step`, in staff positions); Oak must rewrite the ABC itself and re-render. Tuplets are limited to single digits 2–9 and cannot be nested (open issue #1168 asks for more). Clicks on empty staff space produce no callback, because elements are only hit within 12px. abcjs ships only as a CommonJS/UMD module, about 512 KB minified with the synth included. It has no `exports` or `module` field and its types have no default export. Every DOM access I found in the bundle sits inside a function, so SSR should not crash on import (an inference from a grep).

(5) No maintained JS library takes rational-onset events and produces properly notated ties, tuplets and ABC, so a hand-written quantizer is justified. Options considered:
- @xromdev/notation: 64th-note tick grid, approximate triplets only, pre-1.0.
- musicxml-io: serializes MusicXML and ABC from an already-notated score.
- music21j: beams and MusicXML export; I found no measure or tie generation.
- webmscore: GPL, last published 2023.

VexFlow 5 is better for a click-to-place input staff because it has Stave.getLineForY. Verovio 6.4.1 has the best playback sync (renderToTimemap and getElementsAtTime) and an editing API, but it is about 7.4 MB of WASM under the LGPL. For display plus highlighting, abcjs with `!class=` IDs is sufficient.

findings.detail: Named exports: AbcNotation, Array, Chord, ChordType, Collection, Core, DurationValue, Interval, Key, Midi, Mode, Note, Pcset, Progression, Range, RhythmPattern, RomanNumeral, Scale, ScaleType, TimeSignature, VoiceLeading, Voicing, VoicingDictionary, plus `export * from @tonaljs/core`. The deprecated aliases Tonal, PcSet, ChordDictionary and ScaleDictionary are still exported. Dependencies are pinned exactly: note 4.12.3, key 4.11.4, chord 6.2.1, chord-type 5.2.1, interval 5.1.1, scale 4.13.6, mode 4.9.4, roman-numeral 4.9.3, progression 4.9.4, duration-value 4.9.1, time-signature 4.10.1, rhythm-pattern 1.0.1, abc-notation 4.9.3. ESM is dist/index.mjs and CJS is dist/index.js. Per the changelog, 6.5.1 exists because 6.5.0's tsdown build produced index.cjs instead of index.js, which broke require/import resolution in Node.

`Note.fromMidi(midi: number): string` always uses flats (61 → 'Db4') and rounds fractional input (61.7 → 'D4'). `Note.fromMidiSharps(midi): string` gives 'C#4'. Both wrap `Midi.midiToNoteName(midi, { sharps?: boolean, pitchClass?: boolean })`. Neither is key-aware, so Oak must implement key-aware spelling itself. Related helpers: `Midi.toMidi(note|number): number|null`, `Midi.freqToMidi`, `Midi.pcsetNearest(chroma)(midi)`.

`Note.get` uses the regex `/^([a-gA-G]?)(#{1,}|b{1,}|x{1,}|)(-?\d*)\s*(.*)$/`. Lowercase letters are accepted and uppercased, and 'x' means a double sharp. A note with no octave gets oct undefined, midi null and freq null. Strudel's 's'/'f' accidentals ('cs4', 'ef4') produce an empty note.
`Note.simplify(name)`:
- returns `midiToNoteName(midi||chroma, { sharps: alt > 0, pitchClass: midi === null })`
- examples: 'B#4' → 'C5', 'E#' → 'F', 'Fb' → 'E'
- only reduces odd spellings; it does not respell into a key.
`Note.enharmonic(name, destPc?)`:
- respells to the target pitch class and adjusts the octave ('F2','E#' → 'E#2')
- returns '' if the chroma differs.
Other signatures: `Note.transpose(note, interval)`, `Note.transposeFifths(note, n)`, `Note.distance(a, b)`, `Note.chroma`, `Note.pitchClass`, `Note.accidentals`, `Note.octave`, `Note.midi`.

`Key.majorKey(tonic): MajorKey` returns:
- type 'major', tonic, alteration (fifths from C), keySignature (e.g. '###' or 'bb'), minorRelative
- grades ['I'..'VII'], always uppercase
- intervals, scale (e.g. F# major → [...,'E#'])
- triads ['C','Dm','Em','F','G','Am','Bdim']
- chords ['Cmaj7','Dm7','Em7','Fmaj7','G7','Am7','Bm7b5']
- chordsHarmonicFunction ['T','SD','T','SD','D','T','D']
- chordScales ['C major','D dorian',...]
- secondaryDominants, secondaryDominantSupertonics, substituteDominants, substituteDominantSupertonics, plus their *MinorRelative variants.
`Key.minorKey(tonic): MinorKey` returns type, tonic, relativeMajor, alteration, keySignature, and natural/harmonic/melodic KeyScale objects. Harmonic chords are mMaj7, m7b5, +maj7, m7, 7, maj7, o7.
Also available: `Key.majorKeyChords(tonic)` and `Key.minorKeyChords(tonic)`, which return {name, roles[]} with roles like 'V/II' and 'subV/...', and `Key.majorTonicFromKeySignature('###' | 3)`.

Functions:
- `Interval.distance(from, to)`: 'C4','G4' → '5P'
- `Interval.semitones(name): number`
- `Interval.quality(name)`: one of 'dddd'..'AAAA', 'm', 'M', 'P'
- `Interval.num`, `Interval.get(name)`: {name, num, q, alt, dir, semitones, simple, type, ...}
- `Interval.simplify`, `Interval.invert`, `Interval.add`, `Interval.subtract`, `Interval.fromSemitones(n)`
Names are in shorthand 'num+quality' form ('3m'). 'm3' is also parsed. fromSemitones uses the fixed table IN=[1,2,2,3,3,4,5,5,6,6,7,7] with IQ='P m M m M P d P m M m M', so a tritone is '5d' and 8 semitones is '6m'. The table is identical in interval@4.8.2, the version Strudel resolves. Since 6.5.0, malformed names such as 'ddd5' are rejected.

`Chord.get(name | [tonic, type, bass?]): Chord`. A Chord has tonic, type (full name), root, bass, rootDegree, symbol, notes (pitch classes) and intervals, and inherits aliases, chroma and setNum from ChordType.
`Chord.getChord(type, tonic?, bass?)`. `Chord.tokenize`:
- splits as letter+acc | oct+type | '/'+bass, so 'C-7' becomes ['C','-7',''] and 'C-' becomes minor
- a bare root 'C' maps through the '' alias to major.
`symbol` keeps the alias as given: Chord.get('C^7').symbol === 'C^7'.
`Chord.detect(notes[], {assumePerfectFifth?})`:
- returns symbols using aliases[0], e.g. ['Cmaj7'], 'Cm7b5', 'Cdim7'
- treats the first input note as the bass, so inversions come back as 'Cmaj7/E' at half weight.
Other functions: `Chord.notes(name, tonic?)` (with octave), `Chord.chordScales`, `Chord.extended`, `Chord.reduced`, `Chord.transpose`, `Chord.degrees`, `Chord.steps`.

findings.topic: Chord aliases: tonal vs iReal/Strudel vs abcjs display
findings.detail:
tonal chord-type 5.2.1 aliases include:
- major: 'M', '^', '', 'maj'
- major seventh: 'maj7', 'Δ' (U+0394), 'ma7', 'M7', 'Maj7', '^7'
- minor: 'm', 'min', '-'; minor seventh: 'm7', 'min7', 'mi7', '-7'
- minor/major seventh: '-^7', '-maj7'
- half-diminished: 'm7b5', 'ø', '-7b5', 'h7', 'h'
- diminished: 'dim', '°', 'o'; diminished seventh: 'dim7', '°7', 'o7'
- augmented: 'aug', '+', '+5', '^#5'
- also '7sus', '9sus', '13sus', '7b9sus', '7alt' (= 1P 3M 5A 7m 9A), '-6', '-69', '-#5', '^7#11', '^9#11'.
Strudel iReal keys missing from tonal: 'h9', '-add9', '-b6', '7susadd3', '7b13sus'. Also missing: 'ø7' (only 'ø' exists) and 'Δ7'/'∆7' (only 'Δ' and '^7').
Strudel voicing() also accepts 'm…', 'M…' and 'aug…' aliases, which are derived from '-', '^' and '+'. It does not accept 'maj7' or 'dim'. Its chord tokenizer requires an uppercase root: /^([A-G][b#]*)([^/]*)[/]?([A-G][b#]*)?$/.

`RomanNumeral.get(src: string|number|Pitch)` returns {name, roman, interval, acc, chordType, alt, step, major, oct, dir}, parsed with `/^(#{1,}|b{1,}|x{1,}|)(IV|I{1,3}|VI{0,2}|iv|i{1,3}|vi{0,2})([^IViv]*)$/`. `major` is just roman === uppercase. `RomanNumeral.names(major=true)`.
`Progression.fromRomanNumerals(tonic, ['I','IIm7','V7'])` gives ['C','Dm7','G7']. It appends chordType to the transposed root and ignores case, so 'ii7' becomes 'D7'.
`Progression.toRomanNumerals('C', ['CMaj7','Dm7','G7'])` gives ['IMaj7','IIm7','V7']. Output is always uppercase with the chord type copied verbatim: 'D-7' becomes 'II-7' and 'Eb' becomes 'bIII'.

`Mode.get(name)` returns {name, modeNum, alt, triad, seventh, aliases, intervals, chroma, setNum,...}. Mode table: ionian (alias 'major', seventh 'Maj7'), dorian ('m7'), phrygian, lydian ('Maj7'), mixolydian ('7'), aeolian (alias 'minor'), locrian ('m7b5'). Other mode functions: `Mode.names()`, `Mode.all()`, `Mode.notes(mode, tonic)`, `Mode.triads(mode, tonic)`, `Mode.seventhChords(mode, tonic)`, `Mode.relativeTonic(dest, src, tonic)`, `Mode.distance`.
`Scale.get('D dorian')` returns {tonic, type, notes, intervals, aliases, chroma,...} and is case-insensitive since 6.0.1. Useful scale names: 'major'/'ionian', 'minor'/'aeolian', 'major pentatonic'/'pentatonic', 'minor pentatonic', 'minor blues'/'blues', 'major blues', 'harmonic minor', 'melodic minor', 'mixolydian'/'dominant', 'altered'/'super locrian', 'half-whole diminished', 'whole tone', 'bebop'.
Other scale functions: `Scale.detect(notes, {tonic?, match?: 'exact'|'fit'})`, `Scale.degrees(name)(n)`, `Scale.steps`, `Scale.modeNames`, `Scale.scaleChords`, `Scale.rangeOf`.
Key and Mode use different spellings, 'maj7' vs 'Maj7'.

`DurationValue.get('q.')` returns {value: 0.375, fraction: [3,8], shorthand, dots, names}. Shorthands are dl, l, d, w, h, q, e, s, t, sf, ...; names include 'quarter' and 'crotchet'. There is no tuplet support and no reverse lookup from value to name.
`TimeSignature.get('6/8'|[6,8])` returns {upper, lower, type: 'simple'|'compound'|'irregular'|'irrational', additive[]}. 'C' and 'C|' are accepted since 6.5.0. `TimeSignature.parse` is also available.
`RhythmPattern` offers euclid, binary, hex, onsets, random, probability and rotate.
`AbcNotation.scientificToAbcNotation('C#4')` gives '^C'. `AbcNotation.abcToScientificNotation('c')` gives 'C5'. `AbcNotation.transpose` and `AbcNotation.distance` also exist. These cover ABC pitch tokens, but not key-signature-relative accidentals.

findings.topic: Strudel's own spelling behaviour (sources of disagreement with answer keys)
findings.detail:
Strudel spells notes in these ways:
- scale(): `Note.transpose(pc+oct, Interval.add(interval, octaves))`, default octave 3. Key-correct spellings, so F#:major yields E#.
- transpose(n) on a note string: `Note.transpose(note, Interval.fromSemitones(n))`, which can give Fb, Cb or Bbb. On a MIDI number it adds semitones.
- chord().voicing(): renderVoicing → midi2note(n) with the flats table, so names are always flat (C, Db, D, Eb, E, F, Gb, ...) regardless of key or chord. For example F# in D^7 comes out as Gb.
- core noteToMidi: regex /^([a-gA-G])([#bsf]*)(-?[0-9]*)$/ where s means sharp, f means flat, default octave 3.
The NotationModel therefore has to re-spell every pitch from MIDI plus key or chord context. Do not trust value.note strings.

`Hap.duration` returns value.duration if that is set, otherwise whole.end − whole.begin, multiplied by value.clip when present. So legato/clip changes the sounding length. Use `whole.begin` and `whole.end` for notation and filter `hap.whole && hap.hasOnset()`. @strudel/core@1.2.6 depends on fraction.js ^5.2.1.

findings.topic: abcjs 6.7.2 clickListener signature and abcElem fields
findings.detail:
Type: `ClickListener = (abcElem: AbcElem, tuneNumber: number, classes: string, analysis: ClickListenerAnalysis, drag: ClickListenerDrag) => void`. The runtime passes a 6th argument, `mouseEvent`.
AbcElem fields:
- `el_type`, `abselem?: AbsoluteElement` (with elemset: SVGElement[], notePositions, x, w, ...)
- `startChar?`, `endChar?` (offsets into the ABC string)
- `averagepitch?` (lowercase p; diatonic, middle C = 0), `minpitch`, `maxpitch`
- `pitches?: {pitch (C4 = 0, diatonic), name, accidental?, verticalPos, startTie?, endTie?, startSlur?}[]`
- `duration`, `rest?`, `chord?`, `startTriplet`, `tripletMultiplier`, `tripletR`
- `currentTrackMilliseconds?`, `midiPitches?: {pitch, duration, start, volume, instrument, gap, cents?}[]`.
midiPitches is filled only by the synth flattener, i.e. after `visualObj.setUpAudio()` or creating a synth. setTiming does not set it.
analysis is {voice, line, measure, staffPos, name, clickedName, parentClasses, clickedClasses, selectableElement}, parsed from the abcjs-v, abcjs-l and abcjs-m classes. The docs describe staffPos as {top, height, zero}, where zero is middle C's y; the .d.ts types it as number.

With add_classes:true, Classes.generate adds:

findings.topic: Highlighting from an external clock; TimingCallbacks
findings.detail:
`new TimingCallbacks(visualObj, {qpm, extraMeasuresAtBeginning, beatSubdivisions, beatCallback, eventCallback, lineEndCallback, lineEndAnticipation})`. Methods: start(pos?, units?), pause(), reset(), stop(), setProgress(pos, 'seconds'|'beats'|'percent'), currentMillisecond(), replaceTarget(), plus a `noteTimings` property.
It runs its own clock: doTiming(timestamp) uses requestAnimationFrame plus a setTimeout jogger with performance.now(), and startTime is derived internally. There is no way to inject a time source, so the only option is to keep calling setProgress(sec, 'seconds') to resync.
For an external clock, call `visualObj.setTiming(bpm)` (works only after render). It returns NoteTimingEvent[] with {milliseconds, type, elements: SVGElement[][], startChar/startCharArray, endCharArray, measureNumber, line, left, top, width, height, midiPitches}. You can also skip abcjs timing entirely and toggle your own CSS classes on elements found through the `!class=` IDs.

findings.detail:
Enable with `{dragging: true, selectTypes: ['note'] | true, selectionColor (default '#ff0000'), dragColor, clickListener}`. While dragging, the SVG is only translated in steps of spacing.STEP = 30*93/720 = 3.875px per diatonic step at scale 1. On mouseup the listener gets `drag = {step, max, index, setSelection(i)}`, where step is the number of visual positions moved (positive means higher). The ABC is not modified. Per the docs, Oak must edit the ABC string itself, using abcElem.startChar/endChar to replace the pitch token, and call renderAbc again.
Clicks only hit selectables within 12px (findElementByCoord). Clicking empty staff space gives no callback, so click-to-place on an empty staff needs Oak's own pointer handler. That handler can derive pitch from the .abcjs-staff and .abcjs-top-line geometry and STEP.

Tuplets: '(p', '(p:q', '(p::r' and '(p:q:r', with p, q and r each a single digit (p 2–9). Default q values come from the tripletQ table (2→3, 3→2, 4→3, 5 depends on the meter). Nesting warns 'Can't nest triplets'.
Keys: K: modes are matched case-insensitively on the first three letters: mix, dor, phr, lyd, loc, aeo→m, maj/ion→'', min/m→m. So 'K:D dor' and 'K:A mix' both work. Clefs: treble, bass, alto, tenor and ±8 variants.
Voices: %%score and %%staves are supported with ( ) [ ] { } and |. '{' marks staves joined by a brace, so `%%score {RH LH}` gives a grand staff and `%%score {RH | LH}` also connects the barlines. Multi-voice uses 'V:id clef=bass'.
Chord symbols, unless %%freegchord is set:
- 'b'/'#' after a letter or digit → ♭/♯
- root+'o' → °, root+'0' → ø, root+'^' followed by a non-letter → '∆' (so 'C^7' shows as 'C∆7', while 'C^' stays 'C^')
- 'h7', '-7', 'maj7' and '+' are shown literally.
The jazzchords option (or %%jazzchords) inserts a \x03 marker so the chord quality renders at 0.7em raised by 0.3em and the bass is offset. It does not translate symbols.
Other supported directives include %%barnumbers, %%voicecolor, %%flatbeams and %%staffnonote. There is no %%propagate-accidentals.

findings.detail:

findings.topic: VexFlow 5.0.0 vs Verovio 6.4.1 vs abcjs for input staff and sync highlight
findings.detail:
VexFlow 5.0.0:
- MIT, last publish 2025-03-05, ESM exports '.', './core', './bravura'.
- Stave has getYForLine(line), getLineForY(y), getYForNote(line) and getNoteStartX(), so mapping a pointer y to a staff line or space for a ghost-note click-to-place UI is direct.
- Oak creates every StaveNote itself, so mapping IDs to SVG for highlighting is easy.
- No automatic layout or line breaking.
Verovio 6.4.1:
- LGPL-3.0, published 2026-11-03; dist/verovio-toolkit-wasm.js is about 7.4 MB. Exports '.', './esm', './wasm', './wasm-hum'.
- Reads ABC (inputFrom 'abc'), MEI and MusicXML.
- Sync API: renderToTimemap(), getElementsAtTime(ms) → {notes: string[], page}, getTimeForElement(id).
- Editor API: edit({action: 'insertNote' | 'insertCursorByPitch' | 'drag' | 'delete' | ...}).
Verdict:
- (a) For a transcription input staff, VexFlow is meaningfully better than abcjs, which only snaps to existing elements within 12px. Verovio's editor is more complete but large.
- (b) For playback highlighting, Verovio's timemap is the most turnkey, but abcjs with `!class=` IDs driven by Strudel's clock is enough, so switching is not justified for display.

risks: Strudel's voicing() always produces flat names (midi2note with the flats table), and numeric transpose can produce Fb, Cb or Bbb. If notation or grading uses value.note strings directly, learners will see 'wrong' spellings (Gb in D major). Re-spell every pitch from MIDI plus key or chord context.

tonal rejects Strudel's 's'/'f' accidentals ('cs4', 'ef4') and returns midi null for a note with no octave, while Strudel defaults to octave 3. Without normalization, grading silently fails on empty Note objects.

Chord symbols do not round-trip between the three systems. abcjs displays '^7' as '∆' (U+2206), but tonal only knows 'Δ' (U+0394) and '^7'. abcjs shows 'ø' for '0', but tonal has no 'ø7'. Strudel's 'h9', '-add9', '-b6', '7susadd3' and '7b13sus' are unknown to tonal. A learner typing what they see on screen can be marked wrong.
Progression.fromRomanNumerals ignores numeral case ('ii7' becomes D7), and toRomanNumerals always outputs uppercase. String comparison of Roman numeral answers will disagree with standard pedagogy.

abcjs tuplets are limited to single digits 2–9 and cannot be nested (issues #1168, #1007). Strudel nesting like 'c d [e f g]', or 11+ subdivisions, needs flattening to one (p:q:r ratio or a quantization fallback, or the notation will be wrong or warn.

abcjs does not beam by meter, split notes at barlines or add ties automatically. The NotationModel must emit beam-group spacing, tied pieces and ABC bar-scoped accidentals (including =naturals) correctly, or the rendering will be wrong.

abcjs startChar/endChar are offsets into the generated ABC string. They change on every regeneration, so prefer stable `!class=oak-e{id}!` IDs, which need add_classes:true and abcjs ≥ 6.7.0. abcElem's shape is documented as 'subject to change', so pin abcjs exactly.
TimingCallbacks keeps its own performance.now() clock and will drift from Strudel's scheduler. Don't use it for sync; drive highlights from Strudel time.
abcjs is CommonJS-only (about 512 KB minified, synth included) with no tree-shaking. Load it lazily.

Open abcjs bugs affect grand staff and wrap (clef changes #1041/#1042, wrap #1070/#1098/#1125, invisible-rest voices #1192). Keep lesson scores simple: fixed staffwidth, explicit line breaks, a single clef per staff.

tonal 6.5.0 had a broken dist (index.cjs vs index.js). Pin tonal to 6.5.1 exactly, and expect duplicate @tonaljs/* copies alongside Strudel's 4.x tree (chord, chord-type, interval and core differ in version).

Reuse candidates are immature or a poor fit: @xromdev/notation is pre-1.0, a month old and built on a 64th-tick grid; musicxml-io's API is declared unstable. Depending on them would bring fit problems with Strudel's rational rhythms.
recommendations: Pipeline step 1, extract. Run `pat.queryArc(0, loopCycles)` and keep haps where `hap.whole && hap.hasOnset()`. Take onset and duration from whole.begin/whole.end as exact rationals, keeping the fraction.js n/d BigInts; ignore clip/legato. Pitch: if the value is a number it is MIDI; if a string, normalize s→#, f→b, uppercase the letter, add octave 3 when missing, then MIDI = Note.midi(...). Keep `{hapKey, locations: hap.context.locations, s/orbit}` for each event.

Pipeline step 2, voices and bars. Assign voices by source (stack layer, `s`, or lesson config). For a piano grand staff, split by register (MIDI < 60 goes to LH) or by layer. Bar index = floor(begin), since 1 cycle = 1 bar. Split events at integer cycle boundaries into tie chains.

Pipeline step 3, rhythm. Within each bar, group by beat using TimeSignature.get(meter).type: simple meters use the beat or half-bar, compound meters use dotted-quarter groups. Take the LCD of onset and offset denominators per group. If the beat-relative denominator has an odd factor k > 1, make a tuplet with p = k, q = the nearest lower power of two (2 for 3, 4 for 5–7, 8 for 9), and r = the note count, emitted explicitly as `(p:q:r`. Turn nested tuplets into a single combined ratio when p ≤ 9 (e.g. a triplet inside a triplet becomes (9:8:3). Otherwise fall back to the nearest 1/12 or 1/16 grid and set an `approximate` flag the UI can show.

Pipeline step 4, durations. Break each written duration into notatable values (whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth, 32nd, with single and double dots), splitting at beat or half-bar boundaries (e.g. no quarter note straddling the middle of a 4/4 bar) and tying the pieces. Fill gaps with rests. Merge events that share onset and duration into chords [..]; put events with differing durations into extra V: voices.

Pipeline step 5, spelling. Take key context from the lesson (tonic + mode → Key.majorKey/minorKey, or Mode.notes(mode, tonic) for modal lessons). For each MIDI note: (a) if its chroma matches a key scale degree, use that scale spelling; (b) otherwise, if a chord symbol is active, use the spelling from Chord.get(sym).notes; (c) otherwise use sharps when going up or when key alteration > 0, and flats when going down or when alteration < 0 (Note.fromMidiSharps / Note.fromMidi). Then apply Note.enharmonic(name, targetPc) to fix octaves (B#3 vs C4, Cb4 vs B3) and Note.simplify to remove double accidentals.

Pipeline step 6, ABC emission. Write the header 'X:1', 'M:4/4', 'L:1/16', 'Q:1/4=bpm', 'K:<tonic> <mode abbrev: dor|phr|lyd|mix|loc|m>' (plus '%%score {RH LH}' and 'V:RH clef=treble' / 'V:LH clef=bass' for piano). Emit each note as `!class=oak-e{id}!` + accidental (computed against the key signature and earlier accidentals in the same bar and octave, including '=') + pitch letter with octave marks (AbcNotation.scientificToAbcNotation gives the base token) + length + '-' for ties. Insert spaces at beam-group boundaries. Translate chord symbols for display ('^7'→'maj7' or '∆7', 'h7'→'ø7' via '07', '-'→'m', 'o'→'°'). Record id→{startChar, endChar, hapKeys, codeLocations} while emitting.

Rendering. Lazy-load with `const abcjs = await import('abcjs')` and call `abcjs.renderAbc(el, abc, { add_classes: true, responsive: 'resize', foregroundColor: 'currentColor', jazzchords: true, clickListener, selectTypes: ['note'] })`. For dark mode, rely on currentColor and style .abcjs-staff and .abcjs-chord with CSS. Call `visualObj.setUpAudio()` only if you need abcElem.midiPitches.

Highlight mapping strategy. Run one requestAnimationFrame loop that reads Strudel's cycle position (I did not verify this scheduler API in this task). Find active NotationModel note IDs with an interval lookup on [begin, end) modulo the loop length, then toggle a class with `svg.querySelectorAll('.oak-e'+id)`. Do not use TimingCallbacks. For the reverse direction, clicking a note: abcElem.extraClass or classes → id → hap.context.locations → select or flash the code range in CodeMirror. Clicking code: cursor offset → events whose locations contain it → add a class to their notes.

Transcription input. For v1, build Oak's own pointer layer over the abcjs SVG. Get staff line y-positions from the '.abcjs-staff' and '.abcjs-top-line' boxes, convert y to a diatonic step with STEP = 3.875px × scale, snap x to a beat grid computed from the NotationModel, show a ghost note, and on commit regenerate ABC from the model, never by editing ABC text. If the input staff grows complex (multi-voice, chords), switch that one widget to VexFlow 5 (Stave.getLineForY) and keep abcjs for display.

Grading with tonal (pin tonal@6.5.1). First normalize symbols: ∆/Δ→'^', ø→'h', °→'o', '−'→'-', ♭→'b', ♯→'#', 's'/'f'→'#'/'b'. Then use:
- Pitches: Note.get(x).midi or .chroma for sound-equality grading; Note.get(x).name or .pc for spelling-sensitive grading.
- Intervals: Interval.distance(a, b) plus Interval.get(...).num and .q, or Interval.semitones.
- Chords: Chord.get(sym) and compare {tonic chroma, chroma string (pitch-class set), bass} rather than .symbol; Chord.detect(notesBassFirst) for 'name this chord'.
- Keys: Key.majorKey(t).chords / .triads / .chordsHarmonicFunction and Key.minorKey(t).harmonic.chords for diatonic answer keys.
- Roman numerals: RomanNumeral.get(rn) for the degree (.step, .alt). Check quality yourself through Chord.get(Progression.fromRomanNumerals(tonic, [rn])[0]). Never trust numeral case.
- Modes and scales: Scale.get / Mode.get for scale and mode questions.
- Meters: TimeSignature.get for meter classification.

Ship a golden test corpus that runs Strudel patterns through queryArc, the NotationModel and ABC. Cover: 'c d e', 'c [d e f]', 'c@3 d', '<c d>', 'c ~ d', ties across bars, quintuplets, nested triplets, voicing() chords in sharp keys, and F#:major scales. Snapshot both the ABC and the spelled pitches, and run with bun test so upgrades of abcjs, tonal or Strudel cannot silently change notation.

Pin abcjs to 6.7.2 exactly: `!class=` needs ≥ 6.7.0 and abcElem's shape is unstable. Add ambient typings that extend AbcElem with `extraClass?: string` and the 6th `mouseEvent` argument of the click listener.
openQuestions: What should notation do with rhythms that cannot be expressed in abcjs, such as `.fast(1.1)`, `nudge`, swing, polymeters like '{c d e}%4' that cross bars, or tuplets with p > 9? Show an 'approximate' flag, refuse to notate, or quantize to a grid chosen per lesson?
Should the notated length follow whole spans or clip/legato-adjusted durations? (This matters for staccato and legato lessons.)

Where does key context come from: always declared by the lesson, inferred (Scale.detect over the bar's pitch classes), or taken from `.scale()` calls (hap.context.scale holds the scale name after scale())?
Which Strudel scheduler/clock API should drive highlighting in @strudel/core@1.2.6 (e.g. repl onDraw/onTrigger or scheduler.now())? I did not verify it in this task.
For grand-staff piano parts: split hands by register at middle C, by stack layer, or by explicit lesson metadata? Cross-staff beaming is not possible in abcjs.
Is it acceptable to add VexFlow 5 (MIT) just for the transcription input widget, or must abcjs be the only engraver for visual consistency?
Is Oak's own install guaranteed to resolve @tonaljs/tonal 4.10.0's caret ranges to today's latest 4.x versions (note 4.12.3 etc.)? With Bun this should be enforced and checked through the lockfile.
